name: Study process & alt-tech
desc: How interconnection studies, queues, and readiness rules should work, and where grid-enhancing or alternative transmission technologies fit.

letters.desc: AEMA supports standardized interconnection studies that treat verifiable load reductions as system-impact mitigation and provide transparency on specific constraints, curtailment frequency, and amounts. The filing also supports queue opt-in for existing applicants and ISO pilots to accelerate learning.
quotes: AEMA urges the Commission to create a Flexible Load Fast Track (FLFT) for facilities that can verifiably adjust their consumption in response to system conditions and harness a broad set of technologies to deliver flexibility to the grid.

The FLFT would be an expedited (60-90 day) interconnection process for loads that commit to flexibility and would incorporate this flexibility into studies that determine whether transmission grid upgrades are necessary to interconnect the load.

Current state-by-state processes are inconsistent, opaque, and time-consuming, resulting in multi-year delays that slow economic growth amid an AI revolution that presents a critical opportunity for U.S. innovation, competitiveness, and prosperity.

The Commission should direct transmission providers to treat this verifiable reduction as equivalent to a system-impact mitigation, allowing such projects to be studied and interconnected on a shorter timeline.

To comply with Principle 7 of the ANOPR and for large loads to decide whether they can be curtailable, transmission owners and RTOs must provide transparency during the study process regarding the specific constraints that a large load would create and the frequency and amount of curtailment that would be necessary.
AEMA supports a clear transition plan (Principle 13) that allows projects already in the queue to opt in to the FLFT if they meet its flexibility and readiness criteria.

letters.desc: AEMA recommends that interconnection studies model a facility's actual, controlled withdrawal profile rather than theoretical maximum demand. Studies should specify clear upper-bound flexibility parameters (hours per year, depth, events) so that operators and customers both understand the commitment required.
quotes: AEMA urges the Commission to adopt an expressly 'all-of-the-above' approach in which any particular technology (whether storage, thermal resources, on-site generation, or software-defined controls) or combination thereof is encouraged so long as it can verifiably deliver the flexibility attributes that support reliability.

AEMA recommends that the interconnection study process be used to define clear, upper-bound limits on the required flexibility (e.g., maximum number of hours per year, hours per event, depth of flexibility, and events per year) needed to mitigate specific system constraints.
interconnection studies must reflect the actual, controlled operating profile of a facility rather than a theoretical maximum withdrawal.

letters.desc: Advanced Energy United supports standardized, transparent study processes for large load interconnection, including concurrent load-and-supply studies with clear eligibility rules, SSR/RMR screening for partial suspension, and load forecasting discipline tied to queue milestones.
quotes: However, a loosely defined load/supply resource interconnection pathway that provides an expedited pathway for generation interconnection without appropriate safeguards would result in undue discrimination and unjust and unreasonable rates.

This means (1) this expedited pathway should not confer the same interconnection service as is available to interconnection customers serving native load, and (2) this pathway should be available only to generation or storage resources that are not similarly situated to other interconnection customers in that they meet eligibility parameters that meaningfully, transparently, and objectively differentiate projects that proceed via expedited pathways from projects in the general queue.

United agrees that such facilities should go through an SSR/RMR type study, and that such studies should include evaluation of potential resource adequacy concerns. United also emphasizes that the Commission can take this action regardless of whether it asserts jurisdiction over the interconnection of new large loads directly to the transmission system.

letters.desc: A4CRE describes CRE as providing a path for large-load demand without requiring complex interconnection studies. This relieves pressure on transmission planning by diverting loads that would otherwise require significant system upgrades.
quotes: CRE provides a parallel, voluntary path for meeting large-load demand—particularly data centers and industrial facilities—without burdening existing systems or requiring complex interconnection studies.

CRE utilities relieve the bulk power system of the obligation to plan for and serve very large loads. By allowing those loads to internalize their own costs and risks, CRE reduces upward pressure on transmission expansion, generation additions, and interconnection queues.

letters.desc: AES urges FERC to develop a thorough evidentiary record, incorporating existing stakeholder and RTO processes and technical conference testimony, before finalizing rules, so that any standards reflect actual regional and operational complexity.
quotes: AES respectfully recommends that the Commission develop a robust record and consider existing stakeholder and state initiatives before seeking to standardize large load interconnection.

AES believes that the system operator should be required to study that generation as a retirement if it is going to be effectively taken behind-the-meter in a manner that removes the energy and capacity benefits from the market.

letters.desc: The Alliance asks the Commission to require transmission providers to analyze reliability and service quality impacts on Tribal communities as part of their transmission service planning for large loads, treating this as a mandatory component of the interconnection study process.
quotes: The Alliance urges the Commission to require transmission providers to include an analysis of potential reliability, resilience, and service quality impacts on Tribal communities as part of their transmission service planning for large loads.

letters.desc: Alliant Energy supports study reforms that reduce queue backlogs, including deposits and readiness requirements, but insists study processes must be flexible across regions and grandfathered for projects already underway. It argues that poorly designed uniform rules would create delays rather than reduce them.
quotes: Such a low threshold would unnecessarily draw numerous smaller, less impactful projects into the interconnection process, creating backlogs, congestion, and delays that undermine the very objectives of the ANOPR.
it is critical for the Commission to recognize that simply assuming generation and load offset each other is insufficient and could jeopardize reliability, affordability, and customer interests.
Expedited interconnection processes like ERAS—not netting—are the right solution to integrate large loads efficiently and maintain a robust, reliable grid.

a one-size-fits-all approach would be counterproductive.  Large load interconnection processes vary across transmission providers, and imposing uniform requirements risks disrupting effective practices already in place.

large loads that have begun the formal interconnection process with the relevant transmission owner or provider by the rule's effective date should continue without having to backtrack to meet new requirements.

letters.desc: Amazon Energy supports standardized study procedures, milestones, and readiness requirements for large loads, particularly within a common ISO or RTO. It argues standardization improves processing efficiency, transmission planning, and load-forecasting accuracy.
quotes: Amazon Energy supports the proposal in the ANOPR that, "like generating facilities, load and hybrid facilities should be subject to standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties,"

Amazon Energy urges the Commission to consider imposing similar standardization and requirements here to ensure the timely and efficient processing of large load interconnection requests, particularly for interconnections within the same ISO/RTO.

standardizing milestones and requirements for large load interconnections within a common ISO/RTO will lead to better transmission planning outcomes, and in turn, result in improved accuracy in load forecasting.

letters.desc: Expedited interconnection and fast-track pathways avoid prolonged interconnection studies and associated delays by allowing existing generators contracting with large loads to bypass lengthy review processes.
quotes: New large load customers that enter into bilateral contracts with existing generators to generate more power either by increasing their capacity factor or adding new generation at an existing site should be eligible for fast-track interconnection treatment.

An expedited interconnection path also would incentivize bilateral contracting between underutilized generating capacity and large loads. Such contracting would make efficient use of existing infrastructure, minimize if not eliminate the factors that have prompted premature retirement, and avoid unnecessary and costly transmission expansion.

Allowing an existing generator to re-secure those rights will avoid the quagmire of the interconnection study process and its associated delays and thus achieve the ANOPR's goal of timely and orderly interconnection of large loads to the transmission system.

letters.desc: ACC supports clearer, more consistent rules for studying and processing large-load interconnection requests. Current regional variation creates uncertainty around project timelines and upgrade responsibilities, which the rulemaking should address.
quotes: Chemical manufacturing relies on highly reliable and competitively priced electricity, and many future facilities will require transmission-level interconnection in order to expand or modernize operations to meet the increasing demands driven by AI, Data Center, and domestic manufacturing.
Current practices for connecting large loads to the transmission system vary across regions and often create uncertainty for project timelines and upgrade responsibilities.
Ensuring reliable electricity access for these facilities is essential to maintaining U.S. competitiveness in advanced technologies.

letters.desc: ACORE urges FERC to go beyond interconnection and integrate large load and generation interconnection needs into long-term transmission planning, working with DOE and the national labs on common load-forecasting methods.
quotes: we urge the Commission to avoid focusing solely on interconnection and instead take steps to expand and modernize the transmission system to achieve the greatest cost savings and reliability benefits.

the Commission to work with DOE and the National Laboratories to establish best practices and common methodologies for the forecasting of large loads and their power needs that can be incorporated into the long-term transmission planning process.
An essential component of improving the interconnection of large loads will be to fully integrate interconnection-driven needs into longer-term transmission planning.

letters.desc: AEP argues that interconnecting large loads requires simultaneous reforms to the generation interconnection process. It supports a connect-and-manage approach that allows generators to energize subject to curtailment before network upgrades are complete, and proactive scenario-based transmission planning that studies load and generation together rather than in silos.
quotes: an approach which focuses solely on interconnecting large loads to the electric grid will not fully support rapid data center and industrial load growth.
The Commission must also make the necessary changes to ensure that the generation needed to serve that load is able to come online in a timely and efficient fashion.

AEP supports the application of a 'connect and manage' approach (in tandem with other reforms, such as the entry fee model for generator interconnection described below) as a practical solution for the timely interconnection of generation.
Under this approach, all generators pay an entry fee and can rapidly connect to the grid subject to curtailment until supporting network transmission is planned and constructed.

The Commission should decisively address the current generation interconnection models which are hindering sufficient generation from coming online quickly enough to meet today's generation resource adequacy and reliability needs.

AEP supports the widespread adoption of an entry fee model for generator interconnections, which integrates generator interconnection and transmission planning into a single streamlined process, reducing duplicative studies and expediting transmission upgrade identification.

the prevalent siloed approach to transmission planning—in which there are separate, reactive planning processes for generation interconnection and grid expansion—will not deliver infrastructure fast enough to ensure the United States continues to be a leader in artificial intelligence and is able to grow its manufacturing base.

Consistent with the ANOPR's third Principle for Reform—which encourages studying the interconnection of load and generation together—such proactive planning will necessarily integrate the consideration of both.

letters.desc: AEP argues that piecemeal, reactive interconnection studies are insufficient to handle large load growth and that the Commission must drive proactive, multi-value, long-term transmission planning. Short-term flexible tools are useful but cannot substitute for forward-looking network expansion.
quotes: Without much needed reforms, the current approaches threaten to produce insufficient and inefficient infrastructure to reliably support large load growth and economic development.
Short-term, flexible approaches can facilitate speed-to-power, but they cannot ensure a transmission system that can support the projected large load growth.

While short-term speed-to-power solutions are important, the Commission cannot overlook the need to foster proactive transmission planning, which is necessary to ensure cost-effective and affordable transmission system expansion and timely interconnection of new generation resources.

Proactive, multi-value planning is also crucial to foster the development of Extra High Voltage ('EHV') facilities—the essential backbone of the nation's transmission system—because it looks ahead to identify regional and interregional needs and the corresponding EHV solutions.
The Commission should support regional efforts to move towards consolidated, integrated planning, like SPP's CPP.

letters.desc: ANOPR's standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties are consistent with fair cost allocation. These commitments must be well-tailored to large load and hybrid interconnection risks.
quotes: The ANOPR's proposal to impose standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties appears to be consistent with the objective of fairly allocating costs.

But such commitments must be well-tailored to the specific risks posed by large loads and hybrid interconnections, and they must account for regional variations and variations in interconnection configurations.

letters.desc: ATC opposes co-study of hybrid facilities as a default, citing functional differences between generation and load and reliability risks from misalignment at shared interconnection points. If co-study occurs, it requires safeguards and system protection facilities. Grid-enhancing technologies are useful but not substitutes for proper study and new transmission capacity.
quotes: ATC, along with other commenters, urges the Commission to separate studies for generation and load while preserving the flexibility for local planning authorities to rely upon their expertise to adjust sequencing and modeling.
Generation and load are functionally different and should be studied separately.
to the extent hybrid facilities are studied together, safeguards such as process matching and system protection facilities must be incorporated.
Misalignment between load and generation at a shared interconnection point can lead to unintended injections or withdrawals from the transmission system.
transmission owners lack the necessary tools to curtail firm service; therefore, the full impacts of any hybrid facility must be considered to prevent catastrophic consequences.

These tools can optimize existing assets, improve flexibility, and support localized stability, but they cannot fully mitigate reliability risks posed by hybrid facilities and large, highly variable loads.

letters.org: Americans for a Clean Energy Grid
letters.desc: ACEG argues that clearing interconnection queues for large loads requires proactive, comprehensive regional transmission planning under Order No. 1920, not piecemeal upgrade-by-upgrade processing. The filing calls for rapid implementation of Order 1920 alongside any new load interconnection rules, and for regional planners to independently assess and verify large load forecasts rather than relying on rolled-up utility submissions.
quotes: the ANOPR has a significant gap that may jeopardize the ability to achieve the stated goals, by not also specifically tackling the obstacles to building out the transmission needed to interconnect those loads.
the best way to integrate new facilities on the grid is to build out sufficient capacity through proactive well-planned multi-value transmission.

Building transmission upgrades on a sporadic, piecemeal basis to integrate certain resources is simply less efficient and more expensive than integrating both generation and load through proactive and comprehensive planning.

in the final rule, load forecasting was treated as it has always been: through rolling up the forecasts from individual transmission owners within a region. While this may have worked for conventional increases in demand, this does not work for the large loads being forecasted today.

the Commission could do more—either through a supplemental rulemaking associated with Order No. 1920 or provision of guidance in this proceeding—to require transmission planners to independently assess load forecasts and determine that they are sufficiently robust and as accurate as possible.

a requirement that large loads (50 MW or larger, for instance) are backed by stringent financial commitments and are reported to regional transmission planners so that significant loads can be adequately supported and integrated into the larger grid.

As the Commission seeks to accelerate interconnection of new loads, it should do so in conjunction with rapid implementation of Order No. 1920 and require regions to more quickly plan multi-value transmission lines and allocate costs to all customers who use—and benefit from—the integrated transmission system.

it would be a no-regrets course of action to speed regional and interregional transmission planning under Order No. 1920, enhanced by robust load forecasting to accommodate the new realities posed by large loads.

letters.org: Americans for a Clean Energy Grid
letters.desc: Advocates for proactive regional and interregional transmission planning that anticipates large-load demand rather than reacting to individual interconnection requests. Emphasizes need for improved load forecasting at the 75 MW threshold and holistic planning that harmonizes new loads with generation supply. Current siloed and reactive approaches are insufficient to meet utility-scale demand on industrial timelines.
quotes: The core challenge facing the electric system today is not merely procedural delay in generator interconnection studies, but the lack of sufficient transmission infrastructure and forward planning to accommodate new load and new generation in a timely manner... A planning construct designed for marginal load variation is no longer adequate when load is materializing at utility-scale magnitude and on industrial timelines.

the current siloed approach to transmission planning will not deliver infrastructure fast enough to ensure the United States continues to be a leader in artificial intelligence and is able to grow its manufacturing base. Widespread adoption of proactive transmission planning will better anticipate and plan for load and generation in an efficient and cost-effective manner.

Proactively planning transmission can increase transparency on the cost and timing of interconnection and identify cost-effective transmission solutions. In particular, when transmission is proactively planned, the costs for interconnection are provided to interconnection customers upfront, and developers have greater clarity on when they can interconnect, reducing uncertainty and the speculative behavior that increases queue timelines.

to plan better in order to develop a transmission grid that can support the nation's digital infrastructure needs. Doing so requires a holistic transmission planning process that harmonizes both new load interconnection with new generation supply. transmission planners must have a realistic picture of the generators and the large loads planning to interconnect to the transmission grid if they are to plan the grid in an efficient, cost-effective, and reliable manner.
must be understood as a core transmission-infrastructure priority one that modernizes and expands the grid at the scale required, not merely streamlines procedural steps.

Require improved regional forecasting for significant loads (75 MW or more). Ensure cost recovery and cost-allocation mechanisms that protect existing customers while allowing large loads to participate fairly in and benefit from the broader grid. Direct proactively planned multi-value high-capacity transmission as part of the solution

the transmission system must meet the moment. No procedural refinement or queue improvement can substitute for the foundational need for more regional and interregional transmission nor for planning frameworks that anticipate, rather than react to, large-load growth.

letters.desc: Antora asks that the non-firm, curtailable nature of flexible loads be built into the interconnection study process and resource adequacy requirements so study assumptions reflect actual operating profiles rather than full-capacity continuous use.
quotes: Antora urges the Commission, in crafting its remedy in this proceeding, to go beyond these recent reforms to require all transmission providers to: (1) offer permanent non-firm transmission service; (2) at rates reflecting actual use that is consistent with cost causation principles; (3) with curtailment requirements for non-firm load integrated into the interconnection study process and resource adequacy requirements.

letters.desc: Arevia strongly supports studying hybrid load and generation facilities together, including within cluster study frameworks, while respecting regional implementation variations.
quotes: Arevia supports and strongly recommends studying load and generation and hybrid project together.
Arevia supports studying large load projects within the cluster study framework, particularly when paired with a corresponding generation asset.
Arevia recognizes that implementation of cluster studies may vary based on regional planning process and defers to regional capabilities on this matter.

letters.desc: Base Power supports frameworks that embed dispatchability into interconnection study procedures and system planning. Contractible, defined performance metrics enable operators to model dispatchable loads accurately and reduce reliance on pessimistic assumptions about firm load.
quotes: Dispatchable load must become ubiquitously contractible.

The Commission should encourage mechanisms, such as expedited interconnection, to incentivize voluntary participation by large loads that choose to make their operations available as dispatchable system assets

Curtailable load and/or dispatchable hybrid facilities...must be implemented as defined, contractible commodities in order to be sufficiently integrated into both operations and system planning, with respect to large load interconnection processes.
establishing clear incentives for dispatchable performance is an appropriate and effective means of enhancing system reliability

letters.desc: Bloom strongly supports studying load and co-located generation together as a composite resource. The current bifurcated approach overstates upgrade needs; an integrated study can cut costs by billions and speed interconnection.
quotes: The ANOPR presents a major leap forward for interconnecting on-site generation and load as a composite resource.  The Commission should act expeditiously in adopting interconnection reforms.

Bloom takes no position on whether the Federal Power Act provides FERC jurisdiction over large load interconnections.  However, if the Commission declines to assert jurisdiction, Bloom urges the Commission to adopt reforms to the large generator interconnection procedures for interconnecting on-site large load – that is, new generation co-located with large load behind the same point of interconnection ("hybrid facilities").

Like the ANOPR, Brattle finds that an integrated interconnection study approach for new load and new generation based on requested firm withdrawals and injections can significantly reduce the need for transmission upgrades, potentially avoiding billions in transmission expansion costs.

under existing rules, load is studied as if it seeks firm rights to withdraw 100% from the transmission system to meet its requirements, while the generator is studied as if it seeks to inject 100% of its capacity into the transmission grid, with some RTOs, like PJM, requiring that generator capacity also be studied for deliverability to load throughout the system.  These bifurcated, non-integrated processes ignore on-site supply benefits and can improperly identify required Network Upgrades, resulting in slower interconnection and unnecessarily increasing Network Upgrade costs.
DOE's proposal makes sense, though the Commission should clarify that such rights refer to "firm" withdrawal and injection rights.

Consistent with existing reliability study requirements for Surplus Interconnection Service, a 90-day period to study hybrid facilities seems reasonable, provided requested withdrawal and injection rights do not identify the need for additional reliability studies to determine if Network Upgrades are required.

letters.desc: Buckeye supports standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to deter speculative projects and improve load forecasting. It also supports applying protections to large load interconnections already in the study process as a transition mechanism.
quotes: There is serious concern that these large loads could drive significant transmission investment and then not show up to pay for it on a sustained basis.
Buckeye supports requirements to deter speculative projects, such as standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties.

Although these requirements may prevent speculative projects from entering the study process, they do not address the major stranded cost concerns with data centers that complete the study process, cause massive transmission upgrades, but then do not have the expected level of demand over a sustained period.
Buckeye supports a transition mechanism for the treatment of large load interconnections that are already being studied.

letters.desc: Transmission owners and RTOs must conduct expedited interconnection studies that transparently disclose the specific constraints, system conditions, and hours driving upgrade needs. This transparency enables customers to develop targeted flexibility solutions that address identified system drivers.
quotes: Calibrant Energy Holdings, LLC ("Calibrant") supports the action taken by Secretary Wright to address the interconnection of large loads. The letter appropriately recognizes the benefits of large load flexibility and recommends an expedited interconnection study process for loads that are curtailable or co-located with generation or energy storage.

Ensure a transparent interconnection process for large loads, where the transmission owners and regional system operators ("RTO/ISOs") provide customers with the specific constraints, system conditions, and/or the hours that are driving the need for new system upgrades and investment. The clear identification of system needs will allow customers to develop solutions to address those needs.

Require that the transmission owners and RTO/ISOs study load flexibility (including hybrid configurations of load including generation or energy storage) as part of the load interconnection process and identify the amount of flexibility needed to avoid each system constraint identified in the study.

letters.desc: CAISO consistently supports study reforms while asking for flexibility so transmission providers can align large load processes with their existing Order No. 2023 procedures and regional planning frameworks. Gross component modeling must remain a requirement even under net-rights approaches.
quotes: Reforms grounded in the existing rules and procedures applicable to large, transmission-connected generators can be a pragmatic approach that can benefit the broader industry by providing consistency and clarity in the interconnection process for large loads.

Providing a single study process for large load, hybrid, and generating facilities may simplify many aspects for transmission providers and developers.  At the same time, it could introduce new complexities to the interconnection study process and transmission planning process, both of which have been significantly reformed by recent Commission orders.

The longstanding approach of enabling transmission providers to propose tailored processes to meet regional needs under the independent entity standard will allow transmission providers to tailor their studies to ensure the orderly and timely interconnection of large loads.

The CAISO supports this proposal, and recommends that if the Commission ultimately mandates specific reforms on this area, that any final rule enable transmission providers to align the large load processes with the processes transmission providers have established in complying with Order No. 2023.
Any final rule should clarify that transmission providers still must have detailed modeling information to 'study' the full load and generating capabilities of each individual part of the facility.
The CAISO also recommends that any reform include the requirement that large loads provide load profiles and expected behavior models as part of the interconnection process.

large loads should be required to submit detailed steady-state, dynamic (RMS), and, for certain facilities, electromagnetic transient (EMT) models reflecting expected demand behavior, similar to the modeling requirements currently applied to inverter-based generators.

letters.desc: The CPUC supports cooperative federalism through voluntary best practices with states to improve interconnection efficiency and study procedures. Standardized study processes must remain flexible enough to evolve with grid integration needs.
quotes: "developing voluntary best practices with states to improve interconnection efficiency, requiring load interconnection processes that enhance transparency, and other novel approaches" necessary at a particular moment.

"Any standardized procedures dealing with large load interconnection, including any efforts to address the costs of studying these customers, must be flexible enough to account for the evolving understanding of just what is necessary to integrate these customers to the grid."

letters.desc: Fisher presents CRE as a parallel path that sidesteps interconnection study queues entirely because CRE utilities are not interconnected to the bulk electric system, meaning they require no interconnection studies or approvals.
quotes: CRE offers a parallel path—privately built capacity that adds supply without affecting regulated rates or queues.

letters.org: CHAMBER OF COMMERCE OF THE UNITED STATES
letters.desc: The Chamber supports streamlining and automating interconnection studies to reduce delays, including through AI. It conditions that support on not upending working state-level processes and insists new queues must not delay requests already pending.
quotes: The Chamber is generally supportive of the Commission's efforts, in part due to the Department of Energy's entreaty, to explore reforms that have the potential to enhance the interconnection process for large loads.

the preexisting process, handled primarily on a state-level basis, is not broken everywhere. Many large loads have been and continue to be connected at the transmission level nationwide. Thus, any reforms proposed or implemented because of this proceeding should be mindful to not upend the progress that is currently being made to interconnect large loads across the country; new delays should not inadvertently be imposed by reforms intended to achieve the opposite result.

Streamlined Interconnection Processes: The Commission should prioritize reforms that reduce delays and administrative burdens in the interconnection process, including through the potential adoption of AI technologies to support the automation and acceleration of required studies, consistent with prudent utility practice.

the Commission should commit specific attention to ensuring that any new interconnection queues or processes not be developed or implemented in a way that unduly delays or interrupts pending requests.

letters.desc: Chevron supports fast-tracking interconnection studies for large loads and their supporting generation, endorsing SPP and MISO ERAS orders as models. It argues that multi-year queue waits are unacceptable and that the NOPR should build on the DOE ANOPR's fourteen principles to accelerate study timelines.
quotes: Chevron encourages the Commission to seize this opportunity to facilitate the expedited interconnection of large loads and generation to support it, including co-located generation.
The Commission should move forward with a rulemaking that generally accords with, and further develops, the fourteen principles set forth in the DOE ANOPR.
New power generation projects for data centers should not wait years in interconnection queues to reach commercial operations.

letters.desc: CEBA supports standardized interconnection study methodologies that model realistic large load operating behavior. Studies should incorporate advanced transmission technologies such as dynamic line ratings, follow Order 2023 precedent, and avoid queue-priority frameworks that undermine nondiscriminatory access.
quotes: CEBA strongly supports the ANOPR proposal to jointly study supply-side and large-load interconnection customers where practicable.

We recommend against introducing procedures which allow loads to 'skip ahead' either study or energization queues. 'Prioritization' frameworks introduce considerable room for fluctuating policy objectives to drive interconnection access and inevitably raise significant questions around non-discriminatory and non-preferential access.

CEBA recommends that the Commission require ATTs—including dynamic line ratings—to be evaluated alongside traditional upgrades for large load interconnections, consistent with Order No. 2023, given the significant benefits identified for consumers and interconnection customers.

FERC should also require transmission providers to study large-load interconnection requests based on realistic operating behavior, like the approach in Order 2023 for storage resources, to improve accuracy, avoid unnecessary upgrades, and reduce excessive costs.

letters.desc: ClearPath supports jointly studying large load and supply-side interconnection customers to reduce speculative queue behavior, identify cost-effective transmission solutions, and ensure all beneficiaries pay. It also recommends that studies use actual operating characteristics rather than worst-case scenarios, which overstate impacts and inflate costs for flexible loads.
quotes: ClearPath strongly supports the ANOPR's proposal to jointly study supply-side interconnection customers and large load interconnection customers to the extent practicable.

developers of both generation and large loads often submit multiple interconnection requests as a means of price discovery and time-to-grid discovery. This creates unmanageable queue volumes, inflated demand and supply forecasts, and significant delays to the interconnection process due to projects withdrawing late into the process when they discover their project is not economically feasible due to costs or energization timelines.

Coordinating interconnection studies for large loads with supply-side interconnection can enable the identification of more cost-effective transmission solutions and ensure that all benefiting customers pay, whether they are load or supply customers.

ClearPath recommends that FERC require transmission providers to study large loads based on their known operating characteristics to increase the accuracy of these studies, avoid unnecessary network upgrades that can slow interconnection, and reduce excessive costs.

We recommend that FERC adopt a similar approach for studying large load withdrawals and/or injections. This advances just and reasonable rates by avoiding overestimation of the impacts of large loads through study assumptions that depict worst-case scenarios, such as curtailable large loads withdrawing at full capacity during peak demand periods

letters.desc: AI-SCA argues that current interconnection timelines are too slow and urges FERC to push transmission providers to develop procedures that produce faster results. It frames long lead times for power access as the defining barrier for data center and AI supply chain development.
quotes: access to sufficient power – and the long lead times often associated with securing it – has become a central barrier to new economic development opportunities in the United States.

Meeting the growing demand from new, critical large loads requires accelerating interconnection processes and establishing additional pathways for large loads to connect to the transmission system in ways that manage costs and preserve long-term reliability for all customers.

we urge the Commission to encourage additional parameters and information from transmission providers to develop large load interconnection procedures that provide flexibility and that result in interconnection times that are faster than current processes.

letters.desc: Committee strongly supports protection of Order 2023 generator interconnection reforms and opposes any discrimination between generators based on whether they support data centers.
quotes: FERC must protect open and non-discriminatory access to the power grid and not undermine the reforms made to generator interconnection queues in Order 2023.
FERC must not allow transmission providers to discriminate between generators based on resource type or if a generator is supporting a data center.

letters.desc: Constellation urges FERC to issue a full or targeted order in the pending PJM Show Cause proceedings immediately, rather than waiting for a comprehensive final rule. It contends the record is fully developed and further delay allows Transmission Owner obstruction to continue unchecked.
quotes: the Commission should "build upon these principles" by issuing a full order in the PJM Show Cause proceedings consistent with the ANOPR's guidance based upon the extensive record already established in that consolidated docket.

The lack of consistent standards for large loads and hybrid facilities creates a vacuum that leaves Transmission Owners with significant discretion to delay or deny large-load and co-location proposals and to impose terms that are neither just nor reasonable.

the Commission should issue a full order in the PJM Show Cause proceedings confirming its preliminary finding that the PJM Tariff is unjust and unreasonable because it does not contain "provisions addressing with sufficient clarity or consistency the rates, terms, and conditions of service that apply to co-location arrangements"

the Commission should immediately order the following: PJM must establish a timeline -- with milestones -- for the completion of load interconnection studies for hybrid in-front-of-the-meter configurations ... with an absolute study completion deadline, including Transmission Owner input, of six months.
the Commission should adopt clear, uniform standards, which should also consider large load forecasting standards and other measures that will expedite large load studies and interconnections.

the Commission should grandfather interconnection studies that already are substantially completed by the time the Commission accepts final compliance filings in response to the Commission's final rules.

letters.desc: Constellation supports standardized study rules and deposits to deter speculative load requests and prevent undue discrimination, drawing lessons from Order No. 2003 generator interconnection procedures. The filing also calls for load forecasting improvements as part of a reliability package.
quotes: the Commission should (i) act quickly, (ii) focus relief in regions where there is evidence of undue discrimination, undue preference or unjust and unreasonable service, (iii) respect regional differences, and (iv) avoid unnecessary jurisdictional fights.

the Commission should issue a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking ("NOPR") that builds upon the principles in the ANOPR and responds to the four areas of consensus. The NOPR should: (i) establish deadlines to meet the Secretary's timeline for a final rule by April 30, 2026; (ii) solicit specific evidence of unjust and unreasonable service for large loads and/or undue discrimination or preference by Transmission Owners to support the Commission's required Federal Power Act ("FPA") section 206 showing in each region and state

Constellation supports extending the option to build to large-load interconnection customers on terms equivalent to those afforded to generator interconnection customers under Order No. 845. Providing qualified customers the ability to construct interconnection facilities under host-utility standards reduces delay, increases certainty, and mirrors the efficiency benefits the Commission recognized when adopting the generator option to build.

letters.desc: Constellation supports reforming interconnection study processes to build on existing studies at existing POIs. LCEP would confirm that already-studied thermal conditions remain valid rather than conducting full new studies, reducing time and cost.
quotes: Constellation submits these supplemental comments to outline a new, reliable, speed-to-service option pairing new generation with large loads at existing power plant sites of at least the same size, and to urge this option's inclusion in the Commission's next steps on the Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking.

This proposal achieves Secretary Wright's objective "to ensure efficient, timely, and non-discriminatory [large] load interconnections" by adding paired new generation and load without changing injection rights or creating withdrawal rights at existing generation sites.

Any final rule on the ANOPR must find that existing tariffs are unjust and unreasonable because they fail to meet "unprecedented current and expected growth of large loads seeking to interconnect to the transmission system" and find that new "standardize[d] interconnection procedures and agreements for such loads, including those seeking to share a point of interconnection with new or existing generation facilities (hybrid facilities)" are required.

Constellation's analysis identified one particular lost opportunity: the current rules do not clearly accommodate the pairing of new generator/load combinations at existing generator's Points of Interconnection that create no new thermal power flow conditions which have not already been studied.

Where additional load, paired with new generation, can be served at an existing Point of Interconnection within the already studied parameters, it is unjust and unreasonable that the existing pro forma LGIP does not provide a pathway to do so.

LCEP Service as outlined here and in Attachment A is just and reasonable and not unduly discriminatory or preferential. Like Surplus Interconnection Service, LCEP Service is an expedited interconnection process outside of the standard interconnection queue for new generation paired with new load at sites with existing generation facilities that have already been studied.
The LCEP Proposal is animated by and can achieve the goal of speed to power for large load projects stymied today by extremely long interconnection timelines.
All such study processes must be tailored to accommodate speed to service or the efficiencies of siting at Points of Interconnection already proven to be reliable will be lost.

The Commission should also require Transmission Providers to clearly identify the studies for evaluating LCEP Service requests. Clear and transparent rules on the studies performed by Transmission Providers are critical to prevent delay.
LCEP Service is one of the simplest and most efficient ways to achieve speed-to-service without jeopardizing reliability or increasing costs to other customers.

LCEP Service also is fully responsive to the ANOPR's directives and principles, including to study load together with Generating Facilities, given "siting a large load near or at the same point of interconnection as a new generating facility could reduce the network upgrades needed to interconnect only the load or only the generating facility" (Third Principle), and incentivizing co-location which can "ensure[] efficient buildout of the transmission system" (Fifth Principle).

letters.desc: Critical Loop asks FERC to require studies that model LLFC flexibility on a basis comparable to traditional upgrades, use time-series and probabilistic methods rather than only worst-case deterministic assumptions, and include side-by-side upgrade tables. Transmission providers and RTOs should also track and publish interconnection timeline statistics so reform progress can be measured.
quotes: for many large loads, time-to-power is the binding constraint. Interconnection queues are severely backlogged, and new transmission and generation are often contentious to permit and develop.

Requirements to curtail should be expressed in duration, magnitude, or frequency and should be built from time-series and probabilistic tools rather than relying only on worst-case deterministic assumptions.

we ask the Commission to ensure that flexible solutions and LLFCs are studied on a basis that can be compared with traditional upgrades. This occurs by requiring transmission providers to explicitly model enforceable flexibility and operating envelopes, rather than defaulting to static maximum-withdrawal assumptions that treat all co-located resources as absent or charging.

Transmission providers and RTOs might be required to track and publish basic statistics for large-load interconnections, such as the time from request to initial determination and from request to energization, broken out by interconnection type and voltage level.

letters.desc: Crusoe supports study-process reforms but ties their effectiveness to removing speculative queue entries first. Accurate load data is a prerequisite for reliable interconnection studies.
quotes: Joint interconnection studies for hybrid facilities that bring new generation with load will expedite the interconnection process and minimize the need for costly and time-consuming construction of network upgrades because the impact of the new load can be offset by the addition of new generation.

Speculative interconnection requests are hindering AI deployment across the country.  Speculative requests will continue to delay interconnection for large scale projects and lead to uncertainty in real load demand.

letters.desc: CTC requests that transmission providers explicitly evaluate reconductoring with commercially available advanced conductors as a standard alternative in interconnection and planning studies. The company argues this approach directly advances FERC's objectives by minimizing costly network upgrades and ensuring timely interconnection.
quotes: Reconductoring with advanced conductors is a proven, fast, and cost-effective way to create transmission headroom on existing corridors.

Carbon composite core advanced conductors can double the capacity on existing structures because they do not have the increase in weight and sag necessary when capacity is increased with early and mid-1900s steel core conductors like ACSR and ACSS.

Should FERC decide to invoke authority over the interconnection of large loads greater than 20 megawatts (MW), we urge the Commission to require transmission providers to explicitly evaluate reconductoring with commercially available advanced conductors as a standard alternative in interconnection and planning studies before ordering more extensive network upgrades.

Southern California Edison reconductored 137 miles of its 230 kV Big Creek transmission corridor with ACCC Conductor, avoiding a costly rebuild while eliminating sag violations and adding more than 60% additional line capacity. The project cut costs from $135 million to $48 million, reduced completion time from 48 to 18 months, improved safety, lowered line losses by 30%, and delivered significant environmental and customer savings.

letters.desc: DCC supports integrated interconnection studies and broader transmission planning reform, framing interconnection delays as a symptom of insufficient infrastructure rather than a standalone procedural problem.
quotes: interconnection reform is a prerequisite for U.S. leadership in AI, advanced manufacturing, and the digital economy
the goal of this proceeding must be to "accelerate—not pause—critical load and generation projects already advancing under existing frameworks."
DCC advocated for studying new load and new generation together to capture system benefits.
interconnection delays as a "symptom of a deeper and more structural issue"—a lack of sufficient transmission infrastructure and forward-looking planning.

DCC's call for the Commission to "focus on the infrastructure challenge through appropriate long-term transmission planning" and to require deployment of grid-enhancing technologies is a necessary component of any effective interconnection reform effort.

letters.desc: DEC cites multi-year queues and inconsistent study processes as the primary barrier for large-load developers. It asks FERC to direct transmission providers to post transparent study timelines and milestone schedules, and to take corrective action when deadlines are missed.
quotes: Developers face multi-year queues, inconsistent study processes, and unclear cost responsibilities that slow deployment and create uncertainty.

DEC supports the Department's initiative and encourages the Commission to establish a transparent, performance-based framework that recognizes flexibility as a grid resource, accelerates access to transmission, and ensures reliability and fairness for all users.

The Commission should direct jurisdictional transmission providers to include clear procedures within their Open Access Transmission Tariffs (OATTs) for evaluating large, transmission-level customers capable of providing real-time telemetry and verifiable curtailment.
Recognizing flexible demand within existing OATT frameworks would not create new service categories but would clarify how transmission providers study, model, and coordinate with these facilities.
Transmission providers should post transparent study timelines, milestone schedules, and progress updates for these projects to ensure accountability and predictability.
The absence of consistent frameworks across RTOs and ISOs creates uncertainty for developers and operators.

letters.desc: DPN backs studying load and hybrid facilities together with generation, arguing it enables efficient siting and reduces the need for costly network upgrades.
quotes: load and hybrid facilities should be studied together with generating facilities. Such an approach will allow for efficient siting of loads and generating facilities and thereby minimize the need for costly network upgrades.

letters.desc: EDF supports a standardized, nondiscriminatory load interconnection queue modeled on the LGIP, with better storage modeling, transparent procedures, and tiered treatment based on grid impact.
quotes: EDF supports the DOE Secretary's request for the Commission to establish a uniform, open access framework for large load and hybrid facilities to interconnect to the transmission system that does not infringe on the jurisdiction of the relevant state regulatory authorities.

A bifurcated or tiered review process should be implemented, allowing low-impact loads that are inherently less likely to cause significant transmission system upgrades to be studied and brought online more quickly than higher-impact loads.

interconnection studies should better utilize storage assets in interconnection requests.  Currently, interconnection studies do not accurately model real time operating characteristics of storage resources, which limits opportunities for storage resources to be deployed to serve large load needs.

letters.desc: EEI supports interconnection study processes that are flexible enough to handle diverse load characteristics but include strong readiness requirements and adequate deposits to prevent the queue saturation seen in generator interconnection programs.
quotes: EEI member companies agree that any large-load interconnection program or tariff adopted by the Commission must address speculative projects and provide a framework to allow transmission providers to more accurately forecast demand on their systems. With a large load interconnection, a study will need to be performed. Study deposits sufficient not only to cover the cost of the study but also to deter speculative study requests are appropriate.

Generator interconnection queues became unmanageable precisely because they permitted entry without strong readiness requirements which hindered transmission planning and delayed needed infrastructure.

letters.desc: EEI supports studying large load interconnections in a way that reflects their actual use of the grid, including curtailability, rather than applying uniform or net-based assumptions that misrepresent true system impact.
quotes: EEI members share the Administration's goal of enabling speed-to-power for large load customers.  We urge the Commission to move deliberately forward in a manner that protects other customers, ensures grid reliability, and acknowledges the distinct role of the states.

letters.desc: EEI supports orderly study processes for large load interconnections and cites FERC approval of study processes in SPP as a model. The filing frames timely, transparent studies as central to achieving speed and predictability.
quotes: EEI shares the Administration's commitment to energy dominance and specifically supports improving the speed, efficiency, fairness, and predictability of large load interconnections.

EEI member companies are committed to working collaboratively with states, large load customers, the Commission, and other stakeholders to ensure the timely interconnection of large loads while protecting all customers and the grid.
Approve a Large Load study process and Generation Assessment process in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP).

letters.desc: EPSA supports a standardized, open-access interconnection study process to replace opaque, unfiled Transmission Owner procedures. It urges the Commission to complete the PJM Show Cause proceeding and to protect advanced in-flight projects through legacy treatment during any transition.
quotes: rules of the road are necessary to provide sufficient market certainty and the transparency needed to enable large loads to interconnect to the transmission system efficiently and fairly, and to be able to do so quickly.

It would be entirely inconsistent with the intent of the ANOPR to further delay resolution of the Show Cause proceeding to clarify the rules applicable to large load interconnections in PJM, which has been awaiting Commission action based on an extensive record for over six months.

existing projects that have reached advanced interconnection milestones should be afforded legacy-based treatment in order to rely on the framework under which their commercial arrangement has made substantial progress.

interconnection procedures and agreements for large loads require a level of standardization to establish certainty and transparency – both of which are sorely lacking today in the opaque and unfiled individual Transmission Owner processes that exacerbate confusion and delay regarding new load connections while furthering uncertainty by establishing load forecasts inflated by speculative projects.

establishing a clear, expedited glide path for large load customer interconnections to the transmission system should bring visibility to committed new demand, shining a light on how much of forecasted demand growth is ready and able to join the system.
we need a transparent, workable process that resolves the problems of the existing transmission owner processes which are not subject to open access principles.
the Commission should direct ISOs/RTOs to complete studies within a specific time – bundled on a concurrent timeline with any transmission owner studies to the extent possible.

letters.desc: ELCON supports interconnection studies tailored to the operational needs of new large loads, including coordination with generator queues for better forecasting. Regions with existing adequate protocols should be able to satisfy requirements without being overridden by one-size-fits-all federal rules.
quotes: Rather than instituting an arbitrary MW threshold, the Commission should understand what load interconnection protocols have already been established in certain regions and tailor principles to address the bottlenecks that are specific to new large loads and their electricity needs.
responsible entities should be provided with an opportunity to demonstrate that its current rules and procedures meet or exceed any Commission guidelines.

Requirements that are specifically targeted to remove speculative projects that will never be built (or projects that 'shop' multiple connection points) will effectively reduce the number of studies to be performed and provide a more accurate load forecast.

ELCON appreciates the flexibility provided by principles five through seven to study load interconnection requests according to their operational needs and allow for expedited study for those customers agreeing to be curtailable and/or dispatchable.

Varying configurations of large loads, sometimes combined with behind-the-meter generation, must be considered in interconnection studies to allow for the most efficient solutions to serving large loads.
Coordinating the generator interconnection process with the large load interconnection process would, in itself, improve load forecasting as well as siting decisions, as recognized in the ANOPR.

letters.desc: ECA regards joint study of loads and their associated generation as one of the largest benefits Commission action can provide. It also supports broader transmission planning reform to better incorporate large load growth and associated generation development.
quotes: Aligning load interconnection and generator interconnection and better incorporating large load growth into transmission planning are the two biggest benefits action on the ANOPR can provide.
ECA strongly agrees with the need for study processes to more closely link new large loads with the new generation resources that they may wish to construct or contract.

letters.desc: ECA argues that unclear large load interconnection rules harm both large customers seeking speed to power and other customers exposed to cost shift, giving FERC ample basis to act. ECA supports broad reforms covering all transmission providers and opposes narrowing the scope to RTOs or unbundled systems only.
quotes: Commission action on large load interconnection to the transmission system is needed to ensure just and reasonable rates and prevent undue discrimination and will open new opportunities to meet the needs of new large loads for "speed to power" while protecting other customers from harm.

Large load customers like data centers, manufacturers, and industry are seeking opportunities to pay for and accelerate timelines for the generation and transmission infrastructure needed to serve them, but are stymied by inconsistent and unclear rules for large load interconnection to transmission, a lack of clear paths to line up load interconnection with the interconnection and delivery of generation they construct or contract to serve them, and fractured and incomplete transmission planning processes that fail to holistically account for projected new large loads and associated generation

ECA suggests a guidelines-based approach, requiring transmission providers across the country to demonstrate that they have in place procedures and agreements for large load interconnection to the transmission system that meet minimum guidelines prescribed by the Commission.

It is entirely reasonable for the Commission to base action here on the unremarkable theory that unprecedented growth in demand from large load customers, combined with unclear and uncertain procedures and agreements for interconnection of such loads to the transmission system that limit the development of new infrastructure to serve them, will lead to unjust and unreasonable rates and the potential for undue discrimination in the provision of transmission service.

The Commission should reject the suggestion that it limit the scope of its required reforms to only those systems where rates for transmission service are unbundled (which could be interpreted as a request to limit the reach of reforms only to Regional Transmission Organizations and Independent System Operators (RTOs/ISOs)).

letters.desc: ECA supports proactive, multi-value regional transmission planning rather than piecemeal reactive approaches. The filing argues that bottom-up proposals from RTOs, utilities, states, and customers should be encouraged to reflect regional differences, and that regional planning processes must be capable of accommodating large loads at reasonable cost.
quotes: no single transmission cost allocation methodology is likely to address all stakeholder concerns. More targeted approaches may better align with cost-causation principles but may also generate disputes regarding attribution of transmission needs and costs.

Bottom-up proposals from states, utilities, RTOs, large load customers, and other stakeholders should be encouraged, especially where they reflect regional differences and pursue more holistic approaches to how the system is planned and paid for.

The most durable path is likely to combine strong state retail tariffs, better and more granular federal-state alignment, improved transparency, targeted federal reforms where transmission costs, planning processes, or cost allocation decisions are beyond the reach of state retail regulation, alongside innovative new customer-centric approaches to transmission planning and expansion outside traditional approaches.

letters.desc: The filing contends that the current study process forces flexible loads to be evaluated at worst-case inflexible peak, overstating required upgrades. Fixing this requires a parallel FLFT study track with a 60 to 90 day timeline and the ability for curtailable customers to be studied against their committed net withdrawal profile.
quotes: The greatest opportunity in this rulemaking is not merely streamlining the administrative study process, but enabling large loads to actively avoid or defer massive grid and energy infrastructure upgrades.

Transmission service frameworks do not yet exist to allow for load flexibility to avoid network upgrades. Network Integration Transmission Service at the wholesale level is non-interruptible under FERC's pro forma tariff. And, while non-firm point-to-point service does exist, there is no non-firm network option for a load to access and draw upon the full network during times it is not curtailed. Nor do utilities studying large load interconnection generally provide a pathway through which a curtailable customer can be studied to avoid network upgrades.

the FLFT would allow facilities meeting defined flexibility thresholds to receive interconnection approval within 60 to 90 days, based on verification of available firm capacity and demonstration of control and telemetry systems.

letters.desc: Non-firm service status for loads with generation allows facilities to be studied as integrated assets, reducing study complexity and timelines while managing supply chain bottlenecks. Load flexibility lowers peak demand assumptions used in transmission planning.
quotes: LCDG enables loads to operate as non-firm service customers, thus allowing facilities to be studied as integrated load-generation assets to manage near-term transmission constraints and supply chain bottlenecks.

large loads can be made flexible with respect to the transmission system through the deployment of on-site or co-located generation. Acknowledging load flexibility during the transmission planning and interconnection processes allows transmission planners to assume lower peak demand for the associated load facility, thereby reducing the immediate need for transmission upgrades and expediting interconnection timelines.

letters.desc: The filer urges the Commission to adopt rules facilitating joint study processes, even provisionally, that evaluate co-located and hybrid facilities such as its LCDG model based on operational behavior and net load impacts, which it says reduces system strain and unlocks grid headroom.
quotes: Enchanted Rock encourages the Commission to adopt rules that will facilitate joint study processes (even if only for a provisional period) and that evaluate co-located and hybrid facilities based on their net impacts to the grid.

a joint study process would allow LCDG and hybrid facilities to be studied based on their operational behavior and net load impacts, which Enchanted Rock believes will result in less strain on the transmission system, unlock available grid headroom, optimize existing transmission infrastructure and more accurately model the flexible capabilities of the system.

letters.desc: ETI argues that the ANOPR's study of interconnection principles is incomplete because it omits price formation. The filing calls for FERC to reopen its price formation inquiry and for DOE to use statutory authority to compel that review, treating market pricing reform as integral to any interconnection study.
quotes: Missing from these principles is a critical core principle that the Commission and the DOE should consider to efficiently shore up large load interconnection: price formation in the Regional Transmission Organization ("RTO") and Independent System Operator ("ISO") markets.
Meeting this growing load will require significant new generation, transmission, and flexible resources—all of which depend on clear and durable RTO-ISO price signals.

ETI recommends that the Commission reopen its price formation inquiry to enact needed RTO-ISO pricing reforms, and absent action initiated by the Commission, for the DOE to formally exercise its statutory authority requesting that the Commission to do so.

letters.org: Enerwise Global Technologies, LLC dba CPower
letters.desc: Interconnection studies should analyze large loads in combination with multiple resource types, including load flexibility. This broader approach can accelerate interconnection by leveraging resources that deploy faster.
quotes: While new generation and transmission infrastructure will be part of the solution, other more quickly deployable solutions, such as load flexibility, will be necessary. Simply put, load flexibility helps balance supply and demand by reducing demand when called upon by the grid operator.

The ANOPR proposes to allow for expedited interconnection of large loads that co-locate with generation. While this is likely to be an important part of the solution space, relying on new generation alone to meet increased demand will put reliability at risk in the intervening years that it takes for these generation assets to come online.

The Joint Parties suggest revising principles three, five, and seven as discussed below. Principle three states that 'to the extent practicable, load and hybrid facilities should be studied together with generating facilities'. This principle should be expanded to allow for study with other types of incremental resources, including load flexibility, in the appropriate location.

Principle five states that 'hybrid facilities should be studied based on the amount of injection and/or withdrawal rights requested'. The Joint Parties agree with this principle but ask that it be clarified that a hybrid facility would include not just load coupled with generation but also load coupled with any other appropriately located incremental resource, including flexible load.

Principle seven states that 'the interconnection study of large loads that agree to be curtailable and hybrid facilities that agree to be curtailable and dispatchable should be expedited.' The Joint Parties agree with this principle but ask that it be expanded to state that large loads that agree to be curtailable or that arrange for load flexibility with an appropriately sited resource be entitled to an expedited interconnection process.

letters.desc: ENGIE supports studying load, hybrid, and generation facilities together to improve accuracy, reduce duplication, and capture the net load and flexibility contributions of hybrid projects. SPP's CPP is highlighted as a leading model.
quotes: ENGIE strongly supports this principle. We believe that a more holistic approach to system planning, including the studying of all types of facilities together, provides a more complete picture of how new facilities will interact with the electric grid.
ENGIE would like to highlight the Southwest Power Pool's ("SPP") soon to be implemented Coordinated Planning Process ("CPP") for being the most robust, holistic planning process of any ISO/RTO.

ENGIE strongly supports this proposal for several reasons. First, focusing on the requested injection and withdrawal level will increase the accuracy of the interconnection process by aligning interconnection studies with the facility's actual impact on the grid.

letters.org: Entergy Services, LLCEntergy New Orleans, LLCEntergy Louisiana, LLC ,Entergy Mississippi, LLC ,Entergy Arkansas, LLC ,Entergy Texas, Inc. ,
letters.desc: Entergy points to the LPSC's new guidelines as evidence that state commissions are already conducting the oversight and review needed to protect customers during large load interconnection.
quotes: the Louisiana Public Service Commission ("LPSC") adopted non-binding guidelines for the interconnection of large loads that are intended to ensure that the interests of all customers are protected and balanced.

letters.desc: Cluster studies already identify the transmission and distribution reinforcements triggered by individual large-load requests, but utilities do not use that information to assign costs back to the causers. ELPC recommends that study results be tied directly to cost allocation.
quotes: the Company practices that do provide tracking of these transmission costs are not used to pursue cost allocation that would apply cost-causation principles.
The Company does not plan to use Cluster Studies to assign the costs of new facilities to the Large Demand Project Applicants or Customers that cause those costs.

letters.desc: Eolian supports adoption of pro forma large load interconnection procedures to eliminate the non-transparent, jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction variation that currently enables undue discrimination. It proposes a serial streamlined study track for hybrid facilities and queue priority for curtailable loads as the two central study reforms.
quotes: Eolian strongly supports the Commission's effort to ensure the timely and orderly interconnection of large loads to the transmission system.

Flexibility commitments from loads and hybrid resources can help to protect existing customers by avoiding the need for transmission system upgrades and allowing large loads to reduce the resource adequacy impacts of their interconnection and allow large loads—and the resources needed to serve them—to come online quickly without the need for extensive study or network upgrades.

existing interconnection processes for large loads and hybrid resources suffer from a lack of standardization—both because they differ markedly from jurisdiction to jurisdiction, and because they often rely on unwritten, non-transparent practices and afford unwarranted discretion to the local utility.

The absence of standardized, transparent procedures creates opportunities for undue discrimination in queue processing and transmission upgrade cost assignment as public utilities negotiate individual contracts with loads.

the Commission should direct transmission providers to provide for a FERC-jurisdictional load interconnection process that grants queue priority to loads that make commitments to curtail, and hybrid facilities that make commitments to dispatch and curtail, such that (a) the load or hybrid resource reduces the system's need for capacity or Network Resources, and/or (b) avoids the need for network upgrades.

serial streamlined study of load and hybrid facilities is possible where the facility nominates operating limits (in MW) for aggregate net injections and withdrawals of power, installs necessary control equipment to ensure that the facility is capable of following the dispatch controls of the transmission system operator and balancing authority and respecting operating limits at all times, and is capable at any time of complete self-supply or otherwise curtailing the load such that the facility can take transmission service on a non-firm basis.
each transmission owner can independently conduct streamlined hybrid interconnection processes (even within an ISO/RTO region) in serial fashion in as little as 60-90 days.

letters.desc: Eolian calls for a single, serial, integrated interconnection study for hybrid facilities studied together based on their requested operating limits, completed within a 90-day target. It argues that current pro forma procedures lack any mechanism for studying paired generation and load together, which must change through a Commission rule.
quotes: The Commission must assert jurisdiction over the interconnection of large loads and establish federal requirements for the interconnections of large loads because that step is necessary to ensure that the bulk power system is capable of reliably and affordably integrating large loads.

Consistent with ANOPR Principles Three, Five, and Six, integrated joint study of hybrid load and generation facilities based on requested withdrawal and injection rights is critical to enabling rapid, affordable interconnection of large loads and hybrids.
The load and generation components of a hybrid facility are no different and would be separately subject to such contingency studies under a joint study approach.

The establishment of a non-firm network transmission service tier should be a core part of any final rule, as such a service tier is integral to enabling transmission providers to expedite interconnection for curtailable large loads and curtailable and dispatchable hybrid facilities.

just as an express checkout line appropriately rewards those whose needs can be addressed more quickly with faster service, it is appropriate to study curtailable and dispatchable facilities on a separate, streamlined basis due to their lesser impacts on the broader system

FERC could avoid repeating the problems that have plagued generator interconnection queues through an approach that provides greater up-front cost certainty to interconnection customers, which is the single most powerful tool for reducing speculative and duplicative requests, study complexity, and re-studies.
adopting hybrid-specific rules are a consensus, no-regrets reform that allows the Commission to tackle the lowest hanging fruit of the large load growth challenge.

letters.desc: Eolian argues that load and generation interconnection studies must be coordinated, with consistent standards for when and how load is reflected in generator studies. Real-world examples from PJM and PacifiCorp show that omitting nearby load from generator studies inflates network upgrade costs by tens to hundreds of millions of dollars and can cancel viable projects.
quotes: we have not encountered any transmission provider that currently has a process which (i) adequately integrates or coordinates the interconnection of supply resources and load, (ii) provides developers of supply resources such as Eolian with adequate incentive to locate generation and storage assets in a manner that opens additional system headroom for load interconnection, or (iii) offers the full range of transmission service options necessary to allow supply and load to coordinate to optimally use the existing system and reduce transmission infrastructure needs.

The lack of tariff provisions to afford all three elements results in unjust and unreasonable or unduly discriminatory rates by exacerbating the reliability and affordability impacts of large load growth, while impeding speed-to-power for new large loads.

the Commission can require load and generation study coordination even if it decides against asserting jurisdiction over load interconnection by requiring transmission providers to coordinate in generation interconnection study processes with the relevant transmission owners or electric distribution companies conducting load interconnection studies.
the Commission should require consistent standards for when and how load is included in generator interconnection studies.

PJM's Phase II study results assigned $158 million in network upgrade costs to Matta Grid, largely driven by a grid constraint 25 miles from both the Matta Grid project and the proposed Amazon data center. A Timmons Group study that Eolian commissioned demonstrated that, had PJM included even a very conservative 150 MW of the 770 MW of Amazon load in its Phase II study for Transition Cycle 1, the study results would have shown over $100 million less in system reinforcements assigned to the Matta Grid project.

utilities may provide for outcomes that maximize their own return on equity while triggering the construction of infrastructure that would not be needed were the process to more accurately reflect planned system additions.
