letters.desc: esVolta supports studying large loads together with proximate BESS under standardized national procedures. The filer argues that a controllable BESS injection modeled at the same point of interconnection reduces network upgrade scope and satisfies reliability criteria more efficiently than studying the load alone.
quotes: Absent clear, standardized procedures for large load and hybrid interconnections, transmission providers will continue to rely on ad hoc approaches that risk delaying critical projects, exacerbating reliability concerns, and shifting costs to non-participating customers in ways that are inconsistent with open access and just and reasonable rate requirements.

If an ANOPR is issued, it should seek to include a proposal that articulates core principles, such as studying large loads and hybrid facilities together with generation where practicable, recognizing curtailable and dispatchable configurations (including those supported by BESS) for expedited treatment, and aligning cost responsibility with the specific injection and withdrawal rights requested.

In esVolta's view, the Commission's large-load reforms present an important opportunity to recognize that BESS can directly mitigate these power quality concerns and thereby assist in facilitating the timely and orderly interconnection of large loads consistent with the principles of reform outlined in this proceeding.

Battery energy storage is a proven solution to meeting near-term and longer-term resource adequacy and reliability needs, with a modular design that can be right sized based on need, and one of the shortest construction time frames of any resource (12-18 months).

Studying large loads together with BESS aligns closely with the Department's emphasis on the timely and orderly interconnection of large loads. Where a large load is electrically proximate to BESS that is designed to provide the services described above, the combined configuration is better able to satisfy applicable reliability and power quality criteria without imposing excessive incremental burdens on the transmission system.
BESS enables the large loads to be curtailable or flexible and should jointly be eligible for an expedited pathway to interconnection.

letters.desc: ETX supports a new Load Interconnection Study Procedures modeled on LGIP, with graduated deposits, expedited pathways for mature and flexible projects, open non-discriminatory access, and self-build rights. It urges FERC to reject designs that favor certain participants over others.
quotes: FERC's Form LGIP for generation resources is a reasonable pro-forma for graduated/escalating study deposits and readiness requirements for a new load study procedure ("Load Interconnection Study Procedures"), including formulaic mechanisms for refundability of deposits in the early stages of the process.
The additional and most potent commercial readiness criteria ETX recommends for consideration by the Commission is a Permitting and/or Public Acceptance qualification.

The Commission should reject any Load Interconnection Study Procedures that inherently rewards certain load/market participants to the detriment of others. Open access to the transmission system must be protected in both statute and practice.

The Load Interconnection Study Procedures should establish expedited pathways for more mature projects that pass greater readiness thresholds and for projects with flexible requirements or capabilities that can limit transmission system impacts.

The Load Interconnection Study Procedures should allow for flexible project sizing amendments based on study results that encourage efficient use of transmission resources, especially for Hybrid and/or co-located projects where parallel load and generation studies will create modeling circularities.

Self-build of the interconnection facilities should continue to be an option for projects managed through the Load Interconnection Study Process as it allows the market to optimize for speed and cost, eliminating potential deliverability or cost-inflation bottlenecks.

letters.desc: Exelon argues that interconnection reform alone is insufficient because generation capacity is not keeping pace with retiring resources and rising demand. PJM in particular faces structural barriers to new supply, and the Commission should advance reforms that also speed generator interconnection.
quotes: Large load interconnection frameworks must not only aim to expediently, fairly, and reliably interconnect new customers, these processes must also take care not to exacerbate affordability challenges facing the country.
Generation capacity is not being developed fast enough to replace retiring resources and meet these expanded demands on the system.

letters.desc: Fervo supports coordinated study processes and modeling frameworks that align large-load and hybrid interconnections with generator procedures, creating procedural consistency and enabling existing projects to retain queue benefits.
quotes: a 20 MW threshold is reasonable, appropriately tailored to the types of high-impact projects this rulemaking is intended to address, and fully consistent with the structure of the existing pro forma LGIP and LGIA

The LGIP framework is the Commission's established mechanism for studying and processing generation interconnection requests that can materially affect transmission system reliability. Aligning the applicability threshold for large-load and hybrid interconnections with this framework can ensure procedural consistency, reduce administrative complexity for transmission providers, and create a predictable pathway for customers whose system impacts are similar to those of large generators.

Fervo supports the Commission's focus on ensuring that large-load and hybrid interconnection customers demonstrate commercial readiness before entering and advancing through the interconnection queue. Fervo encourages the Commission to prioritize readiness criteria that mirror the maturity expectations already applied to large generator interconnection customers, including demonstrated site control or contracting milestones.

Applying a readiness framework to load and hybrid customers can help transmission providers distinguish commercially viable projects, improve queue efficiency, and reduce speculative requests without imposing unnecessary financial barriers.

Fervo therefore recommends that generation projects already in the generation interconnection queue, or in late-stage development, be permitted to elect into the new coordinated hybrid study framework where doing so would better reflect these reduced system impacts.

Allowing transmission providers to apply the new modeling assumptions, hybrid treatment rules, and coordinated study processes to existing queue positions, without forcing restudy or loss of queue priority, would ensure that early geothermal hybrid projects can access the benefits of reforms intended for exactly this type of configuration.

letters.desc: FirstEnergy endorses milestone-based, cluster-style interconnection study reforms that let viable projects advance ahead of speculative ones, drawing on lessons from generator interconnection processes and PJM's proposed large-load track.
quotes: The Commission should consider reforms in this proceeding that allow interconnection-ready projects to timely advance through the queue, similar to PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.'s ("PJM") consideration of rules for an expedited interconnection track for the interconnection of data centers and other large loads.

By allowing projects that meet defined technical, financial, and permitting milestones to proceed ahead of other less-developed requests, transmission providers can reduce unnecessary delays and lower the queue backlog.

letters.desc: FirstEnergy argues the rule should stay tightly scoped to speed-to-power and should not layer in regional planning competition, mandatory tool mandates, or option-to-build extensions. Each addition would complicate the proceeding and slow interconnection of data center loads.
quotes: any federal rules governing the interconnection of large load customers should be narrowly tailored to achieving the Administration's speed to power mandate as quickly, affordably, and efficiently as possible.

The Commission should not require that all network upgrades that are determined to be necessary solutions to interconnecting large load customers be included as projects subject to competition in regional transmission planning processes.
there is now significant evidence that Order No. 1000 competitive transmission processes are not having the intended result in terms of either efficiency or cost-effectiveness.

AI tools at present are not sufficiently advanced to meaningfully accelerate planning and load analyses, although FirstEnergy anticipates that AI tools will eventually play an important role in interconnection studies.
the Commission should avoid regulating the study practices of transmission providers at the detailed level of dictating the use of particular tools or programs.
That principle clashes with the ANOPR's "speed to power" aims: it will introduce delays, inefficiencies, and reliability issues.

letters.desc: Fluence argues that study assumptions for BESS charging should not trigger upgrade requirements unnecessarily, and that overly conservative assumptions extend study timelines and undermine the benefits BESS provides to interconnection queues.
quotes: the Commission should ensure any final action allows storage resources to charge will not trigger the need for upgrades.

If unreasonable assumptions are applied to BESS that result in unnecessary and lengthy study processes, it will limit large loads from benefiting from the optionality that BESS can provide, which will ultimately exacerbate interconnection delays as opposed to quickening the pace of interconnection.

letters.desc: Geronimo Power supports studying large loads together with associated generation to reveal net grid impact and reduce unnecessary network upgrades, and calls for a formal, transparent process to replace the current ad hoc approach.
quotes: Geronimo Power urges the Commission to promptly move forward with a notice of proposed rulemaking and final rule in this proceeding that builds on many of the principles articulated in the ANOPR to ensure large loads may interconnect to the grid in an efficient, timely, and non-discriminatory manner that will enable the expedited development of industries that are key to America's economic competitiveness while simultaneously mitigating impacts to the grid and its existing customers.
large loads seeking to interconnect to the grid face ad hoc and opaque study processes—to the extent that a formal process exists at all.

The Commission can avoid repeating the mistakes that led to unmanageable generator interconnection queues by requiring that large loads demonstrate that their load is supported by a binding commitment of capacity sufficient to serve a significant proportion of their needs given the specified operational characteristics of the load.

letters.desc: Google supports establishing a coordinated, expedited interconnection study process that integrates large load data with generation queues, giving regional planners a complete picture of supply and demand. It proposes a firm 90-day study timeline and calls for the Commission to accelerate reforms that can be deployed quickly.
quotes: Google urges the Commission to promptly and pragmatically prioritize the reforms that can be implemented most quickly and that will incentivize digital and energy infrastructure development in a manner that maximizes use of the existing infrastructure and minimizes strain on the grid.

Large load interconnection requests remain, in many respects, a blind spot for regional transmission planners because of the differing utility-specific requirements and approaches for definitively incorporating a load into their planning forecasts.

Without a comprehensive, coordinated transmission planning process built on a more complete picture of growth in supply and demand, we will be stuck developing transmission infrastructure through piecemeal, reactive processes that are insufficient to secure our position as a global manufacturing and economic powerhouse for decades to come.

The Commission should establish nationwide rules governing interconnection arrangements involving generation resources paired with new large loads that share either the same or an electrically proximate point of interconnection.

The coordinated and expedited study of electrically proximate large loads and grid-connected generators will facilitate the development of digital infrastructure while minimizing the strain on, and maximizing the use of, existing power infrastructure.

The Commission should establish a firm timeline for these and similar interconnection studies.  Google proposes a 90-day study timeline, which is consistent with recent expedited interconnection procedures approved by the Commission.

letters.desc: Google argues that studying large loads and associated generation together, rather than in isolation, is essential to identify efficient network upgrades and reduce interconnection timelines. The current reactive, siloed approach produces piecemeal infrastructure that cannot keep pace with demand.
quotes: Inadequate electric transmission infrastructure is becoming the principal limitation to interconnecting new large loads, including data centers, and the needed generation capacity at the speed and scale necessary to sustain our global economic competitiveness.
it takes too long to interconnect new large loads and new generation, and the cost of doing so is too high. Lengthy interconnection delays are directly driving up energy prices.

the record is clear: to get large load interconnection right, the Commission must consider the interplay between transmission capacity and the interconnection of both large loads and the generators that supply them.

The way to address that foundational transmission issue is to adopt a holistic transmission planning process that optimizes grid development by accounting for both generators and the large loads planning to interconnect.

Google agrees with commenters that the Commission should establish pathways for facilitating the expedited study and interconnection of electrically proximate pairs of generation and load, as doing so will reduce the network upgrades needed to interconnect new resources, which can accelerate the pace at which new generation comes online.

letters.org: Governor Josh Shapiro and Governor Glenn Youngkin
letters.desc: The governors call for national RTO load forecast standards to address inaccuracies caused by LLAs applying across multiple territories, and for a general fix to interconnection queue delays rather than only a targeted LLA solution.
quotes: It would also similarly require that hybrid facilities be studied more efficiently.
this proposal could be even more impactful if FERC were to develop national standards and guidelines for RTO LLA forecasts.
these forecasts have failed to account for the common practice of a single LLA applying for interconnection in multiple utility service territories.

some recent load forecasts have markedly exceeded real-world constraints on load construction, such as the available supply of semiconductor chips, risking significant overbuild and associated cost increases for consumers.

we also respectfully suggest that FERC examine interconnection study processes, and whether it should be considered not just and reasonable for an interconnection request to take longer than six months, as recently requested by thirteen governors of both parties.

a more general solution to interconnection queue delays is critical to enable the important investments in manufacturing, AI, and infrastructure that are needed for the United States to compete and win.

letters.desc: GridCARE argues that current study methods rely on static, worst-case assumptions that underestimate available grid capacity. The company supports study reforms that incorporate temporal, behavioral, and operational data so that planners can distinguish short-duration constraints from structural limitations and reduce unnecessary upgrade requirements.
quotes: longstanding planning and interconnection methodologies—relying heavily on static load profiles, worst-case peak assumptions, and deterministic single-snapshot analyses—no longer reflect how the modern grid operates nor how large loads actually behave.

planners can underestimate the hosting capacity that exists across the vast majority of hours. This gap between actual operational conditions and modeling assumptions contributes to the perception that only long-lead infrastructure can serve new load, when in many cases the constraint may be limited to a small number of hours or conditions.

utilities and RTOs lack standardized or consistent formats for customer-provided data, making it challenging to assess large numbers of requests or differentiate between short-duration constraints and structural limitations.

PJM's Critical Issue Fast Path, SPP's High-Impact Large Load process, and ISO-NE's ongoing work on load characterization all demonstrate that regions are exploring ways to streamline studies, incorporate temporal and behavioral data, better align study processes with actual system operations, and improve coordination with utilities.

the Commission could encourage or require transmission providers to publish transmission level hosting capacity maps or locational headroom indicators that give large load customers signals on where interconnection is most feasible.

letters.desc: GridStor wants paired large loads and ESRs studied as coordinated loads with integrated control, arguing that independent study forces them to vie for transmission capacity and delays and raises the cost of both.
quotes: In particular, we ask that any Commission consideration of such coordinated study include the load side of paired facilities like ESRs, not only the generation side.

The present approach to studying loads independently creates a competitive dynamic between any paired ESR and large loads, forcing them to vie for transmission capacity rather than provide desired mutual benefit.
The Commission should enable studies of large loads and paired ESRs as coordinated loads, i.e., with integrated control that act as a single resource.

letters.desc: Helion advocates for modernizing interconnection study processes through automation, standardized timelines, and expedited pathways to reduce delays that currently take years. The filing states interconnection processes are too slow and cumbersome, with projects delayed years in queues, and recommends requiring AI-based automation, establishing real-time study standards, and setting progressive timeline targets as systems are deployed.
quotes: The United States is entering an era of explosive electricity demand driven by artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, and industrial reshoring. At the same time, the processes for adding new generation and transmission are too slow and cumbersome to meet the demands of America's competitive environment.

Regional operators are warning of capacity shortfalls as early as this year, with projects delayed years by interconnection queues. Developers are forced to choose where to build based not on where power is needed most, but on where approvals can be secured fastest.

That is why Helion believes it is essential to simultaneously address the ANOPR comments and to reevaluate and improve generation interconnection practices in a single rulemaking process that prioritizes an interconnection process capable of meeting the moment.
FERC has a once-in-a-generation opportunity to break the logjam that has made our own regulatory process the biggest barrier to American progress.
Expedited study pathways for resources providing baseload, dispatchable, non-fuel-limited power
Require transmission providers to deploy AI and advanced modeling tools to automate and accelerate interconnection studies for all new load and generation requests
Establish standards for real-time or near-instantaneous study results, particularly for projects with minimal transmission impact or those pairing loads with baseload, dispatchable generation
Incorporate fusion energy and any other advanced baseload, dispatchable, non-fuel limited technologies into transmission planning models and resource adequacy assessments
The interconnection challenges facing America's energy system are policy choices, not technical limitations.

letters.desc: The IL OAG calls for clear interconnection rules to address the scale of large load requests and their market effects. It supports requiring load-generation pairing as part of the study framework and making deposits and readiness requirements strong enough to filter speculative projects.
quotes: large load interconnection requests accounted for only 80 MW in 2019, but jumped to 652 MW in 2022, to 3,931 MW in 2024, and to an astonishing 8,272 MW in 2025.

Adopting clear rules on the interconnection of large loads to the transmission system is necessary to address the effect that these outsized loads have on the wholesale electricity markets and on the transmission system and to prevent practices that will lead to unjust and unreasonable cost shifts and prices.
The ANOPR should expressly include discussion of requiring large load to be matched with equivalent new generation in order to connect to the federal transmission system.

letters.desc: The IEA supports FERC's goal of improving large load interconnections and favors a cooperative federal-state approach rather than federal standardization. The filer argues that Indiana's individualized contracts under state oversight better serve all parties than a one-size-fits-all federal standard. Beyond load interconnections, FERC should focus on RTO queue reform and transmission investment, areas where states lack direct regulatory authority.
quotes: The IEA supports FERC's goal of ensuring that large new loads — including industrial, manufacturing, and data-center projects — can interconnect efficiently and reliably.

However, as noted in NARUC's November 11, 2025 resolution on this topic, the ANOPR raises important questions about jurisdictional boundaries under the Federal Power Act ("FPA"), which sets out clear delineations of federal and state regulatory authority. Moreover, states such as Indiana are demonstrating that state procedures are proactively and effectively addressing new large load customer interconnections, rendering significant FERC intrusions into state jurisdiction unnecessary and potentially duplicative.

In addition, for decades the IEA electric utilities have used individualized electric service contracts, approved by the IURC, to address electric interconnection and power supply to large, sophisticated customers. As noted above, the 2024 Indiana legislation also provides for expedited IURC approvals of such individualized contracts which can be customized to meet the unique needs of both the customers and the utilities. While the ANOPR asserts a desire to standardize large load customer interconnections, the IEA respectfully submits that unique contracts between a utility and its large load retail customers, scrutinized by state regulators, will better serve the large load customers, the utility, and the utility's other retail customers.

The IEA supports FERC's commitment to improving the interconnection process for large loads so long as it does so in a manner that preserves the jurisdictional framework established by Congress and affirmed by the courts. The IEA submits that a cooperative federal–state approach will ensure that large-load interconnections occur efficiently, reliably, and lawfully — promoting economic growth while maintaining regulatory boundaries.

Recognize that states are proactively and effectively addressing large load customer challenges, including transmission interconnections. Explicitly preserve state authority over all retail service. Ensure retail cost recovery remains under state jurisdiction. In addition, the IEA respectfully urges the FERC to continue to focus its efforts on RTO queue reform and encouraging needed transmission investment.

letters.desc: The filer wants interconnection studies to remain thorough and distinct for load customers, with deposits and readiness checks to gate participation. Hybrid facilities need independent load and generation studies. For curtailable customers, study queue priority is preferable to mandated shorter periods.
quotes: The Indicated PJM TOs agree with principle 4 of the ANOPR proposal to the extent that it requires reasonable study deposits and readiness requirements for large load interconnections. These measures will help ensure that large load customers are sufficiently invested in the load interconnection process, which will deter speculative or duplicative requests.
load and generation should be studied separately in the event the system needs to accommodate the full amount of the on-site load, or on-site generation, without the other.

Rather than mandating a shorter study period for curtailable customers, the Commission could instead consider providing a study priority for curtailable large load customers relative to other large load customers, but limited to those large load customers that make a binding and enforceable commitment to offer a meaningful level of curtailment.

letters.desc: The filer supports studying load and generation from hybrid facilities at full amounts, not on a net basis, to correctly size required upgrades and prevent reliability gaps and cost shifts.
quotes: on-site load and generation need to be studied at their full amounts to ensure reliable interconnection.

letters.desc: Supply-side constraints (delayed nuclear and gas projects) mean new generation cannot be built quickly enough. Demand reduction must be a primary strategy. Historically, demand-side efficiency kept prices stable for 20 years.
quotes: We won't be able to build our way out of this mess. Small nuclear units are still years away, gas generating equipment is not immediately available for new construction. Demand reduction must be considered at least as a partial solution.
For almost 20 years the U.S. had flat demand, which kept electricity prices affordable across most of the country.

letters.desc: Kiesling supports modernizing interconnection studies to model actual flexible operational profiles rather than peak nameplate demand. She cautions against mechanically importing the generator interconnection process to loads, as it was designed for resources that inject power and embeds outdated assumptions about load rigidity.
quotes: The rapid growth of AI data center load presents a critical coordination challenge due to the temporal mismatch between rapid data center deployment (18–24 months) and slow grid infrastructure expansion (7–10 years).

Norris et al. (2025) quantifies this potential: it finds that, with modest curtailment of just 0.25 %–0.5 % of annual uptime, U.S. balancing authorities could integrate nearly 76 GW–98 GW of new large loads using existing capacity without disruptive grid upgrades.

Applying a generator-style interconnection regime to large loads risks entrenching these problems further. The generator process is designed for resources that inject power, not for large, flexible loads whose operational behaviors differ fundamentally from generators.

letters.desc: The filer calls for pre-interconnection UFLS and transmission planning studies, clustered analysis of concentrated large loads, and minimum technical interconnection requirements for voltage support, frequency ride-through, and demand response to be codified in FAC-001 and FAC-002.
quotes: Explore the need for augmentation of the TPL-001-5.1 to require explicit modeling of large, concentrated loads in both near term and long term planning assessments even if those projects are offering to take non-firm 'flexible' electric service.

Require all regional transmission organizations, planning coordinators and transmission owners to establish minimum technical interconnection requirements for connecting large loads, similar but not identical to generator requirements (unless the new large load bringing its own generation to the process), including voltage support, frequency ride-through, and demand response capability.

letters.desc: The filer contends that probabilistic grid reliability forecasting, built on public EIA, weather, and LMP data, is accurate enough today to be incorporated into interconnection study processes.
quotes: forward-looking grid stress prediction, using publicly available data, is technically viable today and could inform interconnection study processes.

We score daily failure probability across 6 US RTOs using EIA demand, weather, and LMP congestion data. Our walk-forward validated model detects 87% of reliability events with a 13% false positive rate.

letters.desc: The filer argues that interconnection study processes focused purely on electrical infrastructure miss a layer of analysis that determines whether projects succeed in practice. Facilities that pass technical study but land in communities lacking housing, schools, or water capacity face operational failures that undermine the goals of timely and orderly interconnection.
quotes: interconnection standards that ignore community-infrastructure capacity produce outcomes that are technically efficient but operationally fragile.

A facility that secures grid access but locates in a community without adequate workforce housing, schools, healthcare, or water infrastructure will face recruitment failures, local opposition, and political risk that undermine the 'timely and orderly' interconnection the ANOPR is designed to achieve.

letters.desc: 60-day study timelines should be paired with mandatory physics-based validation to ensure speed does not compromise reliability. A hybrid approach using machine-learning for data ingestion combined with deterministic engineering models (power-flow, thermal) validates every result against physical law.
quotes: Any acceleration of interconnection or System Impact Study timelines toward the proposed 60-day target should be paired with a requirement that automated or AI-assisted study tools be validated against deterministic, physics-based engineering models, so that speed does not come at the cost of reliability.

The sound path is a hybrid, physics-constrained approach: machine-learning components accelerate data ingestion and scenario generation, while a deterministic engineering layer, such as power-flow and thermal models, validates every result against physical law before it is relied upon.
The need to integrate large loads, including AI data centers, in a timely and orderly manner is urgent, and tools to do so reliably are largely available today.

letters.desc: The filer supports FERC requiring fault-level stiff-point qualification as a condition for initiating large-load interconnection studies, modeled on arc furnace standards. This would filter the queue at entry, reducing study costs and directing development to nodes the grid can absorb. The current first-come, first-served queue rewards position over siting quality and imposes upgrade costs system-wide.
quotes: A governance framework characterized by non-disclosure agreement opacity, cost externalization onto residential ratepayers, and an interconnection queue that rewards position over siting quality is generating community and regulatory resistance that has already resulted in an estimated $100 billion in delayed or canceled investment nationally.

Extending the fault-level qualification standards that utilities applied to electric arc furnace operators beginning in the 1970s to data center interconnection, combined with node-level demand caps embedded in interconnection agreements, would implement a stiff-point siting standard that directs large digital infrastructure loads toward the transmission nodes capable of absorbing them without cascading grid stress or ratepayer cost socialization.

The interconnection queue, which nationally had grown to over two thousand gigawatts of pending requests by 2024, with PJM accounting for a substantial share of that backlog, functions on a first-come, first-served allocation mechanism that rewards queue position rather than siting quality.

The critical difference is that the electric arc furnace interconnection standard required demonstration of fault-level adequacy and installation of reactive power compensation equipment as conditions of interconnection approval. No equivalent standard currently governs data center interconnection. The result is a systematic mismatch between the locations where data center demand is concentrated and the locations where the grid can actually absorb it.

A demand cap that halts new interconnection approvals at a node once its available capacity has been committed forces the next developer to either identify a different node, fund the upgrade required to expand capacity at the chosen node, or wait until existing load is reduced. In each case, the cost of the siting decision is borne by the party making it.

FERC should initiate a rulemaking establishing fault-level adequacy as a condition of large-load interconnection eligibility, with technical specifications derived from IEEE standards long applied by utilities to large industrial load interconnections.

PJM, MISO, SPP, and other RTOs and ISOs operating under FERC jurisdiction should file tariff amendments implementing node-level demand caps for large-load interconnection. Caps should be set at the fault-level capacity available at each interconnection point, net of existing committed load.

letters.org: Industrial Energy Consumers of America et al.
letters.desc: The filers urge FERC to require transmission owners and regional grid operators to conduct transparent load forecasting and system impact studies, including mandatory evaluation of grid-enhancing technologies and reconductoring before authorizing new transmission buildout.
quotes: the Commission could – to protect existing customers and promote an efficient electric system – mandate the relevant transmission owner or regional grid operator evaluate the use of advanced reconductoring and the use of GETs, and other efficiency and optimization measures for any new large load interconnection application and related studies.

letters.org: Industrial Energy Consumers of America et al.
letters.desc: The filers call for FERC to require systematic GETs evaluation in every transmission and load study, not merely encourage it. They want a new independent FERC office to review proposed solutions, mandatory public documentation when GETs are rejected, and no rush toward a load queue. They argue near-term focus should be optimizing existing capacity rather than mandating new queues.
quotes: The time has come and gone for voluntary or incentivized consideration of GETs.

To unleash the ANOPR's speed-to-power objectives, the Commission should narrowly focus its near-term efforts on optimizing existing system capacity (or transfer capability) via reconductoring and deployment of GETs and require the transparency of load forecasting and assumptions underlying transmission system studies.

the Commission must refrain from establishing incentives for GETs, but instead require that transmission owners and transmission providers routinely and systematically evaluate GETs as a means for optimizing existing transmission facilities to accommodate new large load interconnections and other load growth.

If a traditional upgrade or new line or facility is necessary and more cost-effective than GET deployment, then documentation and analysis supporting the traditional upgrade should be provided publicly so that the parties to the interconnection process, customers, and state and federal regulators have full visibility into the decision.
GETs must be required and should no longer be voluntary or simply encouraged or incentivized.
the Commission should create a new office or staff that independently evaluates any proposed transmission solutions associated with a large load interconnection request.
Increased transparency and visibility into the impacts of large load requests is an area where the Commission should focus its efforts in developing any NOPR.

the Commission should consider implementing an optional and elective, fast lane, federal interconnection process, consistent with the framework in the initial comments of the Industrial Customer Organizations.
mandating a load interconnection queue process in the near term is not advised at this time.

letters.desc: ITI supports studying generation and load together to reduce transmission and distribution upgrades, including cluster study processes. Studies should comprehensively model colocation, curtailment, and other arrangements that reduce upgrade costs and speed energization timelines.
quotes: ITI supports the principle that load and generation should be studied together. We would like to clarify that this should not be limited to colocation arrangements. If new generating facilities are located at or near new load facilities, then they would both require less transmission and distribution upgrades than if they were studied separately.

Interconnection studies should comprehensively model large load customers' generation colocation arrangements, curtailment abilities, or arrangements with other parties that would result in fewer upgrades. Fewer system upgrades resulting from interconnection studies lead to faster energization timelines for large loads requesting interconnection.
FERC should also consider introducing a cluster study process for large loads, similar to the cluster study process in Order 2023 for generation.

letters.desc: iMasons argues that the current fragmented, state-by-utility process produces opaque rules, inaccurate load forecasts, and inefficient infrastructure investment. The final rule should set minimum national standards with consistent technical requirements developed in coordination with NERC.
quotes: The United States' current large load interconnection landscape consists of a disjointed, state-by-state, and in some instances, utility-by-utility, set of rules and processes that are often opaque and routinely in flux.

maintaining the status quo with respect to large load interconnections will prevent the United States from building out data centers at the pace and scale needed to win the AI race and stay competitive globally, which will undermine the country's short and long-term economic, national security and scientific interests.

the lack of coordination with regard to large load interconnection processes leads to inaccurate load forecasts, resulting in, among other things, the inefficient buildout of generation and transmission to serve load.

interconnecting utilities should be required to provide large load developers with: 1) sufficient information regarding anticipated state-jurisdictional and FERC-jurisdictional costs that they will be expected to bear, including a clear understanding of how FERC-jurisdictional costs are expected to be reflected in retail rates; and 2) drafts of all relevant agreements that they will need to execute to interconnect their projects.

iMasons urges the Commission to work with NERC and transmission providers to expedite the development of clear and consistent technical standards that will govern the interconnection of large loads nationally.

letters.desc: IFP backs the ANOPR's call for a dedicated, standardized interconnection study framework for large loads. Standardization is needed to give transmission providers accurate demand forecasts and concentrate study resources on viable projects.
quotes: IFP strongly supports the Principles identified in the Commission's ANOPR.

the ANOPR's principles directed at accelerating and standardizing large load interconnection are needed to maintain United States leadership in both AI research and development as well as AI deployment.

Principle 4, which calls for standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties, is a necessary means of filtering out speculative projects, providing transmission providers with more useful information to more accurately forecast demand on their systems.

letters.desc: IECA backs simultaneous network impact studies for co-located load and generation to reduce upgrade costs and enable expedited approval.
quotes: We fully support the proposal in the ANOPR of simultaneously studying the impacts on the network of one or more large loads (i.e., Data Centers) and one or more associated electric generating facilities as offsetting loads and resources and therefore worthy of expedited consideration and approval as a reasonable approach to addressing the interconnection of Data Centers that co-locate with existing or new electric generation facilities.

letters.desc: IECA backs simultaneous impact studies for co-located loads and generation, provided grid impacts are addressed. It also supports assigning all study costs to the large load developer.
quotes: we also support having the costs of interconnections of large loads, including the costs of all necessary system impact studies, be borne by the developers and customers of such large loads, which should place the risk of stranded investment on those in the best position to manage such risk, i.e., the developers of such large loads.

We support the simultaneous study of system impacts from a Co-Located Load with its Co-Located Generation and the expeditious approval of the interconnection of both at a single point of interconnection or at two or more "proximate" points of interconnection, provided that the impacts on the transmission grid and other users of that transmission grid are addressed as set forth in Section III.B. of these Reply Comments.

letters.org: Invenergy Wind Development North America LLCInvenergy Solar Development North America LLCInvenergy Thermal Development Holdings LLC ,
letters.desc: Invenergy backs a joint study process because separate queues and TO-only footprint analysis miss cheaper regional transmission solutions and generate avoidable upgrade costs. A single queue increases transparency for all developers and limits opportunities for undue discrimination.
quotes: transmission owners across the country have adopted a hodge-podge of load interconnection procedures that often impose significant regulatory and financial burdens that threaten to stymie data center deployment and which to date have not served as an effective mechanism for screening non-speculative interconnection requests, reducing ratepayer costs, or increasing speed to power.
Load and hybrid interconnection requests should be studied in the existing generator interconnection queue(s) with generator interconnection requests and not in a separate large load queue.
studying load and generation separately can, and often does, result in the identification of network upgrades that would not be needed had the facilities been studied together.

load interconnections, unlike generator interconnection requests, are studied exclusively by each transmission owner and typically only include transmission solutions in that particular transmission owner's footprint, the study process often overlooks potentially less-expensive transmission solutions that would have been identified by looking at the system more holistically

letters.desc: The ANOPR should move forward to establish nationwide process standardization and certainty for large load interconnection, incorporating lessons from accelerated processes like MISO ERAS and enabling cluster studies across RTOs.
quotes: Iron Mountain largely supports the Commission expeditiously moving the Secretary's proposed ANOPR forward to a NOPR and eventually a FERC order.
Iron Mountain supports the proposed ANOPR because it would provide nationwide process standardization and certainty with the potential for speed to power.

When reviewing the Secretary's proposal, the Commission should take lessons learned from MISO and SPP to expedite generator interconnections, allow cluster studies and study transmission projects across Regional Transmission Organizations (RTOs).

MISO's recently approved Expedited Resource Addition Study (ERAS) process provides a targeted solution to get needed generation resources interconnected and online to meet the same load challenges as justification for the proposed ANOPR.

letters.desc: ISO-NE notes that New England already includes RNS requests in cluster studies. It recommends that cost responsibility for cluster upgrades be confined to the same cluster to prevent cascading restudies of completed cluster studies. Phased projects should be studied at their full aggregate load.
quotes: rules for interconnection of large loads should address interconnection of projects in stages.  For example, consider a large load customer's proposal to interconnect 30 MW in two stages of 15 MW each.  ISO-NE submits that the aggregate total of 30 MW should be captured in the supporting interconnection study to fully evaluate the system impacts of the total amount of load

The principle should also establish that upgrades identified in the Cluster Studies (and the corresponding cost responsibility for such upgrades) will be limited to the requests for projects that were part of the same Cluster that included the load and/or hybrid facility.   Without this limitation, there could be a potential increase of restudies of previously completed Cluster Studies.

letters.desc: ITC emphasizes that proactive long-term transmission planning through MISO's Long-Range Transmission Planning portfolios, paired with grid investments and local transmission owner knowledge, enables efficient large load interconnection. The filer argues this forward-looking approach delivers better outcomes than quick or narrowly focused solutions.
quotes: ITC supports the Commission's efforts to evaluate and identify potential reforms to ensure large loads can interconnect quickly and reliably while avoiding cost shifts to existing customers.

current regulatory frameworks, including large loads' obligations to pay for the ongoing development, maintenance, and operation of the overall transmission system through network transmission service charges, accomplish these goals when paired with proactive transmission planning, the knowledge of local Transmission Owners, and other policies that promote optimal long-term solutions over quick or narrowly focused fixes.

ITC Midwest's forward-looking, proactive approach to grid development, reinforced through MISO's Long-Range Transmission Planning ("LRTP") portfolios, has enabled faster large-load interconnections by providing available regional capacity and reducing the scope and cost of network upgrades, benefiting both new customers and existing ratepayers.

A key factor in accommodating the data center growth in Iowa was ITC Midwest's ability to start developing the LRTP projects right after MISO Board approval due to the segments not being eligible for Order No. 1000 competition. If the projects had been subject to the solicitation process, it would have added almost two years of delay before determining who was responsible for construction, irreparably undermining the in-service timeline requirements.

we believe the enormous new loads already in the pipeline are just the beginning. As LRTP projects come online, we are optimistic Iowa will be positioned to accommodate additional data center investment and other future load growth, improving reliability and increasing rate benefits for customers over time.

letters.desc: The KCC favors RTO-level stakeholder processes to develop targeted tariff reforms rather than top-down FERC rulemaking. It argues regional stakeholders are best placed to craft narrow wholesale reforms that respect jurisdictional boundaries while addressing the underlying problems.
quotes: the focus on cost allocation within interconnection studies is misplaced. The larger issue is the cost increases and potential cost shifts associated with regional transmission expansion plans, which states do not have authority to fully address.
stakeholders at the RTO level are best positioned to address this issue by crafting the narrow reforms referred to in Section II.A.1 and presenting those reforms to FERC

regional stakeholders are best positioned to develop reforms that meet the dual objectives of respecting jurisdictional boundaries and effectively addressing the underlying issues that are at the heart of this inquiry

letters.desc: The Alliance urges FERC to base transmission planning on accurate, non-inflated load forecasts from large energy users and to route projects away from conserved and high-value agricultural lands. It also endorses re-conductoring as a near-term capacity tool that avoids new land disturbance.
quotes: FERC should seek to identify and advance transmission projects that avoid conserved lands and yet-to-be-conserved lands of high conservation or agricultural value.
The Alliance encourages FERC to support the re-conductoring of existing transmission lines with higher-performance wires, which can rapidly increase transmission capacity at a low cost.
Without data on the actual energy usage of large energy users like data centers, grid planners can't determine what level of grid expansion is needed and where.

forecasts of electricity demand stemming from data center growth are beset with uncertainty — the extent and pace of data center demand growth remain highly uncertain, and the specific locations even more difficult to predict.

letters.desc: LPPC advocates for a Commission-convened forum with state and industry stakeholders to develop a voluntary, consensus-based approach to large load interconnection, beginning with a technical conference. The framework would use ANOPR reform principles as a starting point and could be adopted voluntarily across states, with FERC retaining discretion to mandate action later if progress stalls.
quotes: LPPC expressed support for the objective articulated by the Department of Energy ("DOE") of a consistent, nationwide approach to large load interconnection. However, LPPC asked that this be accomplished while respecting the role reserved under the Federal Power Act ("FPA") to state authorities over retail service, of which large load is an increasing component.

LPPC here renews the request outlined in its initial comments that the Commission convene a forum to develop a consensus-based approach to large load interconnection that may be adopted voluntarily across the nation.

NARUC "pledges to engage with regulated entities and with other stakeholders to explore consensus solutions for FERC's consideration that will help meet national goals, while avoiding disputes over jurisdiction that would impede achieving our shared goals."

Rather than unilaterally imposing federal jurisdiction on these interconnections, FERC should pursue a cooperative approach – potentially developing voluntary best practices with states and other novel approaches to meet the moment – without undermining state authority or established statutory frameworks.

That forum, overseen by FERC, should include NARUC and representatives from the investor-owned utility, public power and cooperative communities. LPPC would commit to participate in such a forum and supports the suggestion it understands NARUC will make in reply comments in this docket that this discussion begin with a Commission-sponsored technical conference.

As to the substance of an interconnection framework, LPPC envisions that the Principles of Reform outlined in the ANOPR would serve as a starting point for relevant discussions. Assuming consensus can be achieved, the framework may be articulated in a policy statement or simply in an order closing this proceeding.

Following some period of time for voluntary adoption of the framework, FERC may reserve the option of taking further action if it determines that progress in interconnecting large loads has unreasonably stalled.

letters.desc: LPPC supports improving the speed, efficiency, fairness, and predictability of large load interconnections and aligns itself with the goal of integrating new demand responsibly.
quotes: We share the Administration's commitment to energy dominance and specifically support improving the speed, efficiency, fairness, and predictability of large load interconnections.

letters.desc: LIPA supports comprehensive large load interconnection studies that screen for oscillatory behaviors, assess system impacts of load tripping, and evaluate closed-loop control instability. Studies must be tailored to location-specific grid conditions.
quotes: Require the large load interconnection study process to screen for, and assess, the potential for adverse oscillatory behaviors that may require physical (i.e., equipment upgrades) or operational measures to avoid, minimize and mitigate potentially adverse impacts upon the grid; and Allow interconnecting transmission owners to adopt general and locationally specific protection measures and equipment standards necessary to limit adverse oscillatory behavior from large loads and co-located loads.

If a large load facility is susceptible to rapid disconnection or load change in response to a system disturbance, then the large load interconnection study process should assess the potential system impact resulting from such abrupt changes; and As part of the planning, design and construction of interconnection facilities for large loads, transmission owners should have the right to require load to implement and maintain disturbance ride through capability that is necessary to ensure system stability and security.

The large load interconnection study process should assess the potential system impacts resulting from closed loop instability in the system and identify avoidance, minimization and mitigation measures that would reduce the risks of significant adverse impacts to the grid. Transmission owners should have the flexibility to identify locationally specific load facility oscillatory dampening characteristics that are necessary for system security and included in the development of the large load's interconnection facilities.

letters.desc: Longroad supports the ANOPR's study reforms but argues they are insufficient unless generation, transmission, and load are studied together under the same modeling assumptions. The current siloed, static base-case approach produces piecemeal transmission and NRIS queue gridlock. An option for large load to build stand-alone facilities is also part of the study-process fix.
quotes: Simply creating a standalone large load interconnection process for public utility transmission providers to implement alongside the current uncoordinated generation queue and transmission planning processes will not provide the required speed and cost efficiencies.

Longroad is concerned that merely grafting on a separate load interconnection process that is addressed in isolation will only exacerbate the inefficiencies that currently exist in the siloed generation and transmission planning processes.

Currently, different models and assumptions within and outside of regional transmission organizations ("RTOs") are used for generation and transmission planning. This fractionated nature and use of different modeling assumptions are causing, in some instances, transmission overbuild or piecemeal transmission that is not efficiently optimized.

NRIS studies have become impossible to solve, rendering them meaningless in some planning regions because many projects with interconnection agreements do not have a viable development path (offtake) and yet are still consuming NRIS capacity.

Open Access 2.0 would take the nation to the next level where transmission planning, generator interconnection and large load interconnection are modeled the same and in a coordinated, cohesive fashion.
The base case should be updated for all known and confirmed load, which will minimize piecemeal build -- at least until Open Access 2.0 principles are adopted.

National security interests cannot be held hostage to public utility transmission provider delays. If large load can build the "stand-alone" connection facilities faster and at a lower cost than the interconnecting utility, the national security need and fairness to the consumer dictate that it must be allowed.

letters.desc: LS Power consistently argues that large-load interconnection should be integrated into existing Order No. 1000/1920 regional planning and generation interconnection study processes, not handled through separate ad hoc mechanisms. This ensures consistent modeling, coordinated protection, and NERC compliance.
quotes: The Commission should integrate new large loads into the Commission-jurisdictional transmission grid through revisions to existing regional transmission planning and transmission interconnection frameworks rather than establishing additional ad hoc, piecemeal processes solely for large-load interconnections.

The Commission should require that hybrid facility (large load and associated matching generation) interconnections with the interstate transmission grid be studied together where they are anticipated to interconnect electrically close to each other.
The existing generation interconnection frameworks should be used and improved upon to establish standardized pro-forma terms for large load interconnections.
To introduce resource adequacy as a consideration in determining whether and at what cost to interconnect new large load would necessarily discriminate against that new load and existing generators.

Large-load interconnection should be integrated into existing planning and study processes for generation interconnection. Large-load integration should be handled within the same coordinated regional planning and study framework used for generation and reliability.

letters.org: Maine Office of the Public Advocate
letters.desc: Maine OPA supports the Secretary's proposal for timely and orderly interconnection reforms and urges that the large load process parallel the generator interconnection timeline to avoid accelerated deployment.
quotes: the Maine OPA supports the Secretary of Energy's proposal to implement reforms to ensure the timely and orderly interconnection of large loads to the interstate transmission system.
any interconnection process adopted by the Commission for large loads should parallel the process applied to interconnecting generators.

letters.desc: The Maryland PSC supports cost-causation-based assignment of all reliability impacts through interconnection studies, and recommends that LSEs be required to demonstrate matched new supply before large load additions are approved.
quotes: The Maryland PSC supports the principle of cost allocation on the basis of cost causation, and would emphasize that the total impact to grid reliability caused by a new large load or hybrid facility should be fully represented in the costs that they are assigned through interconnection studies.

a path forward could be accomplished by requiring LSEs to identify the amount of large load additions they intend to supply, and to be held accountable for accommodating these additions in a manner that retains reliability and affordability for other customers. The LSE would need to demonstrate to the RTO/ISO and state regulators sufficient amounts of new generation or new demand response related to the amounts of new large loads to be served.

letters.desc: Maven Solutions supports requiring a public benefit study before any direct cost assignment, covering congestion relief, reliability improvement, transfer capability, generation deliverability, and avoided-cost benefits. The filing also ties this to NERC reliability conditions: computational-load modeling and dynamic-load simulations must be satisfied before a customer receives transmission service under any expansion rate.
quotes: A transmission facility built to interconnect a data center may simultaneously improve regional reliability, reduce congestion, increase transfer capability, support future load service, and enable generation deliverability for parties who had no part in the interconnection request.
"Triggered by a data center" is not the same as "benefits only a data center." FirstEnergy wants the causation label without doing the beneficiary math.
A rate-design framework that assigns capital costs without addressing dynamic-load performance creates a dangerous half-solution.

The Commission should not adopt any cost-allocation framework for large computational loads without requiring the applicant to satisfy NERC's emerging reliability obligations as a condition of receiving transmission service.

letters.desc: The filer argues that connection queue backlogs and structural weaknesses in existing regimes require a coherent, multi-part policy response rather than isolated fixes. Reforms to queue management, cost allocation, flexibility, and socio-environmental screening should be designed together.
quotes: Long connection queues, disputes over reinforcement cost allocation, and the growing political sensitivity of new large-load projects have exposed structural weaknesses in existing connection regimes.

Speculative requests for connections are either not backed by a finalised project but serve as a way to hold a place in queue as the project is developed, or an existing project that applies for connections in multiple locations with the intent of building in only the one that gives them the lowest cost.

our key recommendation is that reforms should be designed as a coherent package: queue management, cost allocation, flexibility incentives and socio-environmental screening work best cohesively, rather than introduced separately.
the rapid growth of data centre demand is not inherently incompatible with grid reliability, affordability or net-zero objectives, but it does require a deliberate and integrated policy response.

letters.desc: Meta supports adoption of guidance and best practices rather than detailed binding rules for large load interconnection. The company argues that guidance encourages uniformity while allowing private-sector innovation and accommodation of varying regional circumstances. Imposing one-size-fits-all rules risks slowing successful interconnection processes.
quotes: the Commission should consider adopting guidance, best practices, and, if appropriate, minimum standards for large load interconnection rather than promulgating a binding, detailed rule

Adopting guidance would encourage uniformity in industry practices while allowing for continued private-sector innovation and accommodating the varying stages of data center deployment across the country
Data center developers and other sources of large load need faster, transparent, and more predictable interconnection processes

The Commission should therefore consider developing minimum standards for the interconnection of large loads and encouraging greater uniformity in the processes that utilities, grid operators, and regulators use to bring data centers online

The Commission, however, should not rush to impose a one-size-fits-all regulatory solution nationwide. Some regions of the country are just beginning to bring data centers online, while others have already interconnected substantial large data center loads and are working quickly to add more. Keeping this momentum going is imperative. Issuing a detailed, standard rule that fails to account for the diversity in the economic landscape could slow down successful interconnection processes

Meta also agrees with the ANOPR's recommendation in paragraph 20 that large load be studied together with generating facilities such as by studying 'the composite behavior of co-located load and generation' so long as joint study processes do not delay the interconnection of large loads
the Commission should call on utilities and grid operators to promptly develop streamlined study processes to study large load and incremental generation simultaneously and on an expedited basis

letters.desc: Microsoft wants standardized, transparent study processes that remove uncertainty and reduce network-upgrade cost and scope. It also notes study reform could make system-level load forecasting more consistent for planners.
quotes: Microsoft believes studying load and generation together has the potential to speed up the interconnection process for load and generation by eliminating duplicative, and potentially conflicting, studies and will facilitate more efficient grid planning by more closely aligning generation capacity needs with large loads.

In Microsoft’s view, the changes ripe for consideration are those that (i) focus on processes that will increase speed-to-market for new customers and new generation and (ii) reduce the cost and scope of network upgrades needed for interconnection.
Microsoft supports standardizing study requirements to provide greater regulatory certainty, deter speculation, and enhance transparency so businesses can plan with more predictability.
Interconnection processes should clearly articulate study requirements, financial commitments, timelines, and responsibilities of the utility and the customer.
An additional benefit of interconnection study reform is that it could bring greater consistency to system-level load forecasting for system planners.

letters.desc: Rather than a binding generic rule, the filer suggests the Commission issue a policy statement to guide regional innovation. Time spent on rulemaking compliance is time not spent on actual load integration.
quotes: Time spent participating in and complying with any such rulemaking is time not spent on supporting load growth in the region.  Another alternative to taking generic action is to issue a policy statement to guide the industry regarding large load interconnections.

letters.desc: The filer supports accelerating large load integration through existing and new MISO processes, including EPR, ERAS, and JTIQ. They report concrete results: 10.7 GW approved and 9.7 GW under review through EPR in 2026 alone. They want the Commission to support these regional efforts rather than impose uniform federal rules.
quotes: the MISO Transmission Owners strongly support the ANOPR's goals of interconnecting large loads in a timely and reliable manner that avoids unfair cost shifts.

the MISO Transmission Owners welcome any and all support from the Commission that avoids a "one-size-fits-all" approach and provides flexibility and encourages Federal Power Act section 205 filings to craft innovative solutions that optimize regional differences in achieving timely, reliable, and affordable speed to power.

the EPR process is an open, transparent, and streamlined process that permits MISO to review and approve transmission projects proposed by transmission owners faster than the regular MTEP cycle, which can take years to review and approve transmission upgrades.
So far in 2026, MISO has approved EPR projects supporting 10.7 GW of new load additions and currently an additional 9.7 GW are under review.

the MISO Transmission Owners are active participants in several MISO stakeholder initiatives specifically designed to improve speed to power for large loads while ensuring reliability, including consideration of a new Zero-Injection Generator Interconnection Agreement ("ZGIA") and new reliability requirements regarding large loads.

letters.desc: Missouri PSC urges FERC to incorporate the MISO and SPP large load interconnection frameworks, which were developed through stakeholder engagement, into its final rule. Standardized study procedures and a defined queue would reduce regulatory burden while protecting reliability.
quotes: FERC's final rule should draw from existing RTO approaches. Both MISO and SPP developed their large load interconnection provisions through stakeholder engagement, and thus they provide examples of effective approaches that FERC should incorporate into its final rule.

Standardized study procedures and a defined interconnection queue could reduce regulatory burden and uncertainty for large load customers, protect the safety and reliability of the transmission system, uphold cost causation principles, protect customers from stranded costs, and mitigate the risks of speculative projects that complicate state-level load forecasting and resource planning.

The ANOPR does not explain whether, or how, current state and RTO interconnection practices are discriminatory or unjust or unreasonable. Unlike generation, load represents an opportunity for a utility to increase revenue, not competition.

letters.desc: The Monitor argues that interconnection studies must confirm both transmission and capacity adequacy before any large load is allowed to connect. PJM already has this authority under existing rules, and FERC should confirm it and direct PJM to create a load queue that holds requests until they can be served reliably.
quotes: PJM is currently proposing to allow the interconnection of large new data center loads that it cannot serve reliably and that will require load curtailments (black outs) of the data centers or of other customers at times.

The Market Monitor requests that the Commission rule that PJM has the authority to add large new data center loads only when they can be served reliably as defined both by transmission and capacity adequacy.
The Market Monitor believes that under current rules, PJM does have the authority to require that the loads can be served reliably before allowing the loads to be added to the system.
PJM has the authority to create a load queue.

more explicit rules are plainly needed in order to remove confusion and to provide PJM the tools to protect resource adequacy and to ensure just and reasonable capacity prices and to ensure that there is a clear path to provide for the reliable interconnection of large new data center loads.

letters.desc: The Market Monitor contends that any load interconnection study process must assess generation adequacy, not just transmission access. Interconnection without a corresponding capacity check cannot produce reliable service.
quotes: Commenters with specific proposals generally seek to avoid the only just, reasonable and not unduly discriminatory action available to the Commission that will protect reliability and affordability for existing customers which is to provide clear incentives to large new data center loads to get to market quickly and reliably and to refuse to permit reliability to be undermined by adding large new data center loads without corresponding new generation.

The ANOPR does not propose to include a requirement in the interconnection procedures for large loads, that interconnection of large loads to the grid must be predicated on the ability to provide reliable service which in turn requires generation capacity which in turn means that there should be a load queue. The NOPR should include such a requirement.

The best incentive to bring only real projects is to provide an expedited option to bring your own new generation. This incentive would be much stronger and more effective and more focused on a real solution than requiring deposits.
In their current and proposed forms, demand side solutions offer no viable substitution for generation capacity resources.

letters.org: National Association of State Utility Consumer Advocates
letters.desc: Consumer advocates support interconnection study processes that allow efficient siting of loads and generating facilities to minimize costly network upgrades.
quotes: strong readiness and financial requirements to deter speculative large-load interconnection requests that can distort transmission planning and increase costs for consumers

letters.desc: National Grid supports a uniform federal framework as a baseline for large load interconnection studies but requires regional flexibility to adapt timelines and procedures. Using generator interconnection rules as a starting point is acceptable so long as the differences between load and generation customers are recognized.
quotes: National Grid strongly supports the statement of the Secretary that "large loads, including AI data centers, served by public utilities must be able to connect to the transmission system in a timely, orderly, and non-discriminatory manner."

Allowing large load interconnection customers the option to construct their own network upgrades introduces risks that could jeopardize overall system reliability.  National Grid believes that maintaining transmission owner control over these upgrades is essential to ensure consistency, safety, and long-term system integrity.

Rather than subjecting these projects to full cluster study timelines, the Commission could explore exemptions or streamlined processes for hybrid facilities where generation is primarily intended to serve the associated load.

The NYISO already has procedures in place to study large loads interconnecting to the transmission system.  Allowing the NYISO and other regions to leverage these existing processes will help avoid unnecessary delays and support innovation.

letters.org: Natural Resource Defense CouncilSustainable FERC ProjectClean Air Task Force ,Coalition for Affordable Utility Services and Energy Efficie ,EARTHJUSTICE ,ENVIRONMENTAL DEFENSE FUND ,MONTANA ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION CENTER ,Sierra Club ,Southern Environmental Law Center ,
letters.desc: Interconnection studies must be thorough enough to identify upgrade beneficiaries and support accurate cost allocation. The filers also call for proactive, system-wide planning over reactive project-by-project responses, and warn that fast-track processes must not degrade the existing generator interconnection queue.
quotes: in the long term, building out the system in response to discrete, emergent needs rather than through proactive, forward-looking, system-wide planning fails to identify the most cost-effective infrastructure investments, which would solve the reliability issues associated with new large loads and provide broader system benefits.

FERC should emphasize accelerating interconnection processes generally over adopting separate fast-tracks, and must at least implement safeguards to prevent fast-tracks from causing harm to the existing generator interconnection process.

FERC must ensure that load interconnection studies are sufficiently rigorous and transparent to identify the beneficiaries of network upgrades and enable cost-allocation that is roughly commensurate with the benefits.

letters.desc: NMPRC supports FERC's efforts to create transparent, standardized, and efficient interconnection procedures for large loads and hybrid facilities.
quotes: The NMPRC supports the Commission's efforts to provide transparent, standardized, and efficient interconnection procedures for large loads and hybrid facilities on the transmission system.

letters.org: New York State Public Service Commission
letters.desc: The NYSPSC argues that NERC's own findings about the speed and scale of data center connections call for deliberate analysis of reliability impacts, not an expedited rulemaking that treats rapid interconnection as inherently desirable.
quotes: This information does not suggest that an urgent need exists for the Commission to facilitate additional interconnections to the transmission system.  In fact, it suggests the opposite – a need to ensure that the current "rapid" pace of interconnections is carefully analyzed to ensure large loads do not adversely impact reliability or the electric system at large.

letters.org: New York State Reliability Council, L.L.C.
letters.desc: Comprehensive studies of reliability and resilience impacts must be conducted in advance of interconnection and incorporated into facility design. Current five-year UFLS review cycles are inadequate for the pace and magnitude of large load additions.
quotes: Potential adverse impacts to reliability and resilience must be examined in advance (not reactively) and be addressed through the design of the interconnection facility.
Given the magnitude of the proposed loads, these studies should be conducted in advance of interconnection to assure the functionality of automatic underfrequency load shedding programs.

The NYSRC is in support of the Commission's inquiry into necessary reforms to effectuate the interconnection of large loads. Accordingly, the NYSRC submits that automatic UFLS programs must be considered in the design of large load facilities interconnecting to the transmission system from a preemptive or proactive planning perspective.

letters.org: New York Transmission OwnersCentral Hudson Gas & Electric CorporationNew York Power Authority ,New York State Electric & Gas Corp. and Rochester Gas and El ,Niagara Mohawk d/b/a/ National Grid ,Consolidated Edison Company of New York, Inc. and Orange and ,Long Island Power Authority ,
letters.desc: The NYTOs support building any federal framework on NYISO's existing Commission-approved reliability planning processes rather than creating a new federal structure. Reliability must remain the foundation of every study decision, and NERC, regional, and local reliability structures should remain core to any federally directed process.
quotes: building on NYISO's existing Commission-approved reliability planning processes that coordinate these comprehensive mechanisms—rather than creating an entirely new structure for transmission-level load—will promote continuity and make use of experience already gained.
Reliability is the foundation of every planning and interconnection decision and must remain the top priority.
Large-load requests should not be forced into generator cluster studies unless regional circumstances support doing so.

letters.desc: NERC supports studying large load impacts on the BPS and is already conducting that work through the Large Loads Action Plan, white papers, a Level 2 Alert, and a draft Reliability Guideline. NERC expects to deliver findings and next steps to FERC by Q1 2026, including analysis of whether registry criteria or Reliability Standards revisions are warranted.
quotes: Such unique challenges include demand forecasting and planning for system behavior when some large loads, such as data centers for cryptocurrency mining and artificial intelligence, are substantially larger and constructed more quickly than prior large loads using the BPS.

NERC plans to coordinate with stakeholders over the following year to explore potential revisions to the registry criteria and Reliability Standards that would incorporate large loads impacting the reliable operation of the BPS.

the Large Loads Action Plan includes an action item on registration analysis, which analyzes the legal basis for registration of large users of the BPS and whether there are Reliability Standards requirements that could apply to such users.
In the first quarter of 2026, NERC will develop additional findings, guidance, and next steps to account for the BPS reliability needs associated with large loads.
By February 27, 2026, NERC will submit a report to the Commission regarding responses to the Level 2 Alert.
