letters.desc: NERC is accelerating development of registry criteria and Reliability Standards specifically for large loads, targeting completion by December 31, 2026. These updates will provide clarity on which entities must comply and what actions they must take.
quotes: Under the accelerated large load action plan, NERC intends to file revised registry criteria and Reliability Standards on or before December 31, 2026.
NERC concluded that it would accelerate the large load action plan and initiate efforts to update its registry criteria and develop initial Reliability Standards to include large loads.

These updates would provide certainty on which parties should be subject to NERC requirements (per updated registry criteria) and what those parties should be required to do (per updated Reliability Standards).

letters.desc: NCUC demonstrates that North Carolina has strong, transparent state regulatory processes already effectively managing large-load integration. The state has implemented semiannual large-load reporting requirements, cluster-based interconnection studies (predating federal Order 2023), and multi-layered review through CPIRP and rate-case proceedings. NCUC's framework provides oversight exceeding RTO transparency and accountability requirements.
quotes: North Carolina maintains a robust structure of oversight and public participation that, in several key respects, exceeds the transparency and accountability requirements found in regional transmission organizations (RTOs)

the NCUC allowed Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC and Duke Energy Progress, LLC (together, Duke) to re-file and adjust their planning assumptions when updated economic-development forecasts, including data centers, materially changed the projected load forecast
the final order issued by the NCUC on November 1, 2024 required Duke to file semiannual large-load reports to monitor new economic-development activity and large customer additions
North Carolina's regulatory framework is already actively, effectively, and efficiently managing large-load integration in a transparent, least-cost, and reliability-focused manner

letters.desc: NREMC supports studying large loads and hybrid facilities jointly with new generating facilities to reduce the need for costly network upgrades. Implementation must align with existing procedures and avoid duplicative studies that could delay or undermine the intended efficiencies.
quotes: NREMC agrees that, to the extent practicable, studying load and hybrid facilities together with new generating facilities can support more efficient siting decisions and reduce the need for costly network upgrades. Co-locating a large load front-of-meter with newly developed generation, not generation pulled from the existing supply stack, can meaningfully reduce the overall interconnection footprint and limit the transmission reinforcements that would otherwise be required if each facility were studied independently.

Any proposed changes will need to be aligned with existing generator-interconnection procedures, transmission-service request processes, and ongoing regional transmission-planning activities. Absent a clear transition framework, transmission providers and customers could face conflicting requirements, duplicative studies, or delays that undermine the very efficiencies these reforms are intended to achieve.

letters.desc: NRG argues that simply shifting dysfunctional state queues to FERC jurisdiction solves nothing. It proposes the Commission mandate open seasons modeled on gas pipeline practice, allocating interconnection capacity by NPV rather than request timing. This would clear speculative projects and bring the most megawatts online at the lowest overall cost.
quotes: NRG strongly supports the principles set forth in the ANOPR but proposes several discrete modifications to ensure that the final rule successfully implements those principles.

the ANOPR will not have fulfilled its goals and risen to this critical moment if it merely transfers jurisdiction over dysfunctional load queues from state commissions to FERC or drags large loads into the dysfunction of the generator interconnection queues.

A far better approach would be an open season or an auction mechanism that allocates capacity in a manner that maximizes the net present value ("NPV") of bids as understood through an efficient combination of relevant variables (e.g., least cost, amount of incremental demand capable of being served, and speed to market).

the Commission should mandate the use of open seasons to allocate load interconnection capacity.  FERC-regulated interstate natural gas pipelines have long employed "open seasons to gauge demand for prospective expansion capacity . . . ."

letters.org: Office of the Ohio Consumers' Counsel
letters.desc: OCC opposes purely serial interconnection studies, which fragment planning and overlook cumulative impacts. A coordinated or clustered study framework should evaluate all large-load and hybrid requests together, and all facilities including local ones must be subject to Commission review.
quotes: speculative filings- particularly by unconfirmed data center and industrial developers- have contributed to inaccurate demand forecasts and queue congestion, which can lead to unnecessary or premature network upgrades later recovered from consumers.

Large load interconnections to any interstate transmission facility, no matter how local in nature from a planning perspective, should not escape Commission review under the ANOPR and any proposed or final rules on this matter.

the RTO or regional planning authority should perform a forward-looking resource adequacy assessment- spanning at least three years – to determine whether the suspension would erode reserve margins or necessitate additional capacity procurement.

letters.desc: Study deposits and milestones improve utility load forecasting and planning by preventing misallocation of resources and overinvestment, freeing limited utility resources for truly shovel-ready projects.
quotes: This frees up limited utility resources to be spent on projects that are truly shovel-ready. It also informs critical utility load forecasting and planning processes, helping to prevent misallocation of resources or overinvestment in the system.

letters.desc: ANOPR principles for large load integration, if implemented, enable efficient grid development. Study processes must capture co-location benefits and avoid worst-case assumptions when hybrid facilities operate reliably.
quotes: The principles articulated in the ANOPR, if implemented thoughtfully, will facilitate efficient grid development and support innovative models like Oklo's.
hybrid facilities should be studied based on the amount of injection and/or withdrawal rights requested. This focus on net impact, rather than gross characteristics, is critical.
Methodologies should not default to 'worst-case' assumptions (e.g., assuming co-located generation is offline during peak load) if the facility is not configured to operate that way.

letters.desc: ODEC urges FERC to mandate that large loads meet NERC reliability standards and be registered with NERC, and that NERC update its reliability standards to address operational complexities large loads create. ODEC also supports requiring must-run studies when existing generators are partially suspended to serve co-located large loads.
quotes: the Commission should use this proceeding to provide clarity and a set of policies or principles that must be adopted by transmission providers, with flexibility for regional differences.

ODEC reiterates its agreement with ANOPR Principle 14 and urges the Commission to adopt a requirement in the Final Rule that utilities serving large loads must meet all applicable NERC reliability standards and OATT provisions, as well as require large loads to be registered with NERC and require NERC to enhance its existing registry criteria and Reliability Standards and create new Standards as required to address the operational complexities that large loads introduce to the grid.

ODEC supports the ANOPR proposal in Principle 10, to require a system support resource/reliability must run type study for partial suspension of existing generators to serve new loads at the same location.

letters.desc: ON supports codifying NERC Level 3 Alert recommendations and NOGRR 282 into uniform, enforceable national rules. The company argues this approach prevents regional fragmentation and ensures consistent technical requirements across all RTOs and ISOs.
quotes: ON strongly supports the effort by the Commission to consider potential reforms to large load interconnection.
Often overlooked are the power quality and system stability risks posed by these loads that are larger, more volatile, and more fragile than what grid operators are accustomed to seeing.

ON urges the Commission to use this and related rulemakings to accelerate adoption of new standards for the interconnection of large computational loads to ensure grid reliability, power quality, and system stability.
The NERC alert provides a strong initial set of actions and should be codified into uniform, enforceable rules.

ERCOT's large-load interconnection process for load facilities of 75 MW or greater, together with the pending NOGRR 282 and its associated work streams, establishes voltage and frequency ride-through requirements for Large Electronic Loads with explicit ramp-rate limits and addresses modeling, ramp behavior, operating coordination, and interconnection documentation.

The risk of inaction is regional fragmentation: PJM, the California Independent System Operator (CAISO), the Midcontinent Independent System Operator (MISO), the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), and other grid operators each developing their own responses.

letters.desc: OpenAI supports standardized readiness criteria using strict commercial-readiness metrics, and net-impact studies that reduce study duration, to direct scarce study resources to vetted projects.
quotes: OpenAI supports a clear pathway for load paired with on-site or behind-the-meter generationtobeevaluatedonanet-impactbasistocapturerealsystemeffectsandreducestudy burdensandduration.

OpenAI supports standardized readiness criteria that classify large loads based on strict metrics for commercial readiness, end user alignment, site and engineering maturity, and near-term operational timelines.

letters.desc: OpenAI urges faster, more predictable interconnection processes for ready large loads to maintain U.S. competitiveness and prevent gridlock that could push infrastructure development to other countries.
quotes: If interconnection timelines for large loads remain measured in many years, America risks surrendering a decisive advantage to systems that can mobilize infrastructure by centralized command.
OpenAI urges the Commission to advance reforms that preserve system reliability while materially improving the speed, predictability, and scalability of large-load interconnections.
encourages stakeholders to promote simple and actionable steps to expedite the interconnection of ready, high-value large loads, including loads that will help maintain U.S. dominance in AI research.

letters.desc: Oracle supports procedural reforms to speed FERC's own decision-making, including shot clocks and shorter comment periods. The filing links energy access delays directly to slower AI infrastructure deployment.
quotes: One of the most significant and widespread delays Oracle encounters when siting data centers in the United States is access to sufficient energy.
The Commission should support efforts to streamline administrative procedures and harmonize standards related to load sheds and down time.
the Commission could explore imposing decision shot clocks on its own cases.

letters.desc: Oracle argues that data center infrastructure investments improve grid resiliency and reliability at a time of significant grid modernization needs. The company identifies current regulatory fragmentation and interconnection delays as barriers to beneficial investments.
quotes: Patchwork state regulation, long interconnection queues, and complex dynamics between transmission and generation operators complicates efforts to implement and integrate Oracle's beneficial investments.

These infrastructure upgrades can improve the resiliency and reliability of the power grid for all consumers connected to it, at a time when the nation's electric grid is facing significant needs for systematic repair, replacement, and modernization.

letters.desc: OMS supports thorough transmission-level study requirements and argues that connecting large loads without adequate analysis of resource adequacy and cost allocation creates reliability risks. Any FERC role should be confined to the study process itself.
quotes: connecting large loads to the bulk power system without thorough study, without sufficient resource support, and without appropriate cost alignment could introduce new reliability risks and inequities across customer classes.
the Commission should limit its authority over large-load interconnection requests to the study process itself, with clear guardrails ensuring no effect on retail service obligations.

FERC should require large loads seeking to interconnect to demonstrate: site control, proof of transmission service, state notification and consultation, and disconnection authority if service obligations are not met.

letters.desc: Paces argues that manual study processes cannot scale to meet large-load demand and endorses AI agents running approved power-flow tools under engineer oversight. It recommends FERC explicitly permit this approach and pair it with a short study SLA to make automation necessary.
quotes: interconnection studies up to 20x faster with full audit trails and sign-off

manual study processes and speculative, project-by-project signals are producing slow interconnection queues and plans for load that will never be built, while a small set of constraints strands the load that actually can be built
FERC's large-loads rule is the chance to fix both problems

State that transmission providers are encouraged to use AI agents to operate approved study tools and scripts, as long as qualified engineers own the methodology and sign-off and workflows are auditable.
Encourage or require a SLA of <20 business days for all large load initial studies which makes the leveraging of AI automation essential to meet such a timeline.

Direct transmission providers that face material large-load growth to build parcel-level maps of developable large-load sites (zoning, setbacks, floodplains, water, ownership, etc.) and overlay them with bus-level withdrawal headroom.
the real operational risk is mis-located, speculative load plus manual-only study processes that cannot scale

letters.org: Pennsylvania Office of Consumer AdvocateDelaware Division of the Public Advocate
letters.desc: The filers support studying large loads and hybrid facilities together with generation to minimize upgrade costs, but insist the process be technically sound, comply with all NERC guidelines, and not sacrifice reliability or accuracy for speed.
quotes: The Joint Consumer Advocates seek to ensure that these ratepayers do not pay higher rates for less reliable (i.e., inferior) service resulting from the interconnection of large loads that do not offset their load through the addition of timely, local, and adequate capacity resources.
The interconnection study process should not be accelerated at the expense of reliability or accuracy of identifying network upgrades.

The Joint Consumer Advocates support establishing a large load and hybrid interconnection queue that is centrally managed by the same entity that manages/administers resource adequacy processes, like PJM. This queue should have standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to deter speculative projects and provide transmission providers and RTOs with useful information to forecast demand on their systems accurately.

The Joint Consumer Advocates support large loads and hybrid facilities that interconnect to the system only if they bring sufficient capacity (either through generation and reserves or capacity-backed demand response) to offset the additional load brought onto the grid.
The interconnection study process should comply with all NERC guidelines and Reliability Standards and not be accelerated at the expense of reliability or accuracy of identifying network upgrades.

letters.org: Pennsylvania Office of Consumer AdvocateDelaware Division of the Public AdvocateIllinois Office of Attorney General ,
letters.desc: The filers support comprehensive and technically sound interconnection studies for large loads and hybrid facilities. They argue the 20 MW threshold and aggregate demand basis ensure the study process captures all facilities that pose reliability risks, and that joint studies of hybrid facilities must not compromise study quality.
quotes: Residential ratepayers should not suffer unreliable electricity service or pay unreasonably high rates for inferior, unreliable grid service as a result of the interconnection of large loads that do not offset their demand through the addition of timely, local, and adequate capacity resources.

FERC should stay the course and adopt the proposed 20 MW threshold to define large loads and hybrid facilities because this MW threshold helps protect against reliability concerns from large loads or hybrid facilities by requiring proper interconnection studies that will reduce reliability risks for all electricity consumers.
the threshold 'should apply to the customer's aggregate power requirement rather than to a single point of interconnection.'

The definition of large load and hybrid facilities should use the planned full operational capacity, even if the facility is planning to ramp up its operations over time. Otherwise, a new large load or hybrid facility could circumvent the threshold requirement by phasing in its operations.

letters.desc: PFT supports requiring large loads to provide accurate, timely information on their plans and operations to support transmission and generation planning. The filer also endorses safe harbor provisions tied to demonstrated state-level planning effectiveness, and calls for FERC to strengthen transmission planning requirements broadly.
quotes: DOE and FERC could consider, for example, establishing safe harbor provisions whereby states demonstrating effective management of large load interconnection remain free from federal procedural mandates or that encourage states to continue to holistically solve the interrelated challenges of interconnection of large loads and critical new generation.

PFT urges FERC to support the existing functions of state utility regulators while focusing on reforming capacity markets, strengthening transmission planning requirements, and taking a hard look at whether co-located loads are avoiding their share of grid costs and upgrades.

FERC should at a minimum take steps to require that transmission-interconnected large loads participate in efforts to ensure the reliability of the grid and support good transmission and generation planning by providing accurate and timely information about their plans and operations—and are penalized for failure to disclose relevant information or for seeking multiple, duplicative interconnections that distort load forecasting and planning.

letters.desc: CRE can deliver capacity in months instead of years by bypassing interconnection queues and transmission planning cycles, allowing developers to move from concept to operation rapidly while reducing pressure on existing queues and transmission constraints.
quotes: CRE could deliver new capacity in months, not years—without the need to navigate interconnection queues, transmission planning cycles, or state rate proceedings, private developers can move from project concept to commercial operation on timelines that match the urgency of demand growth.

letters.org: PSEG CompaniesPSEG Energy Resources & Trade LLCPSEG Power LLC ,Public Service Electric and Gas Company ,
letters.desc: PSEG supports a timely, standardized study process for large load interconnections and wants the Commission to act quickly. It also requests a fast-track study path for state-sponsored generation to close the resource adequacy gap.
quotes: the time has come for the Commission to act expeditiously by establishing rules that will provide clarity and finality.
there is an urgent need to create an expedited interconnection track to bring state-sponsored resources online faster.
layering on an RMR study that examines resource adequacy issues is unnecessary, inefficient, unduly discriminatory, and not the correct legal or practical fit for these arrangements.

letters.desc: RSI argues that swift FERC action is warranted on the generation side, including assessment of whether further reforms beyond Order 2023 are needed, and that cost-causation misalignment in the current study process should be corrected.
quotes: Limiting the applicability of a rulemaking to those processes that are already FERC-jurisdictional (i.e. expanding the LGIA concept to others seeking to connect to the transmission grid to participate in wholesale markets) reduces the novelty of an ultimate rule, maintains the current balance between state and federal oversight, reduces litigation risk, and ensures that resource adequacy concerns with the rule (that load will take power before generation can catch up) are mitigated
[t]he current system for generation interconnection is inefficient and misaligns cost allocation relative to the beneficiary pays principle.

letters.desc: Efficient large load integration is central to grid growth. Streamlined study processes that incorporate flexibility mechanisms enable quick, reliable, and affordable interconnections.
quotes: enabling the efficient integration of new large loads will be central to the next era of grid growth

FERC should expand its expedited interconnection considerations beyond large load curtailability and co-located generation dispatchability to include appropriately located off-site distributed energy resources that can deliver curtailment or dispatch services under contract.

By allowing both durable peak reductions and aggregated distributed flexibility to qualify under Principles 3 and 7, FERC can give large loads more options to meet interconnection requirements quickly, affordably, and reliably.

letters.desc: RWECE argues that reform timelines exceeding four years fail to meet the ANOPR's acceleration goals. It cites SPP's consolidated planning process as a cautionary example and calls for near-term solutions to be adopted far more quickly.
quotes: Implementing new interconnection mechanisms quickly is important as well.
RWECE believes that solutions which require more than 4 years to complete do not address the issues identified in the ANOPR.

letters.desc: Shell Energy prioritizes improving load projection accuracy in capacity markets over other study reforms, and supports net injection/withdrawal as a tool to speed study timelines for hybrid facilities. NERC and RTO/ISO input is needed before mandating expedited transient stability studies.
quotes: First and highest priority should be for improving accuracy of load projections used in current competitive markets.
Shell Energy views this as the most important principle proposed in the ANOPR. This reform, with proper transparency reporting, significantly improves the credibility of the load forecasts.
Including large loads that pay study deposits and meet established readiness criteria in capacity market demand curves can be executed efficiently relative to other reforms.

Shell Energy supports analyzing the net impact of hybrid/co-located load with generation to allow for more efficient siting, faster study processing and shorter transmission infrastructure construction timelines.
Expedited study processes envisioned under this ANOPR should not cause delays, uncertainty, or allocation of new costs to generator interconnection customers already in queues.

letters.desc: SMA supports studying load and hybrid facilities together with generators, citing current gaps where each side ignores risks from the other. Without joint simulation, grid risks from large dynamic loads go unaddressed.
quotes: SMA believes that without significant reforms, the existing system will be unable to support the rapid deployment of AI data centers necessary for the U.S. to win the global race in AI and digital infrastructure, while ensuring that the regular rate payers have access to affordable and reliable power.

SMA strongly supports the simulation of load and hybrid facilities together as we find large gaps today in addressing the risks on both the grid and AI data center (load) sides, in that the load-side ignores real risks to the grid and vice versa.

letters.desc: SEIA identifies inaccurate load forecasting as the central problem: hyperscalers submit duplicative interconnection requests across multiple utilities, distorting load projections that feed wholesale markets and transmission planning. A standardized interconnection process with readiness requirements and standardized reporting by load-serving entities would improve forecast accuracy.
quotes: the interconnection of these new large loads to the grid is governed by a patchwork of regulations and business practices that fail to deliver accurate load projections or encourage the development of generation to provide energy to those new loads.
Data centers often submit multiple interconnection requests for the same project, and some hyperscalers have acknowledged engaging with multiple utilities simultaneously for a single facility.
SEIA recommends that the Commission allow flexibility in how these studies are conducted and prioritized so that they align appropriately with each region's existing queue and study procedures.
any study of the large load and associated generation, whether co-located or not, must reflect the actual operational needs of the load.

letters.desc: The seven-factor test has guided FERC for nearly three decades, survived court review, and established regulatory certainty. Altering it would lose that certainty and create conflicts between federal regulation and state tariffs. The test should remain unchanged to maintain the state-federal jurisdictional balance.
quotes: We want to emphasize the importance of recognizing and respecting state jurisdiction and avoiding unintended consequences.

In the ANOPR, the Commission expresses its intention not to 'impinge on States' authority over retail electricity sales by asserting jurisdiction over the interconnection of large loads to the transmission system.' Nonetheless, the unintended consequence of expanding the definition of the transmission system may do just that.
This standard has remained in place for nearly three decades, having survived and guided many court cases.

In the ANOPR, the Commission references the seven-factor test and the need to strictly adhere to it. We urge the Commission to not only adhere to the test but to refrain from altering the test or making other changes that would redefine which facilities are considered transmission subject to FERC's jurisdiction.
Altering this precedent would lead to loss of regulatory certainty and could result in conflicts between federal regulation and state-approved tariffs.

Much of the balance of state and federal jurisdiction rests upon the defining of transmission and distribution systems. If the seven-factor test is not preserved, expanding which facilities classify as transmission could create a new class of customers whose rights and privileges extend beyond, and conflict with, state law.

The SPP and MISO approaches to large load interconnection represent well-vetted processes which resulted from significant stakeholder input and buy-in. Both approaches help to address the challenges associated with large load customers while respecting and maintaining state and federal jurisdiction.

letters.desc: SCE emphasizes proactive reliability studies and integrated resource planning are critical before large loads interconnect, to ensure sufficient generation capacity. Federal rules should defer to California's established state planning processes (Resource Adequacy, Integrated Resource Planning, and CAISO Transmission Planning) rather than conflicting with them.
quotes: Given the potential size of large data centers seeking to interconnect, it is critical that proactive reliability studies and integrated planning are thoroughly executed to ensure there is sufficient generation capacity to serve large loads upon interconnection.

the Commission should recognize and support the need for this type of proactive planning while ensuring that any future Commission rule does not conflict with existing state reliability planning processes, and should give deference to the established processes governed by the state regulators.

letters.org: Southern Company Services, Inc.Alabama Power CompanyGeorgia Power Company ,Mississippi Power Company ,
letters.desc: Southern Companies contend that interconnection reform alone cannot solve the AI boom's power supply challenge. They highlight their integrated resource planning process, which evaluates generation, fuel, and transmission together under state oversight, as the mechanism that has kept the Southeast free from resource adequacy crises seen elsewhere.
quotes: Transmission interconnection reform alone cannot ensure that adequate generating capacity, fuel supply, and supporting infrastructure will exist to serve rapidly growing large loads.

the Commission should be mindful, while considering load interconnection reforms, not to create obstacles to integrated resource planning processes that already consider power supply, fuel, and transmission together, and which have the State regulatory support needed to build the generation resources to support AI dominance.

letters.org: Southern Company Services, Inc.Alabama Power CompanyGeorgia Power Company ,Mississippi Power Company ,
letters.desc: The filing credits its vertically-integrated structure and integrated resource planning for holistically combining generation, fuel, transmission, and distribution to serve large loads.
quotes: Southern Companies explained that their vertically-integrated structure and integrated resource planning process enable them to plan for and serve large load customers by holistically combining generation, fuel, transmission, and distribution planning.

letters.org: Southern Environmental Law CenterAppalachian VoicesNorth Carolina Sustainable Energy Association ,South Carolina Coastal Conservation League ,Southern Alliance for Clean Energy ,
letters.desc: The filers support adopting Order No. 2023-style cluster studies, financial commitments, and readiness requirements for large load interconnection, and urge the Commission to add load forecasting standards to reduce speculative queue entries. They also call for rigorous compliance with Order No. 1920 transmission planning to accompany any new interconnection rule.
quotes: the lack of uniform conditions placed on large load interconnections to the transmission system fails to limit speculative interconnection requests, which could lead to overbuilding, a heightened risk of stranded investment, and unjust and unreasonable rates borne by transmission customers.
The Commission should implement study deposits, readiness deposits, and withdrawal penalties in any standardized large load interconnection procedures.
the Commission should require large loads to pay higher study deposits and withdrawal penalties than those applicable to generator interconnections.
the Commission should require rigorous compliance with Order No. 1920.

the Commission should also establish load forecasting requirements that allow transmission providers to mitigate the uncertainty in large load demand forecasting for large loads to ensure just and reasonable rates.

letters.org: Southern Environmental Law CenterNorth Carolina Sustainable Energy AssociationAppalachian Voices ,Coastal Conservation League ,Southern Alliance for Clean Energy ,
letters.desc: The filers support establishing a formal large load interconnection process that firms up load forecasts and reduces speculative requests. They note Georgia Power's model still overestimates large load materialization even after state reforms, and that earlier interconnection commitments combined with joint state-federal queues would improve forecast accuracy and administrative efficiency.
quotes: the size, speed, and density of this surge threaten to overwhelm the transmission grid and the ability of ratepayers to subsidize its expansion.
A large load interconnection process could require large loads to commit to an interconnection request earlier than when a retail service obligation would otherwise attach.
the Commission could encourage joint state and federal interconnection queues

excluding the cost of large load-specific network upgrades from rate base . . . would also prevent transmission providers from earning a return on these facilities, thereby incentivizing them to prioritize transmission upgrades planned through the Order No. 1920 processes

letters.desc: SMECO calls for a final rule establishing standardized, non-discriminatory procedures for orderly interconnections of large new loads without compromising reliability.
quotes: SMECO respectfully submits that a final rule to establish standardized, non-discriminatory procedures for "orderly" interconnections of large new loads without compromising reliability is needed at the present time.

SMECO supports a final rule that would consider expanding the reliability studies that PJM performs pursuant to PJM Tariff, Part V to an existing generating facility that seeks to enter a partial suspension, as described in the ANOPR, to serve any new load authorized to take service in a co-located or hybrid configuration.

letters.org: Southwest Power Pool Transmission Owner Group
letters.desc: The group endorses study processes that pair load and generation, evaluate reliability impacts of partial suspension, and avoid delaying regional proposals that already reflect ANOPR principles. Speed to market depends on rigorous but streamlined study procedures.
quotes: it would be a serious error to force the region to pause this work to await a nationwide rule.
It is essential that any large load rulemaking facilitate the ability to serve new loads with grid-connected generation in a manner similar to the SPP HILL Proposal.

an existing generation resource that intends to divert a material amount of its capacity to serve a new large load at the same location should first submit to a study by the transmission provider to determine whether the diversion of that generation capacity will undermine reliable transmission.

letters.org: Southwest Power Pool Transmission Owner Group
letters.desc: The filer endorses CPP's approach of combining load and generation study into one recurring cycle to reduce upgrade costs and improve system planning.
quotes: CPP 'eliminat[es] the silos between the transmission planning process and the generator interconnection process, synthesizing and streamlining them into one recurring three-year planning cycle.'

letters.desc: SPP supports rigorous interconnection study requirements including transient stability analysis, short-circuit ratio analysis, and critical clearing time screening. SPP argues study scope must cover full gross withdrawal and injection, not net figures, and that cluster studies may be needed at high queue volumes.
quotes: SPP cannot appropriately study the actual impacts of that load on the Transmission System without studying the full impact of its potential withdrawals from the Transmission System. Although this load may have a generator capable of offsetting the load at most times, in the event that generator goes offline, SPP would have to provide the full MW amount to serve that load, and would, therefore, experience the effects of its full withdrawal even if only temporarily.

Based on SPP's experience, 60 days is not sufficient time to study the reliability impacts of large loads. SPP's new HILL policy in the High Impact Large Load Filing provides for a 90 day study time to allow for the necessary stability studies, such as transient stability analysis, short-circuit ratio analysis, and a critical clearing time screening to determine if further electromagnetic transient stability (EMS) analysis is needed.
SPP suggests allowing each region to determine the best approach to minimize the time of study.

letters.desc: The filing argues that interconnection studies should explicitly model the reliability contributions and transmission resilience benefits of fast-responding loads, incorporating their ability to modify demand near-instantaneously during system failures. This ensures system operators accurately assess the actual impact on grid stability.
quotes: Splight strongly supports this principle and respectfully urges the Commission to go further by explicitly recognizing the value of large loads that implement advanced, automated contingency response technologies ("Fast-Responding Loads") as a basis for both (1) expedited interconnection and (2) allocation of increased capacity in proportional to the speed and amount of curtailment a load is able to provide.

Where transmission adequacy is the fundamental limitation, Fast-Responding Loads should be studied based on their ability to modify demand near-instantaneously in the event of a transmission system failure (for example, Splight's DCM can respond in less than 500 milliseconds) and, should be considered for expedited interconnection as firm loads.
Fast-Responding Loads offer an alternative pathway to maintain adherence to the N-1 or N-1-1 planning and operating criteria, while expanding load service.

letters.desc: Switch supports a uniform, efficient study process with firm timelines for ready projects, modeled on Order 2023 generator interconnection reforms. The company highlights that current regional variation creates uncertainty and delays, and calls for coordination between transmission providers and regional planning entities to eliminate duplicative studies.
quotes: Switch generally supports FERC's effort to develop standardized, transparent, and non-discriminatory procedures tailored to large load interconnections such as data centers.

Current practices vary widely across regions, which can create uncertainty and delays that hinder investment by providing discriminatory access for the interconnection of large loads to the interstate transmission system.

If the Commission goes forward with the proposed ANOPR, it should focus on expediting interconnection of proven large load projects with demonstrated site control, committed customers, applicable permits, executed service agreements and/or project financing.
Any rules adopted by the Commission should prioritize projects that are ready for interconnection and reduce the incentives for speculative, non-viable projects.

As part of this process, the Commission should consider firm timelines for studies and approvals for such projects that are ready for interconnection, similar to generator interconnection reforms under Order No. 2023.
The current process often lacks transparency into load interconnection queues and the study process.
Switch encourages coordination between transmission providers and regional planning entities to avoid duplicative studies and delays.
If the Commission decides to proceed with the proposed ANOPR, it should require transmission providers to publish queue status, study assumptions, and cost estimates for large load interconnections.

letters.desc: Terraflux supports expedited studies for curtailable loads but requires that curtailment parameters be clearly and operationally defined so the facility can be modeled and financed.
quotes: While we agree with the seventh principle's assertion that large load and hybrid facilities which agree to be curtailable should be expedited in a 60-day study duration, the details around curtailment allowances should be clearly and reasonably defined by FERC, such that a facility's "high curtailment scenario" can be still be operationally understood, modeled, and financed against by the interconnection customer.

letters.desc: Flexible loads site near existing sources and require fewer transmission upgrades, cutting study requirements and queue congestion. The filer also asks DOE to coordinate with NERC to set transparent, achievable performance criteria.
quotes: Flexible load does not require the same level of transmission upgrades as other businesses and often locates at or near existing power sources. This reduces required studies, transmission upgrades, and queue congestion.
Expand coordination with NERC and reliability entities to ensure transparent, achievable performance criteria for fast-acting interruptible load.

letters.desc: FERC should establish clear implementation principles and direct RTOs/ISOs to update tariffs and expedite Order 2222 compliance to explicitly allow large loads to study and utilize VPPs in interconnection requests.
quotes: The Commission should also consider directing regional grid operators to update their tariffs to explicitly allow large loads to utilize VPPs in interconnection requests.

By establishing a framework and appropriate ground rules for allowing VPPs to be studied together with load and hybrid facilities, the Commission can ensure that large loads have a diverse suite of tools for flexibility and resource adequacy, accelerate interconnection timelines, and encourage large loads to make DER investments that can simultaneously provide direct consumer savings and resiliency benefits.

letters.desc: Pew supports coordinated study of large loads paired with VPPs alongside generation resources. It contends that studying VPP and load components together in a single integrated process captures combined system effects without inappropriately netting them together or masking reliability risks.
quotes: large load customers and hybrid facilities to be able to contract with VPPs and to have those contracts accounted for within the scope of interconnection procedures would greatly further DOE's goals, while advancing the Commission's statutory mandate and principles of facilitating resource-neutral competition in wholesale markets.

Adopting rules that allow integrated, expedited study of large loads that contract with VPPs will facilitate speed-to-power for large load customers while keeping transmission and energy affordable for existing customers.

the Commission should define hybrid facility in a manner that includes large loads paired with VPPs and/or allow for large load customers and hybrid facilities to contract with VPPs or coordinate operations with jointly-owned VPPs in order to provide curtailment and/or dispatch capability.

Pew urges the Commission to draft its rules in such a way that unlocks the multiple benefits that VPPs can provide both to existing transmission customers and large load customers seeking to interconnect while keeping electricity rates affordable and maintaining grid reliability.

letters.desc: TBA argues that interconnection studies must model enforceable curtailment commitments and multi-day load-shifting. Current practice assumes all loads operate at peak, causing unjustified upgrade cost assignments and blocking entry of flexible technologies. Asset-backed flexibility, such as TES, is more reliable than contractual demand response and should be modeled accordingly.
quotes: When tariffs treat all loads as inflexible peak contributors, they distort competition, raise barriers to entry, and suppress innovation in flexible industrial technologies.
TBA strongly recommends that interconnection studies explicitly incorporate enforceable curtailment commitments and multi-day load-shifting capabilities.
Current modeling practices often inaccurately assume flexible loads will operate inflexibly, resulting in assignment of unnecessary network upgrade costs, resource requirements and reserve margin.
Such mis-modeling functions as a regulatory barrier to competition, encouraging only high-load factor and low-flexibility loads, resulting in an under-utilized grid and higher costs for consumers.
asset-backed flexibility is more predictable, more reliable and more durable because it arises from technological and operational capabilities rather than administrative arrangements.

letters.desc: TBA supports requiring that interconnection, transmission, and planning studies reflect the curtailment commitments of non-firm loads. NYISO's development of flexible load models and CAISO's curtailability threshold are cited as evidence that RTOs recognize this need.
quotes: commenters overwhelmingly agree that large loads capable of providing durable, enforceable flexibility should be eligible for expedited interconnection pathways

only loads that are "completely curtailable or dispatchable" should qualify for expedited interconnection study treatment, underscoring that the depth of flexibility determines whether a project can be evaluated without peak-driven upgrades

NYISO also identifies the development of "Flexible Load models for Large Loads" as a priority in its ongoing internal work plan—a clear recognition that formal modeling constructs are needed to appropriately study and integrate flexible load
non-firm loads must be modeled in interconnection, transmission service, and planning studies consistent with their curtailment rights

letters.desc: Tract urges FERC to apply Order No. 2023-style mandatory study deadlines and queue management rules to large load interconnection, including disclosure of timelines, process steps, and how competing requests are handled.
quotes: Tract supports DOE's proposal to study load and hybrid facilities together with generating facilities located at the same point of interconnection. Such joint study process should be at the option of both the load and generation customer and should be designed in such a way to result in faster and/or less costly interconnection for both the load and the generator.
The Commission should apply the lessons it learned in the generator interconnection process and adopt similar deadlines for studying standardized load interconnection requests.

the Commission should establish standardized rules for each step in the large load interconnection process, the expected timing of each step, and other guidelines governing queue management, including whether the transmission provider is employing a cluster study or sequential study model, similar to generator interconnection.
Tract agrees with the proposal to expedite the interconnection study of large loads that agree to be curtailable and hybrid facilities that agree to be curtailable and dispatchable.

Tract agrees that there must be a plan to implement the proposed reforms that recognize the time, capital, and effort spent on requests that are already being studied for interconnection. Negatively affecting those existing requests not only wastes individual requestor's time, capital, and effort, but could also negatively impact all large load requests by causing cascading re-studies that delay or increase the costs of other large load requests.

letters.desc: TAPS supports a rigorous interconnection study process that deters speculation through deposits and penalties, and favors a single queue to reduce gaming. It opposes any expedited track that could disrupt studies for other interconnection customers.
quotes: the Commission must be proactive in addressing the huge impact that the interconnections of Qualifying Large Loads have on Commission-jurisdictional services to protect transmission customers—and, ultimately, other end-use individual and business ratepayers—from paying costs they did not cause.

The use of a single interconnection queue to study Qualifying Large Loads and Hybrid Facilities together with generating facilities may facilitate identifying and avoiding undue discrimination or preference. Using separate study processes for different types of facilities could create opportunities for gaming the system or raise concerns about undue discrimination.

standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties would be beneficial in the context of Qualifying Large Load interconnections. As in the context of generator interconnections, these kinds of requirements are needed to deter speculative requests that may begin the study process but then withdraw, causing delays and restudies.

letters.desc: The filer wants load and supply studied together but warns against modeling storage with unrealistic charging assumptions that would lengthen studies. It points to Order No. 2023's intended-use modeling as a workable precedent for hybrid interconnection studies.
quotes: The ANOPR’s proposal to expedite interconnection studies for large loads and hybrid facilities that agree to be curtailable and dispatchable can, if implemented effectively, significantly increase the pace of interconnection for large loads and their associated supply resources.

if storage resources are studied using unrealistic assumptions (for instance, that they would opt to charge in congested, high-priced grid intervals), the resulting unnecessarily lengthy study processes could limit load’s ability to benefit from this quickly-deployable asset.
The Commission’s requirement in Order No. 2023 that storage be modeled based upon intended use sets a clear pathway for hybrid interconnection as well.

letters.desc: UCS supports requiring that interconnection studies for hybrid facilities use full nameplate capacity for fault analysis. The filing argues that export-limited capacity is appropriate for thermal screening but not for fault conditions, because power limiting controls have inherent delays and cannot prevent inadvertent export. UCS draws on DER interconnection experience and IEEE 2800 to show this gap applies to transmission-connected systems as well.
quotes: capabilities to limit injections or withdrawals are not instantaneous and are not error-proof.
the full nameplate capacity must still be used when studying fault conditions to identify power quality impacts.

the drafting and adoption of rules that presume tight control and a narrow range of performance from conventional generation with co-located loads will need to be based on clearly stated and explicitly measured standards or limits.

letters.desc: The Congress members ask FERC to assess the aggregate effects of multiple large facilities in a single region, covering transmission congestion, local generation adequacy, and resource adequacy planning. They also want multi-party consultation before approvals that could alter demand forecasts.
quotes: Clear communication between FERC, state regulators, utilities, and local communities before approving large interconnections that may alter demand forecasts or infrastructure needs.
Cumulative impacts of multiple large facilities locating within a single region, including effects on transmission congestion, local generation adequacy, and resource adequacy planning.

letters.desc: Senators support standardizing load forecasting and increasing transparency into data center demand projections. They note that uncertain and speculative projections are driving billions in utility investments.
quotes: In PJM Interconnection, the regional transmission organization (RTO) that serves thirteen states and the District of Columbia in the mid-Atlantic region, data centers will drive 90% of new power demand over the next five years.

Prompted by projections like these – many of which rely on uncertain and speculative data center proposals – utilities and transmission planning regions are spending billions to guarantee the grid can meet this demand.
FERC should also consider broader proceedings that would standardize load forecasting and other practices relevant to addressing data center demand growth.

Without transparency into load forecasting, it is difficult to assess the quality of a utility's load projections, making it challenging to ensure the economically responsible build-out of new generation or transmission assets.

letters.org: Utility Intervention Unit, New York State Department of Stat
letters.desc: The UIU supports using NYISO's existing cluster study methodology for large loads, with the same procedural steps, queue priority rules, and milestones already applied to generators. A separate, lighter process would disrupt sequential cluster studies and create inequities.
quotes: Protecting consumers means ensuring that developers bear the costs of infrastructure driven by their own demand (ignoring co-located generation), that planning processes remain open to public scrutiny, and that regional coordination prevents unintended reliability or cost consequences.
UIU supports the ANOPR proposal to study load and hybrid facilities together with generating facilities.
UIU supports the ANOPR proposal to require that generating facilities, load and hybrid facilities be subject to standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties.

UIU opposes any consideration of a less rigorous interconnection process applicable to large load interconnection. If large load interconnections were managed through a separate, less-rigorous process, it could create inequities and disrupt the timing and results of sequential interconnection cluster studies.

letters.desc: Vantage endorses integrated study processes that evaluate hybrid facility load and generation components together. Sequential studies produce inaccurate grid impact assessments and generate avoidable network upgrade requirements; joint studies eliminate this problem. Interconnection delays under current processes have forced Vantage to invest in stand-alone generation rather than grid-connected projects.
quotes: Vantage emphasizes that the specific principles and reforms concerning (1) hybrid interconnecting data center facilities supported in whole or in part by dedicated generating facilities (Principles 3 and 5), (2) expedited interconnection study procedures (Principle 7), (3) cost allocation for interconnection-related network upgrades (Principle 8), and (4) a fair and structured transition that respects existing rights (Principle 13) are of greatest importance.

Vantage is compelled to make significant investments in power plants, sometimes having to limit or forgo reliance on traditionally reliable grid-connected power due to load interconnection delays, shortages of available utility supply, or infeasible interconnection regulations requiring large new loads to be curtailable.

Currently, many transmission and interconnection study processes involve independent evaluations at different times which can produce unintended results, including inaccurate assessments of impacts on the grid and resulting requirements for network upgrades that could have been avoided or mitigated by undertaking the studies in tandem.

letters.desc: VEIR supports standardized data requirements and predictable study timelines drawn from generator interconnection reforms. The filer also asks for a low-impact study track and incentives for enabling technologies within the NOPR.
quotes: VEIR supports the Commission initiating a rulemaking to develop a transparent, predictable, and technology-neutral framework for these connections, recognizing that timely action is essential for U.S. economic growth, competitiveness and grid resilience.

The large-load interconnection regime can include both procedural mechanisms and technology-neutral performance standards (or incentives) that reward deployment of high-capacity, space-efficient systems. For example, expedited study tracks might apply for projects proposing such high-density conductors.

VEIR invites FERC to consider in the ANOPR stage: (a) whether study cost-allocation frameworks should recognize reduced ROW and environmental impact associated with innovative cable technology; (b) whether pilot or demonstration status of such technologies merits expedited interconnection treatment; and (c) how manufacturing scale-up of such systems may reduce long-lead supply-chain delays that currently hamper large-load attachments.

We ask FERC to consider creating a "low-impact interconnection study track" for projects that demonstrably reduce system or siting complexity—such as those using compact, underground, or non-emitting delivery technologies.
We encourage FERC, in issuing its NOPR, to incorporate mechanisms that actively incentivize or accelerate deployment of enabling solutions like superconducting cable systems.

letters.desc: Verrus wants transmission providers to file transparent, uniform large load interconnection procedures that prohibit discretionary utility reprioritization, require public reporting of queue outcomes, and explicitly model flexible load curtailment in interconnection and planning studies.
quotes: Flexible large loads represent a technology solution that can uniquely speed interconnection time, maximize the use of the grid we have, while also providing a distinct set of benefits to grid operators and resource adequacy planners.

In some jurisdictions, access depends more on negotiations, relationships, or economic-development discretion than on objective, system-based criteria. This uncertainty makes it difficult for emerging flexible-load developers to plan projects, creates inefficiency for utilities, and risks allowing priority to be determined by factors other than measurable system benefit and equitable treatment of all consumers.

Flexible loads that meet this definition should also be allowed to nominate operational flexibility commitments in the study process that allow the Transmission Provider to avoid, reduce, or defer network upgrades, thereby accelerating interconnection and reducing system costs.

The Commission should require transmission providers to adopt large load interconnection procedures that: Apply uniform criteria for readiness and advancement. Prohibit any discretionary reprioritization or selective acceleration by utilities. Require public reporting of queue timelines and outcomes to maintain accountability.

The Commission should require a Fast-Lane Study Track for verified flexible loads, using shorter study timelines and modeling that accounts for their ability to curtail or shift load and to operate on-site resources.

The Commission should require transmission providers to explicitly model flexible-load curtailment potential in their base-case and sensitivity analyses so that flexibility is valued in interconnection studies with respect to network upgrades, and in the studies that underlie local and regional transmission planning.

letters.desc: Verrus argues that a fast-track study lane for curtailable loads is not discriminatory queue-jumping but an engineering efficiency: when a load commits to curtail, the study scope shrinks and a shorter timeline is warranted. Treating a no-upgrade project at the same pace as a complex one is itself discriminatory.
quotes: the current "one-size-fits-all" approach to large load interconnection is unjust, unreasonable, and unduly discriminatory.
Existing rules generally fail to distinguish between loads that strain the grid and loads that possess the physical capability to support it.

an expedited timeline is not discriminatory "queue jumping" as some commenters have suggested—it simply reflects the reduced time required to study a simpler project and the efficiency gains realized when faster projects are allowed to move at a faster pace.

Treating a flexible project that requires zero network upgrades with the same study duration as a massive, inflexible load that requires new transmission lines is, in itself, discriminatory. It delays the efficient project for no technical reason.

Southwest Power Pool's ("SPP") recent High Impact Large Load Generation Assessment ("HILLGA") proposal recognizes that integrating the study of load with electrically proximate generation/resources is more efficient than standalone regulation.

letters.desc: The VSCC argues that load interconnection queues and studies should remain with the utilities that have direct knowledge of the retail system, with state commission oversight. RTO-run queues would duplicate effort, rely on the utility anyway, and introduce regional inefficiencies that harm states with available capacity.
quotes: the best approach to these issues is a cooperative one, where the Commission sets minimum standards for interconnecting utilities to meet, while leaving it to state commissions to regulate these retail tariffs as they have done for many years.

Develop a set of Commission-mandated minimum standards for large load interconnections, such as study deposits, site control requirements, and similar criteria while allowing transmission owners, and not the RTOs, who already face long delays and inefficiencies in their existing generation queues, to continue to manage large load interconnection queues with direct oversight of their state regulatory commissions.

the Commission should acknowledge the inefficiencies inherent to the large, regional queues administered by PJM and other RTOs. These inefficiencies can lead to longer queue lines and projects in states with available capacity being stuck behind projects in states that are already saturated.

The alternative approach envisioned by the ANOPR, which would establish one queue at the RTO for "large loads" and a different queue at the local utility for every other end-use customer still left with the utility, would create planning and study inefficiencies and could potentially disrupt other important loads, like manufacturers and commercial load, from being able to interconnect in a timely manner.

the VSCC encourages the Commission to issue in an eventual Notice of Proposed Rulemaking ("NOPR") in this docket a set of minimum standards for load interconnection tariffs that all load serving utilities would have to meet. Responsibility for load interconnection, including maintaining a load interconnection queue and performing necessary load interconnection studies, would remain with the utility and overseen by state regulators.

letters.desc: Vistra supports standardized, Commission-supervised interconnection study processes limited to transmission system impacts, arguing the current absence of rules lets utilities exercise unchecked discretion and creates unjust rates and discrimination risks. Resource adequacy must be excluded from interconnection studies.
quotes: the 'timely, orderly, and non-discriminatory' interconnection of large loads, including data centers, to the transmission system is critical to ensuring American prosperity as well as the affordability, reliability, and security of our electric system.

the Commission should begin by acting in the multiple long-pending dockets with well-developed evidentiary records.  Doing so would immediately resolve the regulatory uncertainty that has crippled the industry for the past 18 months.

The lack of rates, terms, and conditions for transmission-level load interconnection has created a vacuum in which utilities are exercising unfettered discretion to determine, among other things, the process by which large loads interconnecting to the transmission system are studied, how to allocate the costs incurred to facilitate those load interconnections, and whether to allow large loads to interconnect to the transmission system at all.

the studies involving the interconnection of new loads must focus on studying the impacts to the transmission system.  As noted above, states retain jurisdiction over generation facilities.  With that in mind, and consistent with the Commission's jurisdiction over the transmission system -- and interconnections to it -- load interconnection studies must be focused on identifying the transmission system upgrades needed to facilitate the interconnection and allocating the costs of those upgrades in a manner consistent with the Commission's cost causation principles.

Using the load interconnection process to address resource adequacy issues would also place resource adequacy obligations on the wrong entity.  New loads coming onto the system only create a resource adequacy issue if an LSE signs up new customers without sufficient generation resources to serve those loads.  LSEs should be responsible for resolving resource adequacy issues that they have allowed to arise.

The consideration of resource adequacy issues in load interconnection studies may also grant LSEs a new ability to exercise undue discrimination.  LSEs often have nearly unbounded discretion in producing load forecasts, which is one of the primary tools used to assess whether a resource adequacy concern might arise.

the Commission should also clarify that its new pro forma procedures only apply prospectively, consistent with the rule against retroactive ratemaking.  The Commission should propose a transition process that permits customers that are interconnecting under other processes (such as the necessary study process or any applicable state-level process) to choose whether to continue through those processes or under any new procedures that the Commission adopts.

Transmission owners that have unregulated generation affiliates or operate in states where large loads have the option to select a competitive supplier have a clear incentive to favor the interconnection of new large loads that agree to take electric service from their affiliated generation.  This incentive creates the potential for a textbook example of undue discrimination that must be remedied by a set of national rules that explicitly bar undue discrimination and with on-going compliance checks to ensure those rules are working as designed.

letters.desc: Vistra supports coordinating load and generator studies for co-located facilities to align timelines and reduce uncertainty. It also supports a standardized standalone load interconnection process that would improve load forecasting and capacity market signals.
quotes: Regulatory uncertainty is stymying data center development and the Commission's inaction in its most significant proceedings involving data center development is a major reason why.

there are at least three incentives for discrimination that the Commission can recognize and address: (1) transmission owners with generation affiliates have an incentive to favor the interconnection of large loads that agree to take service from their affiliated generation; (2) transmission owners have an incentive to favor large loads interconnecting in front of the meter to maximize transmission charges; and (3) incumbent utilities have an incentive to seek to develop the generation component of co-located load.
a standardized process could include study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to deter speculative projects that are unlikely to materialize.
A more realistic forecast would result in better transmission planning and capacity market price signals.

letters.desc: The filers endorse holistic study of load and generation but ask that the study scope explicitly include incremental distributed resources in the relevant grid area, and that those resources be netted against load withdrawals and considered in study prioritization.
quotes: These comments endorse the above principles while expanding on them to ensure that “electrically proximate” or “adjacent” grid assets—assets that can mitigate the constraints imposed by new loads where those constraints actually occur—are also considered in study prioritization, netted against load withdrawals for study purposes, and included in speed-to-power incentive structures.

the existing ANOPR Principle Three, “load and hybrid facilities should be studied together with generating facilities,” should explicitly include study of incremental resources in the relevant grid area,16 whether or not those resources look like traditional utility-scale power plants.

letters.desc: Off-site resources should be studied alongside large load interconnection requests on equivalent terms, with system operator control enabling their integration into operations and planning.
quotes: Off-site distributed energy resources ("DERs") can deliver the same types of energy services—generation, load reduction, or transmission relief—that on-site assets provide.
appropriately located off-site resources provide network benefits on par with those provided by on-site resources, and should be studied and interconnected with equivalent priority.

letters.desc: The UTC sees value in FERC identifying principles around load forecasting and load certainty to help system planners and grid operators handle the unique challenges posed by large loads.
quotes: the UTC sees value in identifying principles around load forecasting and load certainty to address the unique challenges that large loads are presenting to system planners and grid operators.

letters.desc: The filers ask FERC to extend the Order No. 2023 ATT study mandate to large load interconnection. They cite FERC's own finding that omitting ATTs produces unjust rates, and argue that ATTs' speed and cost advantages make them essential to any large load rulemaking.
quotes: ATTs can rapidly increase the grid's capacity in 18-36 months using existing infrastructure and rights-of-way ("ROW") providing fast solutions to unlock new grid capacity while also being a bridge to bring new large loads on more quickly while new network transmission upgrades are built.

"Because the benefits of the enumerated alternative transmission technologies identified above are present across all interconnection processes, regardless of the size of the interconnection request, we find that the failure to evaluate the enumerated alternative transmission technologies results in both the pro forma LGIP and pro forma SGIP being unjust, unreasonable, and unduly discriminatory or preferential."

Order No. 2023 found that ATTs "can be deployed more quickly to be used as network upgrades in place of, and at a lower cost than, traditional network upgrades," and highlighted the numerous benefits commenters stated ATTs can provide including, "resolving thermal overloads and avoiding voltage collapse, allowing for better use of the existing transmission system, improving reliability, and reducing interconnection request withdrawals, restudies, and overall interconnection delays."

The WATT and AMP Coalitions respectfully request that the list of ATTs required to be studied in Order No. 2023 should also be required alongside the other principles proposed by the Secretary for any process for the interconnection of large loads to the interstate transmission system.

DLRs were initially included on the ATT list in the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking ("NOPR") for Order No. 2023. However, DLR was removed from the list of ATTs required to be evaluated in Order No. 2023, ostensibly because it was not among the technologies showing the "most potential to be useful," despite a well-developed record showing benefits in the generator interconnection process.
Additionally, the Commission could issue a separate rulemaking on the use of all ATTs to address issues such as congestion or grid efficiency and utilization in near term planning and operations.

letters.desc: The filer supports requiring ATT evaluation in large load interconnection studies, consistent with Order No. 2023 and CEBA's recommendation. It argues this step is necessary but not sufficient, and calls for broader RTO-level studies of DLR and topology optimization potential as well.
quotes: requiring ATTs to be evaluated in interconnection processes is valuable, it is not sufficient to enable large load interconnection at the fastest reasonable pace and lowest possible cost.

we agree with the CEBA's recommendation "that the Commission require ATTs—including dynamic line ratings—to be evaluated alongside traditional upgrades for large load interconnections, consistent with Order No. 2023, given the significant benefits identified for consumers and interconnection customers."

The time has come and gone for voluntary or incentivized consideration of GETs. It is well documented that use of GETs delivers cost reductions and cost avoidance to the benefit of consumers nationwide. Despite this, relatively few projects have been implemented.
accelerated ATT adoption is more likely to speed the interconnection of new large loads to constrained transmission systems rather than frustrate speed to power goals.

The fastest action that can be taken to identify potential untapped grid capacity is large-scale studies by RTOs. RTOs have sufficient data on grid constraints and electricity prices to use publicly available DLR datasets and/or software from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) to quickly determine the likely magnitude of value from DLR.

we urge the Commission to encourage all RTOs to host forums to investigate the opportunity for ATTs and other solutions to increase capacity and improve affordability and how to integrate ATTs into all aspects of an RTO's processes.

ATTs can deliver meaningful increases in transmission capacity to facilitate the interconnection of large load in less than three years. While recent deployments by PG&E, Georgia Power and others validate this potential, utility adoption remains limited.

letters.desc: WIRES supports expediting large load interconnection but urges the Commission not to derail reform efforts already underway in regions across the country. Rather than impose a new regulatory regime, the Commission should accommodate these efforts and allow regional variations in compliance filings to reflect each system's differences.
quotes: WIRES generally supports the urgent need, as recognized by the Secretary, to expedite and streamline the interconnection of large loads.

WIRES urges the Commission to ensure that ongoing regulatory initiatives aimed at achieving the objectives embodied in the Secretary’s proposal are not derailed - intentionally or as an unintended consequence of any Commission action.
Efforts to meet these growing interconnection and emerging transmission needs are already well underway in regions across the United States.

To the extent these ongoing efforts appear likely to yield new processes and reforms that could accomplish the Secretary’s goal of expediting the interconnection of large loads, the Commission should seek to accommodate these efforts expeditiously rather than inadvertently slowing down or preempting them with the adoption of a new regulatory regime.
Similarly, to accommodate more nuanced approaches nationwide, the Commission’s final order should allow for regional variations in compliance filings.

letters.desc: ATC supports joint study of load and generation in principle but warns that combining new generation and new loads in shared models adds complexity and can make cost allocation extremely difficult. ATC urges the Commission to preserve transmission owner discretion to manage study schedules and model updates.
quotes: we are familiar with proposals where the load seeks to ramp up and ramp down by hundreds of megawatts on a second-to-second basis.  This is equivalent to turning Wisconsin's capital city of Madison on and off, repeatedly.  These rapid, significant swings are unlike anything our industry has seen before and incomparable to any other load on today's grid.

the Commission should consider adopting threshold applicability requirements based upon specific operating requirements for all loads in terms of ramp rates (i.e., how quickly they can increase or decrease electricity usage), active power oscillatory behavior (i.e., how much and how fast active power can swing once they are online), and ride-through capability (i.e., how well the load can remain connected and stable during grid disturbances such as voltage dips, frequency excursions, or short interruptions).
ATC recently completed an 18-month study costing approximately $400,000 in contracted engineering services, primarily due to the novelty and complexity of the work.
ATC recommends setting a more realistic expectation of 120 days for study completion.

letters.desc: APS generally supports the study requirement but calls for longer timelines with stakeholder consultation, safeguards against delays to generator interconnection from added complexity, and evaluation criteria focused on reliability and economic impact.
quotes: the ANOPR's position of a 60-day study timeline might be inadequate dependent on the information required for the study itself, and the timeline should be determined in consultation with the stakeholders and transmission planners.
What safeguards will there be to prevent delays to the generator interconnection process given the increase in complexity of the study process?
APS intends to evaluate any draft proposed rule with a focus on system reliability and economic impact.

letters.desc: Duke Energy supports orderly study processes with deposits and readiness requirements, but warns that creating a new large load study process that must coordinate with existing generator interconnection cluster studies raises numerous unresolved implementation questions that could take years to litigate.
quotes: standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties will help to deter speculative requests.
Duke Energy cautions that it may take several years to develop (and potentially litigate) just and reasonable rules to address these issues.
Transmission providers must have the ability to study all load and generation, including hybrid facilities, in a manner that reflects the potential actual operating impacts to the grid.

Duke Energy urges the Commission to consider whether the time needed to address the complexity and details of coordinated load and generation studies will help achieve faster interconnection of large loads or whether such an effort could actually impede timely interconnections of large loads at this pivotal moment.

letters.desc: Entergy supports the principle that load and generation additions should be studied together for efficiency, but opposes applying a uniform federal study process and requires that hybrid loads be studied on a gross rather than net basis to capture actual reliability impacts.
quotes: we agree that the study of load and generation additions together can result in a more efficient and cost-effective identification of transmission upgrades.
we also agree that it is reasonable to take steps to deter speculative loads from delaying the interconnection of genuine projects.
the Commission should allow individual utilities to submit proposals that specifically address the technical details involved in studying new loads or the requirement of operational limitations.

netting should not affect the way an interconnection request is studied.  Studying hybrid facilities in the manner contemplated by the proposed ANOPR may fail to identify needed network upgrades, because it will be blind to potentially substantial new loads, as long as those new loads are 'hybrid.'

Large loads should not be permitted to interconnect without consideration of available generation capacity.
