For example, if existing generation is being used to serve a large load (rather than the construction of new generation), studies to ensure reliability and local resource adequacy will be needed.

letters.desc: Equinix supports study frameworks that accurately model aggregated flexibility resources and reveal the specific constraints driving upgrade costs. However, the company opposes study queue prioritization for flexible or co-located loads, arguing that cost and timeline savings from avoided upgrades are sufficient market incentives.
quotes: where costs incurred provide broader benefit, however, cost allocation should follow the beneficiary pays principle, creating an economic signal that maximizes benefits and minimizes costs for all customers.

Providing that study frameworks accurately model and value the relevant operational characteristics of the proposed large load along with its aggregated flexibility resources, it is not clear to us why study queue prioritization or any other exogenous benefit is necessary or appropriate.

We recommend against introducing study prioritization frameworks. In our experience, operating in 37 countries around the world—including many markets where such frameworks are in place—such approaches introduce considerable room for fluctuating policy objectives to muddy economic signals, and to increase uncertainty, associated financing costs, and interconnection timing.

letters.org: Georgia Power CompanyAlabama Power CompanyMississippi Power Company ,
letters.desc: The filer argues that the Southeast's vertically integrated IRP model performs the coordinated interconnection study function that the ANOPR seeks to create federally. They support the ANOPR's study objectives but oppose applying new study requirements in regions where integrated planning is already delivering timely results. They accept that other regions with backlogs may need reform.
quotes: Southern Companies wholeheartedly endorse the ANOPR's stated objective of ensuring "timely and orderly interconnection of large loads to the transmission system."

In the Southeast, the vertically-integrated nature of Southern Companies' operations, paired with pre-existing integrated planning procedures, enables Southern Companies to adapt quickly and provide the type of coordinated interconnection operations envisioned in the ANOPR.
Southern Companies respectfully urge the Commission to avoid implementing the ANOPR in a manner that would impede these successful existing processes.
if queue backlogs and procedural impediments exist in other parts of the country, the Commission may need to implement reforms of the type proposed in the ANOPR in those regions.

Southern Companies fully support the ANOPR's stated objectives of timely and orderly interconnection of large loads to the transmission system, while also respectfully urging the Commission to focus on legally durable solutions that would not disrupt the successful outcomes already being achieved in the Southeast.

letters.desc: Heron warns that prescriptive generation mandates and lengthy studies raise queue timelines, costs, and upgrades. It wants demonstrated performance at the point of interconnection to satisfy stability rules, and streamlined or distinct study pathways for grid-forming and verifiable loads.
quotes: Overly prescriptive rules with generation mandates or lengthy interconnection studies that fail to recognize the capabilities of modern power electronics to support the grid will produce longer queue timelines, higher costs, and more network upgrades.

Facilities that can demonstrate, at the point of interconnection, that their power draw remains within defined voltage & frequency ride-through, ramp-rate and ripple thresholds should be recognized as meeting the AI training load stability requirements the Commission and NERC are developing, without additional prescriptive equipment mandates.
the Commission should create a distinct interconnection treatment pathway for large loads that demonstrate grid-forming capability

RTOs and transmission providers should be directed to develop streamlined interconnection study procedures for loads implementing open, publicly documented control architectures, reducing the study depth required for facilities whose control behavior is fully verifiable.

letters.desc: LPPC supports interconnection studies for large load but urges flexibility to accommodate regional differences, warning that mandatory joint study or inflexible cluster-study priority rules can disadvantage other projects.
quotes: While many utilities have found it useful to study new load and generation together, in some settings the introduction of large load into the study process will be disruptive of existing study processes and holds the potential to delay both generation and load interconnections.

Establishing an inflexible priority for load and resources that agree to curtail within a cluster study can disadvantage other projects and introduce additional uncertainty for costs and timing of needed generation and network upgrades.

interconnection of large-load facilities dominated by power electronic loads requires specific attention to potential control interactions with other systems in the grid. The relevance of this issue and the necessary interconnection requirements and restrictions are inherently location-specific based on the strength of the grid and the proximity to potentially interacting systems.

letters.desc: NRECA opposes a rigid study requirement for hybrid facilities and calls for regional flexibility. A comprehensive transition period is also needed to coordinate new large-load rules with existing interconnection, transmission service, and planning processes.
quotes: transmission providers should have the flexibility to establish criteria requiring full studies of the separate loss of the generation or load, and dynamic modelling of generation and load operation, where appropriate to ensure system reliability and stability.

A reasonable, orderly and comprehensive transition period will be necessary. The proposed reforms, in whatever form, would require coordination with existing generator-interconnection, transmission-service request, and transmission-planning processes.

letters.org: New York Independent System Operator, Inc.
letters.desc: NYISO supports improved load interconnection study processes but warns that integrating load studies into its new generator cluster process could slow down Order No. 2023 reforms. It also wants resource adequacy impacts assessed for any large load addition, not only co-location proposals.
quotes: Clustering multiple proposed load interconnections with the simultaneous study of proposed generator interconnection requests is likely to present challenges.

Affording flexibility to the NYISO to reform its load process will ensure that the timeliness of the generator interconnection process is not impacted while also furthering the goal of reliably interconnecting large loads to the transmission system fairly and expeditiously.
it is important to note that resource adequacy issues can also arise when large loads are added to the system, unrelated to a proposal to co-locate with an existing generator.

letters.desc: ODEC opposes joint load-generation studies and instead supports separate analyses that account for generator outage scenarios, different retirement timelines, and ELCC values. It also insists that any material change to either component of a hybrid project trigger a refile.
quotes: ODEC does not support studying load and hybrid facilities together with generation facilities.
Generators experience both planned and unplanned outages; thus, the transmission facilities must be evaluated with only the load operational, not the generation.
Any significant change to either the load or the generation should require the project to refile, ensuring that system studies remain accurate and reliable.

letters.desc: PG&E supports grandfathering customers already in study while urging that new rules not mandate joint study processes that would strain existing queues. It also calls for multi-scenario studies for hybrid facilities.
quotes: To avoid delays and the uncertainty of potential mid-stream changes, PG&E strongly recommends that the Commission make clear that a final rule will only apply to large load customers who have not yet submitted an interconnection application to a utility and/or transmission provider as of the date of the Commission issues a decision.

PG&E recommends that the Commission not mandate a single study approach but instead allow individual utilities and/or Regional Transmission Organizations and Independent System Operators ('RTO/ISO') to decide the most efficient way to coordinate planning.

Adding into this mix load and hybrid facility interconnections may only exacerbate this problem. In some parts of the country, load and hybrid facility interconnection requests may be able to be seamlessly added to the generation interconnection process. In other parts of the country, adding this new requirement to an already overburdened process may be detrimental.

the Commission should direct that hybrid facilities be studied under multiple potential scenarios so that the interconnection facilities can be designed and built to accommodate the inevitable circumstance of a generator or large load being partially or wholly off-line.

letters.desc: PJM supports thorough interconnection studies but flags that a new federal load queue creates significant administrative burdens, may not improve outcomes over existing processes, and could conflict with generator interconnection timelines. It recommends leveraging existing necessary study processes where possible.
quotes: While the prospect of a federally-regulated large load interconnection process warrants further exploration, PJM encourages FERC to seize available opportunities to issue nearer-term regulatory guidance on matters squarely within its wholesale and transmission jurisdiction about:  resource adequacy, the provision of ancillary services, mandatory operational regimes, potential wholesale rate classes for different types of load customers, interconnection and transmission planning, cost allocation, and NERC and Tariff reliability obligations and requirements.

there remains a question as to whether any rule developed on the existing record targeted at this specific topic would entangle the Commission and stakeholders in a potentially contentious dispute that would distract from the need to provide a durable pathway to the ANOPR's desired outcome:  timely and orderly large load interconnections.

questions would need to be answered about whether such a new process will necessarily lead to different or enhanced large load interconnection results, and whether the theoretical benefits of a federally-regulated large load interconnection process outweigh the challenges of creating and administering a load queue at the RTO/ISO level.

Even assuming record evidence could support the ANOPR's proposed 20 MW load threshold for the ANOPR's conceptual reforms to apply, is that clear line set at the appropriate level given that large loads, most especially data centers, tend to be substantially larger than 20 MW?  Will such a threshold over capture load subject to the proposed reforms, clog interconnection processes, and stymie the intended proposed reforms?

Can any large load interconnection studies – expedited or otherwise – be completed in 60 days?  Based on PJM's experience in managing, coordinating, and performing interconnection studies under the best of circumstances, such a timeline is not likely to be feasible in reality at least in the shorter-term horizon though PJM is certainly committed to acting with as much speed and accuracy as possible consistent with Good Utility Practice.

Today, it takes approximately 6 months to complete stability studies due to the complexity of the data, modeling, and analytical processes.  And any additional expedited processes – serial in nature or otherwise – may exacerbate or reintroduce queue backlogs for generator interconnection projects subject to cluster studies.

PJM anticipates needing at least 12 or more additional months to implement any new large load interconnection process (although this estimate is admittedly speculative since the full details of the proposed reforms are not yet clearly known).

Many of these principles could be addressed through the existing PJM necessary study process that PJM previously utilized to study, develop, and modify existing generator interconnections and agreements seeking to co-locate large loads.  This effectively means no FERC action may be needed to accomplish some of the proposed reforms in certain instances.

letters.desc: Talen supports cautious, balanced study requirements but opposes enhanced reliability studies that impose disproportionate burdens on large loads contracting with existing generation, calling such asymmetry unlawful discrimination.
quotes: Talen Energy Corporation (“Talen”) files these reply comments to encourage the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“Commission” or “FERC”) to proceed with caution in any action taken following the proposed Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (“ANOPR”) in order to preserve the federal/state jurisdictional balance established under the Federal Power Act (“FPA”) and decades of precedent.

enhanced reliability studies that apply disproportionate requirements to large loads contracting with existing generation as opposed to new generation are unlawful and will result in undue discrimination against existing generation.

letters.desc: The VSCC supports minimum federal standards to remove bottlenecks in load interconnection queues and reform of the generation interconnection process at PJM, but opposes shifting the queue operator role away from transmission owners. It argues structural causes of delay require targeted fixes, not a change in who runs the queue.
quotes: The approach described by the VSCC in its initial comments would ameliorate these concerns by maintaining existing state jurisdiction over interconnection of load, while allowing the Commission to ensure that the states are exercising this jurisdiction subject to minimum baselines that expedite interconnection as much as possible.

merely changing the regulator of such interconnections from state agencies to the Commission and the queue operator from transmission owners to PJM will not accelerate these interconnections if the reason for such delays is structural (i.e. lack of available generation or delayed transmission upgrades).

By implementing a minimum set of standards designed to remove bottlenecks in the interconnection queue itself, interconnections can be expedited while not disturbing existing state-federal jurisdictional boundaries.

the Commission should act within its existing jurisdiction to accelerate interconnection of generation needed to support load. As the Commission has noted in several PJM proceedings, the generation interconnection process desperately needs to be reformed.

The Commission should direct PJM to do more, including additional processes like the RRI. Removing the causes of generation interconnection backlogs would go far in accelerating load interconnections.

state large load tariffs should also require withdrawal or capacity reduction procedures to ensure that projects that inevitably need to exit the queue or adjust injection/withdrawal from the system can do so with minimal disruption to other projects and the orderly interconnection of loads.

letters.desc: The APSC argues that SPP and MISO have already adopted or proposed interconnection study reforms (HILLS, CHILLS, and MISO's expedited process) that address the problems the ANOPR targets. A new federal study requirement would duplicate or override work already producing results in these regions.
quotes: the proposed rule is unnecessarily harmful for Arkansas and risks disrupting well‑functioning regional and state processes.
there are already processes for the integration of large loads and therefore the proposed ANOPR is unnecessary.

SPP is proposing innovative tariff offerings such as the High‑Impact Load ("HILLS") and Conditional High Impact Large Load (CHILLS") proposed tariff revisions which will establish a 90-day study and approval process for interconnecting large loads.

Arkansas supported and FERC recently approved MISO's Expedited Resource Addition Study Process to address faster processes through MISO's interconnection queue, which addresses the issues FERC seeks to remedy.
These reforms are specifically tailored to regional system needs and reflect ongoing coordination among the RTOs, load‑serving entities, transmission owners and state regulators.
Federal action should be reserved for regions where processes are failing, not those where reforms are already in place and producing results.

limits any final rule to transmission‑level engineering studies only; recognizes existing regional processes such as SPP's proposed HILLS and CHILLS as compliant alternatives; sets a minimum load threshold of no less than 100 MW; and requires robust coordination with state regulators.
A federal rule that overrides or duplicates these efforts is unnecessary and counterproductive.

letters.org: California Department of Water Resources State Water Project
letters.desc: DWR warns that preferential queue access for curtailable loads could cause generators to restructure projects to claim the benefit, crowding the queue for other interconnection customers.
quotes: Preferential access to the queue raises the potential for game playing—many generators could conform their projects to include new, curtailable load, thus crowding the queue for other generators and new loads.

letters.desc: Consumers Energy cautions that several ANOPR study proposals could slow generation interconnection timelines at a moment when the Administration has declared new dispatchable generation a priority. The filer urges targeted, careful changes and points to MISO's existing ERAS expedited process as evidence that the region is already under study-queue pressure.
quotes: the Company is concerned that allowing large load customers the option to build may carry unintended reliability risks given that many large load customers are data centers or other large industrial customers that lack the industry expertise required to ensure safe and reliable grid operations.
large load customers should not be entitled to the same option to build as generation owners.
the Commission should carefully evaluate how such changes could impact and potentially slow the interconnection of new generation that the Administration has made a priority.

Certain ANOPR proposals, such as the notion that 'the interconnection study of large loads that agree to be curtailable and hybrid facilities that agree to be curtailable and dispatchable should be expedited,' will burden RTO/ISO resources that are also working to perform timely studies of new generation.
RTOs, ISOs, transmission owners, and generation owners have all worked diligently to incorporate the reforms included in Order No. 2023 and need regulatory certainty moving forward.

letters.desc: Critical Loop opposes the current default of modeling large loads at static maximum withdrawal with all resources unavailable. It argues this assumption overstates upgrade costs and obscures BESS value. The preferred alternative uses LLFC operating envelopes and explicit non-performance contingencies as the base case, paired with hosting-capacity-style data and a 60-day initial determination to speed planning.
quotes: the bottleneck is the commercial and procedural pathway
these same frameworks can reduce the proliferation of 'phantom' large‑load projects, speculative or oversized requests that sit in queues and distort transmission planning and investment signals

transmission providers should evaluate interconnections against those limits with explicit non‑performance contingencies rather than defaulting to a static, all‑resources‑unavailable maximum‑withdrawal assumption that obscures the value of on‑site batteries

Systematize and automate flexible interconnections by requiring publication of hosting‑capacity‑style data for load (hourly and seasonal headroom, constraints, expected curtailment windows) and by offering standardized flexible options (limited‑load profiles, non‑firm service, and joint‑study paths for hybrid or adjacent resources)

A 60‑day requirement for all large‑load requests should provide a binding initial determination that includes a limited‑load capacity profile, identified constraints and telemetry, and a provisional queue position so developers can plan and finance while full engineering studies continue

When developers must anchor a queue position in transparent hosting‑capacity data, tariff‑backed LLFC commitments, and enforceable telemetry and non‑performance provisions, it becomes far less attractive to hold multiple oversized, purely optional positions that inflate apparent load growth
base upgrade requirements should not be set by those sensitivities when enforceable LLFC controls materially bound risk

letters.desc: Entergy opposes both a standard load interconnection queue and a combined generator-load queue, arguing a combined queue would worsen existing generator queue delays and disrupt ongoing reforms. It also opposes mandatory nationwide pro forma study procedures.
quotes: the Commission should not adopt the requests of some Commenters asking the Commission to adopt standardized rules across the country and to require that such rules be included in pro forma procedures that would be filed with the Commission
the Commission should consider establishing a backstop role, so that if load interconnection procedures are stalled for an unreasonable period of time, a large load has clear procedural recourse
A backstop rule would also enable transmission providers to exercise necessary flexibility and judgment in formulating the studies and procedures that are best suited to their systems.
the Commission should not establish a standard queue for load interconnections
a combined queue likely would lead to delays in processing interconnection requests even beyond those that would arise from a standardized load interconnection queue

Studying only a hypothetical "net" injection or withdrawal, without considering the system effects of the hybrid load demanding up to its full gross level of demand (when, for example, its co-located generating facility is unavailable), would create unreasonable reliability risks.
it is premature to assume that the breadth of hybrid options proposed by various commenters should all be entitled to expedited interconnection study or that expedited study is feasible

letters.desc: Eversource opposes mandatory inclusion of loads in the Order No. 2023 cluster study process, arguing its strict and lengthy timelines are infeasible for time-pressured large loads. Inclusion should be optional, and the Commission could consider not including loads at all.
quotes: to the extent any final rule arising out of this proceeding contemplates including qualifying loads in the Order No. 2023-mandated cluster study process, such inclusion should be optional.
the strict and often lengthy study timelines for generator interconnection may not be practically feasible with the tight timelines for the interconnection of large loads
the Commission should consider not including loads in that process at all due to the time pressures described above.

letters.desc: FuelCell Energy opposes studying hybrid facilities based only on net injections and withdrawals. The filing argues that studies must reflect the full operational scope of both generation and load components to enable accurate transmission system impact assessment and prevent future inefficiencies.
quotes: FuelCell Energy generally supports the principles set forth in the Proposed ANOPR, but urges the Commission to consider the unique circumstances presented by hybrid facilities consisting of generation resources co-located with, and intended to support, large loads

Adopting a separate interconnection standard for hybrid facilities that reflects each facility's actual operational characteristics and impact on the transmission grid, instead of applying the thresholds established for generation or load facilities
Developing a framework that ensures that interconnection studies fully reflect each hybrid facility's operational scope as opposed to a facility's net injections or withdrawals

a separate standard is necessary for hybrid facilities that combine significant generation and load components. This distinction is critical because the generation component of a hybrid facility may exceed 20 MW and serve an associated load of comparable or greater magnitude, while the net output of the facility could appear to fall below 20 MW

A facility with a net 10 MW output could, in practice, consist of a 700 MW generator paired with a 690 MW load. Such cases demonstrate the need for a distinct process that enables Transmission Owners and Transmission Providers to properly assess the full system impacts of hybrid facilities
studies of hybrid facilities reflect their full operational scope, rather than only their net injections or withdrawals
the Commission should ensure that the Transmission Owner or Transmission Provider study and account for the full amount of load and MWs of generation that make up a hybrid facility
if the Commission decides to allow hybrid facilities to be studied at the net amount, it should give this as an option rather than a mandatory requirement

letters.desc: The filer opposes proposals to use regional ELCC values from resource adequacy markets as interconnection offset credit for VPPs. He argues the two frameworks are analytically incompatible: resource adequacy is a regional statistical mechanism while interconnection requires worst-case physical analysis at specific nodes. His Monte Carlo model shows a 15:1 median overestimation when regional ELCC is applied to local interconnection.
quotes: This comment demonstrates that such proposals fundamentally conflate two distinct grid reliability mechanisms that operate under entirely different engineering and regulatory frameworks: Resource Adequacy and Nodal Interconnection.

The application of Resource Adequacy metrics to interconnection engineering creates what I term a "Regulatory Hallucination"—a policy framework that appears mathematically valid on paper but lacks physical correspondence to actual grid conditions at the point of interconnection.

Interconnection studies serve an entirely different function: determining whether specific transmission and distribution equipment can safely accommodate a new point-to-point power flow without exceeding thermal, voltage, or stability limits under worst-case conditions.
The consequences of interconnection study failure are not financial—they are physical equipment damage, cascading outages, and potential loss of load.

Residential VPP resources are necessarily dispersed across residential neighborhoods throughout a utility service territory or RTO region. In PJM, a Demand Response aggregator might enroll 50,000 smart thermostats distributed across Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Maryland, and Delaware. These devices provide regional load reduction, but they are not concentrated at the specific transmission node serving the data center.

Interconnection studies must model the worst-case hour for the specific local transmission node, which may not coincide with the regional system peak or the hours when VPP resources achieve maximum performance.

The median Attribution Gap of 4.72% indicates that a VPP receiving 69% ELCC credit in regional Resource Adequacy markets provides approximately 4.7% of that credit value for local interconnection purposes—a factor of 15:1 overestimation if regional ELCC is applied directly.

granting interconnection credit based on regional ELCC would result in overestimation by a factor of 7:1 or greater in 93% of cases, and overestimation by a factor of 3.5:1 or greater in virtually 100% of cases.

Attribution Gap is structural, not transient: The distribution parameters used in this analysis reflect mature VPP programs operating under best practices. The 4-6% median attribution is not a temporary limitation that will disappear with program refinement—it is an inherent consequence of applying regional statistical resources to local deterministic requirements.
The Commission should reject proposals to grant automatic interconnection offset credit based on Resource Adequacy ELCC values.

such contributions must be demonstrated through the same rigorous interconnection study methodology applied to all other resources: Locational specificity... Temporal certainty... Operational firmness... Verification and measurement

letters.desc: FERC should not assert jurisdiction over large load interconnection that would displace state and local regulatory authority. Federal standards should support rather than replace existing state forecasting and planning processes. Process improvements in timeliness, accuracy, and predictability can be achieved through coordinated best practices without federal jurisdiction.
quotes: FERC should be careful not to usurp traditional roles in this proceeding.
forecasting occurs at the state and local levels, so federal standards, if any are established, need to consider how to best and most accurately inform state/local forecasting processes.

significant benefits from FERC's intervention here—such as improving the timeliness and accuracy of load forecasting and predictable interconnection processes—can be accomplished without the Commission asserting jurisdiction over load interconnection.

letters.org: Louisiana Public Service CommissionMississippi Public Service Commission
letters.desc: The commissions argue that load interconnection cannot be treated as a standalone issue separate from generation, distribution, and transmission planning. A FERC-only interconnection study process disrupts the bottom-up integrated planning that incumbent utilities and states currently perform together.
quotes: the proposed implementation of that goal raises jurisdictional, reliability, resource adequacy, transparency, planning, and cost allocation concerns

the interconnection process accomplishes little without actions to evaluate and approve any generation, distribution and intrastate transmission facilities needed to maintain reliability and resource adequacy – all matters that are within the exclusive jurisdiction of retail regulators
Giving FERC jurisdiction over the load interconnection as if it were a standalone issue would hamper the efficient planning and development of these projects.

letters.desc: Maven finds Constellation's reliability analysis fatally incomplete: it omits the scenario where load drops while generation stays online, producing an 800 MW export excursion above studied conditions. NERC's 2026 Level 3 Alert and Gap Assessment require computational-load dynamic modeling, yet Constellation's Attachment A offers only a static megawatt netting table. Maven argues a protection promise in a footnote cannot substitute for a full dynamic contingency study with validated models.
quotes: Constellation's Attachment A presents four scenarios showing that LCEP's net power flows stay within studied conditions. It omits the decisive fifth scenario: the paired load drops while new generation remains online.

That footnote is doing the structural work of the entire reliability argument. It is not a protection design. It is not a clearing-time analysis. It is not a failure-mode study. It is a promise—and the Commission does not set just and reasonable rates on promises.

Constellation's filing states that 'a load outage is not typically planned for currently and therefore should not need to be a part of the LCEP process studies.' That sentence was written one month after NERC issued a Level 3 Essential Action Alert—its highest-urgency notification—requiring registered entities to address computational load modeling, studies, instrumentation, commissioning, operations, protection, and control.

A megawatt netting table cannot substitute for validated dynamic models of computational loads with UPS systems, backup generation, power electronics, vendor-specific control logic, and autonomous protective behavior.

letters.desc: MISO argues that standardized study procedures modeled on the generator interconnection queue would introduce the same delays that plagued Order No. 2003 and subsequent reforms. MISO's existing processes already approved about 17 GW of large loads since 2022 and allow requests to be studied as they arrive rather than queued in cycles.
quotes: the Commission should be mindful of regional differences that might limit the success of a "one size fits all" mandate.  Shifting to standardized large load interconnection procedures could nullify currently effective processes and/or delay significant work that has been undertaken and currently ongoing.
shifting to a one-size-fits all approach could introduce delays to interconnecting large loads, which would be contrary to the very progress desired by the DOE and the Commission.

Fundamentally, MISO questions whether standardized large load interconnection procedures will result in the "speed to power" that is necessary to allow the United States to effectively compete in the global competition for economic development, such as in artificial intelligence and creating manufacturing and industrial jobs.
under MISO's existing processes, since the 2022 MTEP cycle, MISO has approved approximately 17 GW of large load additions.
utilizing a generator interconnection process as a template that historically has experienced delays and is unlikely to provide the speed to power needed by large load customers

only about 13% of the total capacity entering interconnection queues nationwide ultimately achieves commercial operation.  Withdrawals of speculative interconnection requests frequently require restudies, particularly for later-stage withdrawals, which in turn could delay completion of studies and ultimately delay bringing viable generation proposals online.

letters.desc: The filer argues that the diversity of regional situations makes a single federal study or rule framework inappropriate at this time, and supports FERC issuing a policy statement rather than a binding rule.
quotes: the breadth and diversity of comments filed in response to the ANOPR show that rapid interconnection of large loads is a novel and challenging issue that may not be best suited for generic action at this juncture

letters.org: New England States Committee on Electricity
letters.desc: Uniform national interconnection rules risk pushing already constrained regions past their reliability limits. NESCOE notes that data center load growth varies widely by region, and New England has relatively low penetration compared to other areas, making a one-size-fits-all rule particularly ill-suited.
quotes: Standards and processes that some regions can make work might drive already over-subscribed regions past the breaking point and cause significant harm to reliability.

letters.org: North Carolina Utilities Commission Public Staff
letters.desc: Studying large loads jointly with generation would add a layer that causes restudies, delays, and inaccurate studies as projects drop out or change profiles. The filing warns this could reverse progress on generation interconnection, which is the system's driving need.
quotes: Because federal jurisdiction does not extend to facilities used for the generation of electric energy, the rules envisioned by the ANOPR cannot reach the heart of the problem they wish to address. A transmission study of a load that cannot be served is of no value.

adding a new layer to the study process will inevitably cause restudies, delays, and inaccurate studies when projects inevitably either drop out of the queue or seek material changes to their load profiles.

letters.desc: NDPSC opposes FERC rulemaking without documented evidence of discriminatory or inadequate state interconnection processes. New rules should address proven systemic problems and should build on existing RTO-developed solutions rather than impose new federal frameworks.
quotes: While NDPSC supports the general objectives outlined in the ANOPR, we want to emphasize the importance of ensuring that any new processes that may result from this proceeding do not inadvertently disturb the current balance between federal policy and state oversight.

The NDPSC asks the Commission to fully consider the potential impacts to state jurisdiction, incumbent utilities, and, most importantly, all customers when determining whether the commission should expand its jurisdiction by redefining what has historically been state jurisdiction. Finally, NDPSC impresses upon the Commission that any policies resulting from this proceeding be specifically and narrowly tailored to solve a widespread systemic issue

The ANOPR outlines the need to provide open and non-discriminatory access to the transmission system for interconnection of large loads as the principal need for reform. The NDPSC shares the goal of ensuring non-discriminatory access to the transmission system. However, this purpose, which also serves as a justification for the expansion of the Commission's current jurisdiction, is listed without supporting facts. The ANOPR provides no evidence or examples demonstrating that current state or utility interconnection processes are discriminatory or inadequate.
any proposed rule must be necessary to address a concrete, systemic, and nationwide problem.

SPP has worked to expedite the interconnection of large loads such as with their High Impact Large Load (HILL) proposal, recently filed with FERC. The HILL process provides an excellent framework for an interconnection process that meets the rapidly increasing demand for electricity while leaving state jurisdiction intact, protecting legacy customers, and promoting regulatory certainly.

MISO established a mechanism, known as the Expedited Project Review process, to quickly study and approve transmission projects that are necessary to meet urgent reliability requirements, many of which are associated with large load additions.

The SPP and MISO approaches to large load interconnection represent well-vetted processes which resulted from significant stakeholder input and buy-in. Both approaches help to address the challenges associated with large load customers while respecting and maintaining state and federal jurisdiction. The NDPSC supports the work the RTOs are doing and would advocate for a similar large load interconnection process, one that is limited in scope and based on demonstrated methodology already in place within RTO's, to be adopted should FERC move forward with a rule making.

letters.desc: OPSI finds no evidence that current state and utility interconnection study processes are discriminatory, undercutting the rationale for imposing a federal interconnection study regime on load.
quotes: The ANOPR provides no evidence that current state- or utility-administered interconnection processes are discriminatory.

If large load additions come with its own generation and FERC promotes the more efficient study of generation and load together, this could be an incentive for these loads to bring their own generation.

letters.desc: The PA PUC is concerned that mandated interconnection studies and resulting connections without adequate generation could undermine grid reliability. It leaves open limited acceptance of paired study guidance for hybrids if that guidance reduces transmission buildout and study timelines.
quotes: FERC-mandated large load interconnections without sufficient available generation capacity could threaten reliable power service to existing retail customers, as grid operators may lack the resources needed to maintain system stability during peak demand or extreme weather events.

The recommendations that (1) load and hybrid facilities be studied together with generating facilities for efficient siting and be subject to standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties; (2) hybrid facilities be studied based on the amount of injection and/or withdrawal rights requested to provide incentives for co-location with new generation facilities; (3) any hybrid interconnection install the system protection facilities necessary to prevent unauthorized injections or withdrawals that exceed the respective rights; (4) financial penalties for load facilities and hybrid facilities; (5) expedited consideration of interconnection studies of large loads and hybrid facilities that agree to be curtailable and dispatchable; and (6) that load and hybrid facilities should be responsible for 100% of the network upgrades that are assigned through the interconnection studies all have widespread economic and political ramifications.

Further guidance on paired interconnection studies could be welcome, subject to a more detailed proposed rule and opportunity for comment, if that guidance minimized the need for transmission buildout and interconnection study timelines due to the nature of that paired interconnection.

letters.desc: Existing FERC standards are inadequate to address data center reliability risks as evidenced by NERC's Level 3 Alert. Federal reliability standards and NERC authority must be clarified and strengthened before allowing further data center interconnections.
quotes: NERC announced it would issue a Level 3 Alert in May because of significant reliability concerns stemming from the rapid growth of data centers that are straining FERC-jurisdictional power grids.

The Commission's March 23 order dismissing the IMM's request for a temporary moratorium on new data center interconnections is directly at odds with NERC's Level 3 Alert. NERC's warning makes clear that existing FERC standards and orders are inadequate to address the significant reliability issues posed by large loads.

NERC has clearly established that AI data centers are having profound, negative impacts on grid reliability that require Commission confirmation that such facilities must be subject to federal electric reliability standards, including the authority for RTOs to impose forced curtailment of data center loads.

letters.org: Wisconsin Electric Power CompanyWisconsin Public Service Corporation
letters.desc: WEC argues Wisconsin and MISO already have functioning interconnection study processes, including MISO's Expedited Project Review and ERAS processes. They contend a new federal process modeled on the generator interconnection queue would slow rather than speed data center deployments in their region.
quotes: the WEC Companies believe that a federally mandated load interconnection process is not necessary to bring data centers online in a timely manner and could, in fact, introduce significant delay and impede the efforts of the WEC Companies and the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin ("PSCW") to interconnect hyperscale data centers while protecting the WEC Companies' existing retail customers.

a "one size fits all" federalized large load interconnection process could supersede the progress that has been made in Wisconsin and elsewhere and unintentionally delay the otherwise timely and efficient interconnection of data center loads in Wisconsin.
any rulemaking pursuant to the ANOPR should be limited and apply only to regions that do not have similarly strong processes in place.

the Commission should make the "gross" amount of load the default approach for studying large load interconnections consistent with existing Commission precedent.  This will ensure that co-located arrangements are appropriately studied based on their actual use of the transmission system, even if the load or generation has its withdrawal or injection rights based on the net capacity behind the meter.

the Commission should honor established processes that are working well and should not apply federal rules to regions where there are existing or proposed processes or tariffs, such as in Wisconsin.  At a minimum, the Commission should apply the "independent entity variation" standard to load interconnection rules, as it does the generator interconnection rules.

letters.desc: ACP acknowledges the need for record development on jurisdictional and other issues but emphasizes that federal study and action should be measured and respect cooperative federalism principles.
quotes: Load interconnection has historically been a state-jurisdictional issue, and any Federal action should be measured and carefully considered.
A state-driven approach, which would seek to minimize disruption of the multiple large load projects under development and seeking to interconnect today.

several regions are already moving forward with their own, stakeholder-led approaches to large load interconnection, including pairing load and generation. The Commission should ensure that any action in this proceeding supports regional flexibility, and does not deter or supplant proactive regional efforts

letters.desc: Data centers account for about 55 percent of utility demand growth over the next five years, with unprecedented scale (16 GW-scale facilities) coming online in 2026-2027. FERC should balance infrastructure solutions with demand-mitigation strategies including improved forecasting.
quotes: the new large loads present important economic and technological opportunities for our nation; however, due to their unprecedented size, these loads are having, and will continue to have, a direct impact on resource and infrastructure adequacy across the nation which have corresponding impacts on wholesale rates

DGA encourages FERC to consider a broad range of options that are aimed at both: (1) adding needed infrastructure to the grid—including by facilitating cost-effective transmission development to interconnect additional generation capacity in a timely manner, and (2) mitigating the total load requirements to temper additional infrastructure needs—including by improving the accuracy of load forecasting and by reducing overall demand of individual facilities
data centers are the largest driver of demand and energy growth, accounting for about 55% of demand growth in utility load forecasts over the next five years
sixteen GW-scale data centers with an aggregate demand of nearly 30 GW are scheduled to come online in 2026 and 2027

letters.desc: The GPSC is conducting an all-source capacity certification proceeding to evaluate generation needs driven by large load growth, analyzing load forecasting from its 2025 IRP as part of that process.
quotes: The GPSC is also currently conducting an all-source capacity certification proceeding to consider meeting the future needs of Georgia Power customers through cost-effective thermal, renewable, and battery storage technologies.

letters.desc: The filer identifies a coordination failure: data centers deploy in 18 to 24 months while grid infrastructure takes 7 to 10 years. This structural lag is the foundation for recommending a federal framework rather than leaving the problem to case-by-case interconnection.
quotes: The rapid growth of AI data center load presents a critical coordination challenge due to the temporal mismatch between rapid data center deployment (18–24 months) and slow grid infrastructure expansion (7–10 years).

letters.desc: PJM reports progress across its interconnection reform initiatives: 140 GW of requests processed during the 18-month transition, 51 RRI projects totaling 11.8 GW selected, Transition Cycle 1 closing with 135 service agreements (14.77 GW) and Transition Cycle 2 at Phase II representing 30.5 GW (expected complete February 2027), 42.5 GW of projects with signed agreements cleared, and capacity additions in the 2026/2027 auction rising to 2,669 MW UCAP, reversing three prior auction declines.
quotes: From July 2023 through December 2024, during the first 18 months of the transition period, PJM processed approximately 140 gigawatts ("GW") of generator interconnection requests.

and on May 2, 2025, PJM communicated the results of the RRI process to Members: PJM selected 51 projects, including both uprates of existing facilities and new projects, and representing approximately 11.8 GW of energy and 9.3 GW of unforced Capacity ("UCAP").

Transition Cycle No. 1, which is in its Final Agreement Negotiation Phase, will be completed and generators in that Cycle will have signed service agreements to connect to the grid in January or February 2026, as PJM issued 135 Transition Cycle No. 1 service agreements for execution on December 10, 2025.
At present, Transition Cycle No. 1 represents approximately 14.77 GW.

In addition to the projects currently under study or in service agreement negotiations, there are approximately 42.5 GW (installed capacity) of generation projects that have signed service agreements to connect to the grid. These projects have cleared PJM's interconnection process and have no PJM-associated impediment to construction.

Further, PJM notes that the total amount of new generation and generation uprates has increased to 2,669 MW of UCAP for the 2026/2027 Base Residual Auction ("BRA"), which reverses the downward trend in the amount of new generation and generation uprates of the three prior BRAs.

The RRI projects were added to Transition Cycle No. 2, which reached Phase II of the process on December 3, 2025, and is expected to be complete by February 2027.  At present, Transition Cycle No. 2 represents approximately 30.5 GW.

letters.desc: The Senator asks what FERC is doing to improve load forecasting and what contingency strategies FERC would deploy if actual load growth exceeds modeled growth. The questions are informational; no specific reform is endorsed.
quotes: What steps is FERC taking to improve its load forecasting process?
What strategies is FERC prepared to deploy should load growth exceed modeled or predicted growth?

letters.desc: WIRES notes that network upgrade costs identified through the interconnection study process represent investments that benefit the entire transmission system, and that paying only those study-identified costs does not cover ongoing system reliability obligations.
quotes: it shows that when large loads pay only for their required network upgrades and do not contribute to the embedded system costs or the future costs required to maintain system reliability for all customers, including themselves, those costs are shifted onto other customers.
